
The root, AU and schema entrypoints are intended to remain browser-safe. Effect
entrypoints expose Effect-native types for consumers that want service/layer
composition. The publish manifest is dist-only and does not expose `source`
conditions; `bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact` validates
that every public export resolves to packed files. The focused checker is an
Effect-native Bun runtime with typed command and validation failures and a
scope-managed temporary import workspace.

`@taxkit/sdk/schemas` re-exports calculator-owned run contracts for consumer
convenience:

- `CalculatorRunFacts`
- `CalculatorRunRequest`
- `CalculatorRunServiceRequest`
- `CalculatorRunReport`
- `CalculatorRunResponse`
- `CalculatorRunResponseData`
- `CalculatorServiceError`

It also exports SDK-owned safe-result and error schemas such as
`TaxKitCalculationError`, `TaxKitCalculationErrorDetail`,
`TaxKitSchemaDecodeError`, `TaxKitUnexpectedError`,
`TaxKitClientDisposedError` and `TaxKitClientDisposeError`.

## Publication Readiness

The package remains `private: true` until an explicit release approval removes
that flag. Package-name availability is time-sensitive; recheck it live during
a future release-prep slice instead of treating earlier registry results as
current truth.

Packed artifacts should include only `dist`, `README.md` and package metadata.
Do not run `bun run version-repo`, remove `private: true` or publish from this
package without an explicit release-prep approval.

### Downstream validation

The SDK owns the first downstream consumer validation gate:

```sh
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
```

The command builds and Bun-packs the ten-package release closure, including the
compiled public-content contracts now required by the HTTP package. It materializes
each package's dist-only `publishConfig.exports` in a staged tarball and
rejects source files, missing export targets or unresolved `workspace:*` and
`catalog:` ranges. It installs all unpublished tarballs into a temporary
consumer outside the repo, typechecks and runs SDK examples, imports every
JavaScript public entrypoint and bundles the browser-safe SDK surface.

All three SDK checking scripts use Effect FileSystem and scoped child
processes. Manifests are decoded once with the shared script Schemas; staged
publication manifests keep unrelated package metadata and missing dependency
keys. JSON field order may change when the staged manifest is encoded, but
package fields and declared publication targets are preserved. Each command
closes its process before continuing. Collected stdout is limited to 1 MiB;
stderr is drained without retaining or printing its contents. Failure reports
name the step and retain an available exit code, without copying native errors
or captured command output. A cleanup failure fails the check; if work has
already failed, both failures remain available.

`check-boundaries` checks package dependency direction and direct source
references. Only ripgrep exit 1 means no match; a failed search fails the check.
It does not prove the full browser dependency graph. Packed installation,
browser bundling and the Chromium suite provide their own separate evidence.
`check-types` checks both SDK source and the scripts' TypeScript project. The
native `test` suite includes controlled script failures; `test:browser` keeps
these Bun-only command fixtures out of the browser suite.

The command is always strict. Consumer-only file overrides connect unpublished
internal tarballs without changing their concrete registry-ready dependency
ranges. Any manifest or consumer regression prints evidence and exits nonzero;
there is no audit-only success mode.

Use this SDK release-gate order before any future publication work:

```sh
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-boundaries
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk test-types
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk test
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk test:browser
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk build
```

`validate:downstream` is the strict final package-installation gate. Supporting
workspace tests and the focused SDK tarball check do not replace it.

## Guardrails

- Keep this package independent from `@taxkit/api-http`.
- Do not import AU rule packages from the root entrypoint.
- Reuse canonical schemas, branded ids, service contracts, tagged errors and
  constructors from owning packages when implementation starts.
- Use `@taxkit/calculators` as the calculator execution boundary instead of
  duplicating catalog lookup or calculation dispatch.
- Keep transport-owned HTTP clients and OpenAPI helpers in
  `@taxkit/api-http`.

## Commands

```sh
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk test
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk test:browser
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-types
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk build
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk test-types
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-boundaries
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact
bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
```

## Related Docs

- `docs/product-specs/typescript-sdk-and-publishing.md`
- `docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`
- `docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`
- `docs/architecture/package-boundaries.md`
- `docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md`

`@taxkit/sdk/schemas` also re-exports the canonical `CalculatorCapacityExceeded`
and `CalculatorOperationTimedOut` errors. They belong to the widened checked
service union and expose fixed manual-retry guidance for server consumers.
Local SDK calculation does not acquire the API server's pool or time budget.
The actual packed and downstream fixtures check these named exports and types.


SDK Schemas also re-export the canonical `CalculatorMetadataError` union. Server
hosts may apply the calculator-owned five-second policy to all nine methods;
local SDK execution retains its caller-owned lifetime and calculation results.

The downstream consumer also checks core's fallible money/date constructors,
their public error types, safe overflow failures and historical date bytes/key
presence. `aud` requires already checked `Cents`; `audFromCents` returns an
Effect. Public examples use the same owning primitive contracts.

The genuine packed consumer also imports the three public rule-parameter
entrypoints. It rejects incomplete tables at construction and typed/saved
representation decoding, and compares all five retained table, effective-period
and source-artifact encodings against 13 preserved historical SHA-256 values
and two approved 2025–26 Medicare table/source fingerprints. The original
fingerprints remain in the earlier source history; the correction receipt
records their exact legal-data delta. These are
local packed-package checks, not publication or provider proof.


Core trace formula/rounding and question help fields now expose nested Options;
descriptor question/artifact/permission fields expose Options and rule parameter
collections are total arrays. Their encoded forms remain unchanged. SDK
`decodeOutput` checks a report returned by the calculator service against the
selected Schema's Type; it does not decode transport JSON again. Transport
consumers use the owning report codec at their representation boundary.
The genuine packed consumer rejects incorrect trace constructor fields and
child records, preserves service tuple types, compares all 22 saved metadata
response hashes. Only complete Medicare-owned source/table/artifact fragments
and the named annual report edition and $90k Medicare trace are inverted for
that historical comparison. A neighbouring mismatch proves unrelated changed
dates, amounts and versions still fail. Direct corrected parameter fingerprints
and independent annual money tests qualify the real current values.


Calculator-owned context, help and filter fields use `Option<Option<A>>` in
checked TypeScript values: `None` means a missing key, `Some(None)` means a
present undefined key, and `Some(Some(value))` means a present value. Owning
constructors default omitted keys to `None`. JSON and HTTP query fields retain
their ordinary optional representation. Flatten the two absent forms only where
they mean the same thing; do not invent a jurisdiction or tax year.

SDK request aliases derive constructor input from the calculator field owners
and retain descriptor-specific facts. The SDK constructs context/help only; the
selected calculator owns fact decoding and safe error help. Output narrowing
checks the already decoded Schema Type.


The packed consumer also checks the Core diagnostic cause Option Type/default,
its four original encoded forms and removal of the unused catalogue `program`
field. Existing selected-report, input-help, trace/ledger, metadata and source
expectations remain fixed. Legacy diagnostic values are not safe telemetry.


The published schema facade also exposes canonical `CalculatorRateLimited` and
`CalculatorAdmissionUnavailable`. They belong to the expanded checked service
error union; rate guidance carries no connection key or provider cause.
Packed runtime and TypeScript consumers check these identities and reject
private cause/key properties. Direct local SDK calculations do not acquire the
[native host rate policy](../../calculators/README.md#native-calculation-rate-admission),
and their retained reports and caller-owned lifetime remain unchanged.

     9	export const CalculatorConcurrencyLimit = 8;

    12	// The shared service budget covers completion and scoped cleanup. Every caller
    13	// suspends the service invocation so eager metadata construction is counted.
    14	const withinOperationBudget = Effect.fnUntraced(function* <A, E, R>(
    15	  operation: Effect.Effect<A, E, R>
    16	) {
    17	  const started = yield* Clock.monotonicTimeNanos;
    18	  const result = yield* operation.pipe(
    19	    Effect.scoped,
    20	    Effect.timeoutOrElse({
    21	      duration: CalculatorOperationBudget,
    22	      orElse: () => Effect.fail(new CalculatorOperationTimedOut()),
    23	    })
    24	  );

    26	  // Timers cannot pre-empt synchronous JavaScript. Reject a late result
    27	  // once control returns, without claiming that CPU work was stopped.
    28	  return yield* Duration.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(
    29	    Duration.nanos(finished - started),

    10	# HTTP API
    11	
    12	Effect HTTP API package for the current TaxKit health endpoint, public
    13	calculation endpoints, generated docs and API server route wiring.
    14	
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	`@taxkit/api-http` owns the current HTTP API contract, generated OpenAPI
    18	metadata, health and public calculation routes, HTTP status envelopes, thin
    19	handler adapters and typed client helpers used by TaxKit apps. Reusable
    20	calculator schemas, catalog entries, metadata projections, graph construction,
    21	calculation dispatch and schema-guided expected error shaping live in
    22	`@taxkit/calculators`.
    23	
    24	The root export includes `HealthResponse`, the same Schema used by the health
    25	endpoint. The API app's smoke check uses this owner to validate the real health
    26	response without copying its shape. This addition preserves the health wire
    27	format and all existing routes.
    28	
    29	The implemented API surface is:
    30	
    31	- `GET /api/health`
    32	- `GET /api/docs`
    33	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
    34	- `GET /api/v1/jurisdictions`
    35	- `GET /api/v1/tax-years`
    36	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
    37	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId`
    38	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`
    39	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
    40	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
    41	- `GET /api/v1/facts`
    42	- `GET /api/v1/rules`
    43	- `GET /api/v1/docs/navigation`
    44	- `GET /api/v1/docs/page?path=/start/quickstart`
    45	- `GET /api/v1/docs/search?term=Quickstart`
    46	- `GET /api/v1/docs/markdown?path=/start/quickstart`
    47	
    48	The public calculation API routes use the reusable calculator catalogue,
    49	fact and rule descriptors and graph diagnostics from `@taxkit/calculators`.
    50	Every handler, including Calculate, calls `PublicCalculatorService` directly.
    51	The HTTP Calculate route supplies its checked route ID, body and query to the
    52	same named `calculate` operation used by native RPC. Expected service failures
    53	keep the existing HTTP envelope. The status declarations below describe the
    54	additional request and operation protections.
    55	The SDK is a test-only comparison dependency, rather than a server dependency.
    56	
    57	`@taxkit/api-http/server` exports `TaxKitApiRoutesLayer` for application-owned
    58	service and CORS composition. It also retains `TaxKitServerLayer` with the
    59	existing calculator engine and CORS defaults for Bun and in-process consumers.
    60	Both server Layers require the caller's `ContentService`. API hosts supply the
    61	accepted build output; the HTTP package imports only the compiled content
    62	contracts. The native API host supplies its shared calculator service to HTTP
    63	and RPC.
    64	
    65	The `content` group delegates navigation, page lookup and search to that same
    66	content service. Markdown returns the owning processed page body as
    67	`text/markdown`. Page queries use checked, bounded public addresses; search
    68	terms have the owning 100-character limit. Missing pages return fixed typed
    69	JSON 404 guidance and a search-source failure returns fixed typed JSON 503
    70	guidance, without reflecting paths or source-error messages. Native invalid
    71	query responses are empty 400 replies. This surface returns accepted public
    72	documentation only, not personal calculation reports.
    73	
    74	`TaxKitApiInProcessClientLive` also requires supplied content. It now uses the
    75	native Effect HTTP client and router in the caller's Layer scope; each request
    76	closes its own scope. It creates no web-handler runner or Promise bridge.
    77	Its generated client checks the same response Schemas as remote consumers.
    78	
    79	```ts
    80	HTTP calculate
    81	
    82	API host
    83	  -> TaxKitApiRoutesLayer
    84	    -> CalculatorApiHandlerLive
    85	      -> PublicCalculatorService.calculate({ calculatorId, payload, ...query })
    86	        -> selected calculator input decode and CalculationEngine
    87	        -> CalculatorRunResponseData
    88	      -> existing CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope on expected failure
    89	```

    10	# HTTP API
    11	
    12	Effect HTTP API package for the current TaxKit health endpoint, public
    13	calculation endpoints, generated docs and API server route wiring.
    14	
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	`@taxkit/api-http` owns the current HTTP API contract, generated OpenAPI
    18	metadata, health and public calculation routes, HTTP status envelopes, thin
    19	handler adapters and typed client helpers used by TaxKit apps. Reusable
    20	calculator schemas, catalog entries, metadata projections, graph construction,
    21	calculation dispatch and schema-guided expected error shaping live in
    22	`@taxkit/calculators`.
    23	
    24	The root export includes `HealthResponse`, the same Schema used by the health
    25	endpoint. The API app's smoke check uses this owner to validate the real health
    26	response without copying its shape. This addition preserves the health wire
    27	format and all existing routes.
    28	
    29	The implemented API surface is:
    30	
    31	- `GET /api/health`
    32	- `GET /api/docs`
    33	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
    34	- `GET /api/v1/jurisdictions`
    35	- `GET /api/v1/tax-years`
    36	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
    37	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId`
    38	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`
    39	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
    40	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
    41	- `GET /api/v1/facts`
    42	- `GET /api/v1/rules`
    43	- `GET /api/v1/docs/navigation`
    44	- `GET /api/v1/docs/page?path=/start/quickstart`
    45	- `GET /api/v1/docs/search?term=Quickstart`
    46	- `GET /api/v1/docs/markdown?path=/start/quickstart`
    47	
    48	The public calculation API routes use the reusable calculator catalogue,
    49	fact and rule descriptors and graph diagnostics from `@taxkit/calculators`.
    50	Every handler, including Calculate, calls `PublicCalculatorService` directly.
    51	The HTTP Calculate route supplies its checked route ID, body and query to the
    52	same named `calculate` operation used by native RPC. Expected service failures
    53	keep the existing HTTP envelope. The status declarations below describe the
    54	additional request and operation protections.
    55	The SDK is a test-only comparison dependency, rather than a server dependency.
    56	
    57	`@taxkit/api-http/server` exports `TaxKitApiRoutesLayer` for application-owned
    58	service and CORS composition. It also retains `TaxKitServerLayer` with the
    59	existing calculator engine and CORS defaults for Bun and in-process consumers.
    60	Both server Layers require the caller's `ContentService`. API hosts supply the
    61	accepted build output; the HTTP package imports only the compiled content
    62	contracts. The native API host supplies its shared calculator service to HTTP
    63	and RPC.
    64	
    65	The `content` group delegates navigation, page lookup and search to that same
    66	content service. Markdown returns the owning processed page body as
    67	`text/markdown`. Page queries use checked, bounded public addresses; search
    68	terms have the owning 100-character limit. Missing pages return fixed typed
    69	JSON 404 guidance and a search-source failure returns fixed typed JSON 503
    70	guidance, without reflecting paths or source-error messages. Native invalid
    71	query responses are empty 400 replies. This surface returns accepted public
    72	documentation only, not personal calculation reports.
    73	
    74	`TaxKitApiInProcessClientLive` also requires supplied content. It now uses the
    75	native Effect HTTP client and router in the caller's Layer scope; each request
    76	closes its own scope. It creates no web-handler runner or Promise bridge.
    77	Its generated client checks the same response Schemas as remote consumers.
    78	
    79	```ts
    80	HTTP calculate
    81	
    82	API host
    83	  -> TaxKitApiRoutesLayer
    84	    -> CalculatorApiHandlerLive
    85	      -> PublicCalculatorService.calculate({ calculatorId, payload, ...query })
    86	        -> selected calculator input decode and CalculationEngine
    87	        -> CalculatorRunResponseData
    88	      -> existing CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope on expected failure
    89	```

*** Add File: /private/tmp/app-calls-review.md
+# Application call comparison — read-only evidence
+
+Examined TaxKit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442` on clean `codex/common-practice-foundation-review`, and Common Practice `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7` on clean `main`. No app, package or Common Practice files changed. Parent owns the frozen install and current local checks. Dependency-source observations made before that install saw TaxKit Alchemy beta.79; do not treat those as the final installed graph. Published scaffold 0.6.11 was checked by the parent against manifest and release after my public lookup failed.
+
+## Shape and recommended reuse order
+
+```text
+Website HTML / React forms      machine HTTP / RPC / MCP
+          |                               |
+          +---- checked transport --------+
+                           |
+                   native API Worker
+                           |
+                PublicCalculatorService
+                           |
+             catalogue -> Core engine -> AU rules
+                           |
+                checked report + diagnostics
+
+local TypeScript SDK --------> same calculator service
+```
+
+Reuse the Common Practice native Website/API connection and single server runner as the app base; reuse its named client operations and closed errors; retain TaxKit's calculator/core/rules/SDK owners; preserve wire routes and exports with compatibility adapters; then qualify any replacement of the private calculation connection before retiring its current code. HTTP versus RPC for the Website is a design decision after this comparison, not an already settled correction.
+
+## Concrete Website HTTP versus RPC comparison
+
+| Concern | Common Practice / scaffold | Current TaxKit | Recommendation and consequence |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Website server reads | Common Practice `ApiClientsLive` builds typed HTTP Content and Training clients over the native private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts:70-90`). Scaffold uses `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient` then named domain client Layer (`repo-structure/assets/repository/apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts.tmpl:29-51`). | `WebsiteServerLive` builds calculator and docs RPC clients over matching private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:33-208`). | HTTP can be the shared default base. Keeping RPC is also valid if the richer contracts and current proof justify it. Neither choice requires changing a tax rule. |
+| Browser calls | Common Practice's browser WebMCP calls typed HTTP Content/Training services through checked API settings (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts:88-124`). Normal page loading uses TanStack server functions (`apps/web/src/lib/seo/page.functions.ts:13-29`). | React Atom owns calculator RPC calls to public POST `/rpc` (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator.atoms.ts:37-89`). Root checks and seeds configuration (`apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:49-91`). Docs use server functions instead of an independent browser backend. | Prefer one closed Website client contract independent of transport; either private HTTP/public HTTP or private RPC/public RPC may implement it. Keep direct public API calculation and same page-owned command state. |
+| Private rate identity | Common Practice has content reads, no equivalent anonymous-tax calculation allowance in the inspected path. | TaxKit refuses forwarded Worker IP headers and sends the checked original connection identity through a private Worker method, separate from JSON (`packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:11-20`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). | Necessary preservation. Plain binding fetch must not replace this method until it has an equally trusted identity path. A new checked HTTP client alone does not solve this. |
+| Private cancellation | Native binding HTTP can carry an operation signal. Common Practice server entry forwards the request signal (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts:93-101`). | Calculator private `toRpcAsync` call explicitly cannot carry AbortSignal; local cancellation stops waiting, while server work remains bounded (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:60-73`). Docs byte-body binding fetch supplies a signal (`:174-180`). | HTTP has a simpler cancellable transport, but trusted identity and actual remote abort must both be proved. Keep the present limit stated until replacement proof exists. |
+| Client service | Common Practice HTTP and RPC Layers implement the same Content service; generated native client is private (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:25-64`; `packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:28-56`). | RPC has a checked named transport client (`packages/api/rpc/src/service.ts:22-54`). HTTP exposes the generated client and callback wrapper (`packages/api/http/src/client/index.ts:12-24`; `client/service.ts:5-17`). | Important correction: add named checked HTTP operations and keep old entrypoints as compatibility adapters. Do not simply widen the local SDK's error contract to transport errors. |
+| Errors | Common Practice maps unavailable/invalid replies to Content-owned errors, retaining semantic failures (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:15-60`). | RPC projects private request failures to `CalculatorRpcRejected`, retains canonical capacity/rate/time errors, and adds transport errors (`handlers.ts:15-65`; `errors.ts:16-100`). HTTP generated client exposes HTTP/Schema errors and HTTP envelopes. | A checked Website-facing service should share safe named failures regardless of transport, while HTTP status/error bytes and RPC revision 4 stay unchanged. |
+| Whole reply limits | Common Practice HTTP timeout wraps the complete native client operation (40 seconds due image rendering; `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:31-59`, `content/src/service.ts:15-16`). | RPC is ten seconds including reply decode and cleanup, 2 MiB body cap, no automatic retry (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-85`; `response-budget.boundary.ts:12-53`; `schemas.ts:60-61`). HTTP helper has no owning complete-read deadline or byte budget (`client/index.ts:12-16`). | Important correction: supply full-read deadline, byte cap, invalid-reply failure and earlier caller cancellation for the new HTTP client. Keep TaxKit's ten-second budget; Common Practice's 40-second image budget does not fit tax calculation. |
+| RPC receive loop lifetime | Common Practice RPC client is acquired once (`packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:27-31`); it is not the Website's chosen transport. | TaxKit creates/releases each native RPC client in the named operation; retaining an earlier Worker request's receive loop can stall later requests (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:87-107`). | Preserve TaxKit's scope while RPC remains. Copying Common Practice's once-acquired RPC client into this Website would undo a deliberate request-lifetime fix. |
+| Documentation reach | Common Practice HTTP Content has selected data/Markdown/SEO/image variants. | TaxKit RPC also has named discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown operations. Public HTTP currently has four content routes; discovery uses the private RPC operation (`packages/api/http/README.md:43-46`; `apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:145-150`). | HTTP-only Website needs a checked replacement for discovery too. Do not invent a second documentation renderer or source loader in Website. |
+| SDK | Common Practice packages are private source-only. | TaxKit SDK is in-process, not a network client (`packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:4-5`; `src/effect.ts:91-117`; `live.layer.ts:1-9`). | Keep SDK contract, caller-owned lifetime, engine calculation and dist-only exports regardless of Website transport. A Website change has no reason to turn this into a remote SDK. |
+
+Recommendation for the later transport round: use typed HTTP as the default app-base path once the named safe HTTP client and trusted private rate identity are qualified; retain public RPC for existing machine consumers. The alternative is to keep RPC for the Website, preserving its already explicit timeout/byte/cancellation/error policy, while still fixing the weaker HTTP client. This is optional simplification, not evidence that RPC calculations are wrong.
+
+## Representative traces with exact owners
+
+1. Browser calculation: page container wires one Atom command and interrupts it on unmount (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator-page.container.tsx:65-85`). Atom runtime acquires matching public RPC transport (`calculator.atoms.ts:47-89`). Editing interrupts pending work and keeps a stale report (`:98-148`, `:168-225`). RPC encodes `Calculate` revision 4 with native Schemas, scopes its receive loop, disables tracing, enforces ten-second completion and maps fixed failures (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-107`). API routes use the same `PublicCalculatorService` (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:87-117`; RPC handlers `packages/api/rpc/src/handlers.ts:46-65`). Calculator owner selects entry and maps input failures (`packages/calculators/src/live.layer.ts:34-66,83-94`). The entry decodes its actual facts once (`catalog.ts:110-121`) then supplies the scenario + AU rule Layer to Core (`:142-153` for take-home; `:207-217` for annual). Core provides that rule/scenario Layer and returns report + diagnostics (`packages/core/src/engine/live.layer.ts:11-21`). RPC encodes the checked response, Atom receives it, leaf renders readonly report.
+
+2. HTML form without JavaScript: Website admits and bounds form POST, checks form data, constructs the owning request and calls `WebsiteServerApplication.calculate` (`apps/web/src/server.ts:177-237`). Private adapter sends native `/rpc` Request plus original checked identity to API binding-only `calculatorRequest` (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-92`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). API buffers/bounds the JSON reply before the native method's event scope closes (`:241-275`). Website Schema-encodes success/failure into plain TanStack submission data (`server.ts:234-251`), root restores checked result, the page keeps no independent backend. Only plain report/form values enter request context. Changing this custom entry needs no-JavaScript, safe failure and response-consumption proof; it should not be removed just because Common Practice has no tax form.
+
+3. Remote HTTP calculation: native route group decodes URL/body/query with calculator-owned Schemas and preserves existing HTTP error/status envelopes (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:62-104`; handlers `:83-120`). The handler calls the same service; SDK is not in the server dependency path. Request body owner admits streamed 64 KiB within five seconds (`packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-83`). API composition shares the calculation service instance across HTTP and RPC. HTTP client generation uses the same API declarations, but its public helper currently leaves timeout and transport-failure ownership to each consumer.
+
+4. Local SDK: caller-selected descriptor supplies calculator identity and input/report types; canonical context/query constructors precede calculator service call and selected report validation (`packages/sdk/typescript/src/effect.ts:71-117`). Default Layer supplies the same calculator service + Core engine (`live.layer.ts:1-9`). Plain clients have independent lazily started ManagedRuntime, stop pending work when closed, await cleanup; one-shot helpers own temporary Scope (`client.runtime.ts:66-75,95-173,177-225`). Effect callers keep their own service provision and lifetime. This is justified machinery for a Promise SDK, not a duplicate server runner.
+
+5. Remote MCP: six app-owned toolkit definitions reuse canonical calculator/content inputs and replies (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:24-90`). `taxkit_calculate` calls the captured calculator service and projects failures to fixed tool guidance (`:92-148`). The tool has explicit request cancellation that removes its AbortSignal listener and waits for losing work cleanup (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts:6-39`). Native API instance composes modern `2026-07-28` once; registration removes first caller's request/key/signal from retained context (`worker.application.ts:121-157`). Legacy `2025-11-25` sessions have a stage-owned Durable Object, ten-minute Scope with 32 initialisations/32 concurrent requests, native alarm expiry (`mcp-session.layer.ts:51-147`; `mcp.schemas.ts:4-8`). Reply JSON/SSE is fully read under request Scope, 2 MiB/ten seconds, no subscriptions/resumption (`mcp-response.boundary.ts:11-49`). Current documented modern real-network pre-response cancellation relies on the five-second work budget; do not describe in-process early interruption as remote cleanup proof (`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md:720-727`).
+
+## Findings for root crosswalk (provisional IDs)
+
+- APP-001 — important — HTTP client is a raw generated client rather than named checked operations. Earliest owner `packages/api/http/src/client/*`, owner `taxkit-http-api-owner`. Consequence: HTTP consumers repeat deadline/error/credential/redirect/byte policy; the Website cannot simply substitute it for the checked RPC client. Correction: narrow named service backed by private native client; explicit typed origin, fixed failures, whole-read budget and capped reply. Keep existing client creation methods, callback helper and export paths as compatibility adapters until separately approved retirement. Tests: native HTTP good/declared error/malformed body/wrong selected reply/stalled headers then body/caller interruption/secret-negative error. Rollback: leave legacy client path and switch Website imports back; no tax/wire alteration.
+- APP-002 — optional simplification — Website private transport has two handwritten HttpClient adapters and binding-only calculatorRequest, and raw Request/Response materialisation (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-116,165-204`). Earliest owner Website private binding adapter; backend private method/rate owner. Consequence: extra request-body and cancellation code has to stay qualified on Alchemy updates. Correction: adopt the shared native bridge as far as actual host identity, byte-body and abort semantics allow; preserve trusted rate identity and test multiple sequential Worker requests after startup. Retirement conditional: existing docs byte-body custom adapter, custom private HttpClient construction, and private calculatorRequest buffer can only be retired after equivalent identity/cancellation/lifetime proof. HTTP versus RPC is a later choice.
+- APP-003 — preserve justified difference — RPC has separate safe client contract and request/procedure/response policy. Merging it directly into PublicCalculatorService would expose different failures or change SDK expectations. Keep transport projection and domain tax owner separate. A safe consumer-facing contract may be shared within existing calculator owner, but changing public error unions is a declared compatibility change, not a folder rename.
+- APP-004 — preserve necessary difference — TaxKit needs compiled dist-only packages/SDK rather than Common Practice source-only manifests. `packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:14-38` and packed/downstream scripts are the owners. Common Practice Content/HTTP/RPC/MCP `package.json` directly resolve `src`; those are useful private-app patterns but do not prove TaxKit tarball compatibility. Removing source/types/default/publish maps, changing package names or moving exports is breaking unless old names continue to resolve. Keep source condition for local internal packages and dist-only actual publish staging; retain packed installed consumer, declaration and browser bundle proof.
+- APP-005 — preserve necessary difference — tax request limits, anonymous rate identity, shared work pool and safe logging. `packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:9-56` gives each composed isolate eight places/five seconds. Timer cannot stop synchronous CPU; late result is rejected (`:25-33`). No global pool is claimed. Do not copy Common Practice wildcard browser CORS (`apps/api/src/http/handler.layer.ts:46-61`) to the tax API. TaxKit admits exact Website origin and disables native client tracing as containment (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:189-204`; RPC live `:68`, server `packages/api/rpc/src/server.ts:10-15`). Operational tracing requires reviewed safe fields, actual browser b3/traceparent preflight and errors, rather than changing CORS alone.
+- APP-006 — optional — move app-owned MCP tool contracts into a package only if there is a real second consumer. Common Practice's shared ContentToolHandlers works for remote MCP and browser tools (`packages/mcp/src/handlers.layer.ts:6-16`). TaxKit browser tools deliberately operate the page's existing form/answer state; a plain remote calculate handler is not the same interaction. Preserve UI command coordination. Legacy Durable Object session/expiry stays API-host owned regardless of contract location.
+- APP-007 — optional / retain until Q2 — two API execution hosts. Native API Worker has HTTP/RPC/MCP with rate policy; Bun host serves retained HTTP composition only (`apps/api/src/server.ts:1-28`, `src/index.ts:1-20`, `package.json` dev/start). Do not present Bun `dev` as native-pair proof. If Bun is no longer required, retire its launcher/config/smoke-only duplication after caller inventory and agreement. If it remains supported, document/prove its intentional behaviour separately; no need to copy native Cloudflare-only rate binding into an unrelated host.
+
+## Local validation limits
+
+I ran two checks before the parent's frozen install. `bun run --filter=@taxkit/api-rpc test` exited 1: four suites, zero tests; missing workspace exports (`@taxkit/content/live`, `/errors`) and undefined Schema union member. `bun run --filter=api test` exited 1: script could not find Vitest. These are unqualified stale installation/build observations, not proved source failures. Parent subsequently froze installed graph and owns builds/current validation. No further tests run here. Existing test sources are strong required checks but reading them is not executing them:
+
+- RPC `test/deadline.test.ts:34-76,77-109` checks stalled header/body whole deadline and earlier caller interruption.
+- Native Website pair `apps/web/test/native-pair.boundary.test.ts:179-229` checks actual built browser lacks engine/provider/server implementation markers, with positive API marker check.
+- Native browser cancellation `native-cancellation.boundary.test.ts:403-405` explicitly caps remote-operation claims.
+- API official MCP client `apps/api/test/mcp-client.boundary.test.ts:241-352` tests actual client cancellation and calculation-place release.
+- SDK lifetime `packages/sdk/typescript/src/client-lifetime.test.ts` covers separate clients, pending startup/work, close race and private defects; packed/downstream scripts own real package proof.
+
+No tax correctness, final current local test pass, hosted deployment, provider state or published package claim is made by this note.
+
+## Read-path inventory
+

# Application call comparison — read-only evidence

Examined TaxKit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442` on clean `codex/common-practice-foundation-review`, and Common Practice `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7` on clean `main`. No app, package or Common Practice files changed. Parent owns the frozen install and current local checks. Dependency-source observations made before that install saw TaxKit Alchemy beta.79; do not treat those as the final installed graph. Published scaffold 0.6.11 was checked by the parent against manifest and release after my public lookup failed.

## Shape and recommended reuse order

```text
Website HTML / React forms      machine HTTP / RPC / MCP
          |                               |
          +---- checked transport --------+
                           |
                   native API Worker
                           |
                PublicCalculatorService
                           |
             catalogue -> Core engine -> AU rules
                           |
                checked report + diagnostics

local TypeScript SDK --------> same calculator service
```

Reuse the Common Practice native Website/API connection and single server runner as the app base; reuse its named client operations and closed errors; retain TaxKit's calculator/core/rules/SDK owners; preserve wire routes and exports with compatibility adapters; then qualify any replacement of the private calculation connection before retiring its current code. HTTP versus RPC for the Website is a design decision after this comparison, not an already settled correction.

## Concrete Website HTTP versus RPC comparison

| Concern | Common Practice / scaffold | Current TaxKit | Recommendation and consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Website server reads | Common Practice `ApiClientsLive` builds typed HTTP Content and Training clients over the native private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts:70-90`). Scaffold uses `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient` then named domain client Layer (`repo-structure/assets/repository/apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts.tmpl:29-51`). | `WebsiteServerLive` builds calculator and docs RPC clients over matching private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:33-208`). | HTTP can be the shared default base. Keeping RPC is also valid if the richer contracts and current proof justify it. Neither choice requires changing a tax rule. |
| Browser calls | Common Practice's browser WebMCP calls typed HTTP Content/Training services through checked API settings (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts:88-124`). Normal page loading uses TanStack server functions (`apps/web/src/lib/seo/page.functions.ts:13-29`). | React Atom owns calculator RPC calls to public POST `/rpc` (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator.atoms.ts:37-89`). Root checks and seeds configuration (`apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:49-91`). Docs use server functions instead of an independent browser backend. | Prefer one closed Website client contract independent of transport; either private HTTP/public HTTP or private RPC/public RPC may implement it. Keep direct public API calculation and same page-owned command state. |
| Private rate identity | Common Practice has content reads, no equivalent anonymous-tax calculation allowance in the inspected path. | TaxKit refuses forwarded Worker IP headers and sends the checked original connection identity through a private Worker method, separate from JSON (`packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:11-20`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). | Necessary preservation. Plain binding fetch must not replace this method until it has an equally trusted identity path. A new checked HTTP client alone does not solve this. |
| Private cancellation | Native binding HTTP can carry an operation signal. Common Practice server entry forwards the request signal (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts:93-101`). | Calculator private `toRpcAsync` call explicitly cannot carry AbortSignal; local cancellation stops waiting, while server work remains bounded (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:60-73`). Docs byte-body binding fetch supplies a signal (`:174-180`). | HTTP has a simpler cancellable transport, but trusted identity and actual remote abort must both be proved. Keep the present limit stated until replacement proof exists. |
| Client service | Common Practice HTTP and RPC Layers implement the same Content service; generated native client is private (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:25-64`; `packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:28-56`). | RPC has a checked named transport client (`packages/api/rpc/src/service.ts:22-54`). HTTP exposes the generated client and callback wrapper (`packages/api/http/src/client/index.ts:12-24`; `client/service.ts:5-17`). | Important correction: add named checked HTTP operations and keep old entrypoints as compatibility adapters. Do not simply widen the local SDK's error contract to transport errors. |
| Errors | Common Practice maps unavailable/invalid replies to Content-owned errors, retaining semantic failures (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:15-60`). | RPC projects private request failures to `CalculatorRpcRejected`, retains canonical capacity/rate/time errors, and adds transport errors (`handlers.ts:15-65`; `errors.ts:16-100`). HTTP generated client exposes HTTP/Schema errors and HTTP envelopes. | A checked Website-facing service should share safe named failures regardless of transport, while HTTP status/error bytes and RPC revision 4 stay unchanged. |
| Whole reply limits | Common Practice HTTP timeout wraps the complete native client operation (40 seconds due image rendering; `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:31-59`, `content/src/service.ts:15-16`). | RPC is ten seconds including reply decode and cleanup, 2 MiB body cap, no automatic retry (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-85`; `response-budget.boundary.ts:12-53`; `schemas.ts:60-61`). HTTP helper has no owning complete-read deadline or byte budget (`client/index.ts:12-16`). | Important correction: supply full-read deadline, byte cap, invalid-reply failure and earlier caller cancellation for the new HTTP client. Keep TaxKit's ten-second budget; Common Practice's 40-second image budget does not fit tax calculation. |
| RPC receive loop lifetime | Common Practice RPC client is acquired once (`packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:27-31`); it is not the Website's chosen transport. | TaxKit creates/releases each native RPC client in the named operation; retaining an earlier Worker request's receive loop can stall later requests (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:87-107`). | Preserve TaxKit's scope while RPC remains. Copying Common Practice's once-acquired RPC client into this Website would undo a deliberate request-lifetime fix. |
| Documentation reach | Common Practice HTTP Content has selected data/Markdown/SEO/image variants. | TaxKit RPC also has named discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown operations. Public HTTP currently has four content routes; discovery uses the private RPC operation (`packages/api/http/README.md:43-46`; `apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:145-150`). | HTTP-only Website needs a checked replacement for discovery too. Do not invent a second documentation renderer or source loader in Website. |
| SDK | Common Practice packages are private source-only. | TaxKit SDK is in-process, not a network client (`packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:4-5`; `src/effect.ts:91-117`; `live.layer.ts:1-9`). | Keep SDK contract, caller-owned lifetime, engine calculation and dist-only exports regardless of Website transport. A Website change has no reason to turn this into a remote SDK. |

Recommendation for the later transport round: use typed HTTP as the default app-base path once the named safe HTTP client and trusted private rate identity are qualified; retain public RPC for existing machine consumers. The alternative is to keep RPC for the Website, preserving its already explicit timeout/byte/cancellation/error policy, while still fixing the weaker HTTP client. This is optional simplification, not evidence that RPC calculations are wrong.

## Representative traces with exact owners

1. Browser calculation: page container wires one Atom command and interrupts it on unmount (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator-page.container.tsx:65-85`). Atom runtime acquires matching public RPC transport (`calculator.atoms.ts:47-89`). Editing interrupts pending work and keeps a stale report (`:98-148`, `:168-225`). RPC encodes `Calculate` revision 4 with native Schemas, scopes its receive loop, disables tracing, enforces ten-second completion and maps fixed failures (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-107`). API routes use the same `PublicCalculatorService` (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:87-117`; RPC handlers `packages/api/rpc/src/handlers.ts:46-65`). Calculator owner selects entry and maps input failures (`packages/calculators/src/live.layer.ts:34-66,83-94`). The entry decodes its actual facts once (`catalog.ts:110-121`) then supplies the scenario + AU rule Layer to Core (`:142-153` for take-home; `:207-217` for annual). Core provides that rule/scenario Layer and returns report + diagnostics (`packages/core/src/engine/live.layer.ts:11-21`). RPC encodes the checked response, Atom receives it, leaf renders readonly report.

2. HTML form without JavaScript: Website admits and bounds form POST, checks form data, constructs the owning request and calls `WebsiteServerApplication.calculate` (`apps/web/src/server.ts:177-237`). Private adapter sends native `/rpc` Request plus original checked identity to API binding-only `calculatorRequest` (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-92`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). API buffers/bounds the JSON reply before the native method's event scope closes (`:241-275`). Website Schema-encodes success/failure into plain TanStack submission data (`server.ts:234-251`), root restores checked result, the page keeps no independent backend. Only plain report/form values enter request context. Changing this custom entry needs no-JavaScript, safe failure and response-consumption proof; it should not be removed just because Common Practice has no tax form.

3. Remote HTTP calculation: native route group decodes URL/body/query with calculator-owned Schemas and preserves existing HTTP error/status envelopes (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:62-104`; handlers `:83-120`). The handler calls the same service; SDK is not in the server dependency path. Request body owner admits streamed 64 KiB within five seconds (`packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-83`). API composition shares the calculation service instance across HTTP and RPC. HTTP client generation uses the same API declarations, but its public helper currently leaves timeout and transport-failure ownership to each consumer.

4. Local SDK: caller-selected descriptor supplies calculator identity and input/report types; canonical context/query constructors precede calculator service call and selected report validation (`packages/sdk/typescript/src/effect.ts:71-117`). Default Layer supplies the same calculator service + Core engine (`live.layer.ts:1-9`). Plain clients have independent lazily started ManagedRuntime, stop pending work when closed, await cleanup; one-shot helpers own temporary Scope (`client.runtime.ts:66-75,95-173,177-225`). Effect callers keep their own service provision and lifetime. This is justified machinery for a Promise SDK, not a duplicate server runner.

5. Remote MCP: six app-owned toolkit definitions reuse canonical calculator/content inputs and replies (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:24-90`). `taxkit_calculate` calls the captured calculator service and projects failures to fixed tool guidance (`:92-148`). The tool has explicit request cancellation that removes its AbortSignal listener and waits for losing work cleanup (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts:6-39`). Native API instance composes modern `2026-07-28` once; registration removes first caller's request/key/signal from retained context (`worker.application.ts:121-157`). Legacy `2025-11-25` sessions have a stage-owned Durable Object, ten-minute Scope with 32 initialisations/32 concurrent requests, native alarm expiry (`mcp-session.layer.ts:51-147`; `mcp.schemas.ts:4-8`). Reply JSON/SSE is fully read under request Scope, 2 MiB/ten seconds, no subscriptions/resumption (`mcp-response.boundary.ts:11-49`). Current documented modern real-network pre-response cancellation relies on the five-second work budget; do not describe in-process early interruption as remote cleanup proof (`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md:720-727`).

## Findings for root crosswalk (provisional IDs)

- APP-001 — important — HTTP client is a raw generated client rather than named checked operations. Earliest owner `packages/api/http/src/client/*`, owner `taxkit-http-api-owner`. Consequence: HTTP consumers repeat deadline/error/credential/redirect/byte policy; the Website cannot simply substitute it for the checked RPC client. Correction: narrow named service backed by private native client; explicit typed origin, fixed failures, whole-read budget and capped reply. Keep existing client creation methods, callback helper and export paths as compatibility adapters until separately approved retirement. Tests: native HTTP good/declared error/malformed body/wrong selected reply/stalled headers then body/caller interruption/secret-negative error. Rollback: leave legacy client path and switch Website imports back; no tax/wire alteration.
- APP-002 — optional simplification — Website private transport has two handwritten HttpClient adapters and binding-only calculatorRequest, and raw Request/Response materialisation (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-116,165-204`). Earliest owner Website private binding adapter; backend private method/rate owner. Consequence: extra request-body and cancellation code has to stay qualified on Alchemy updates. Correction: adopt the shared native bridge as far as actual host identity, byte-body and abort semantics allow; preserve trusted rate identity and test multiple sequential Worker requests after startup. Retirement conditional: existing docs byte-body custom adapter, custom private HttpClient construction, and private calculatorRequest buffer can only be retired after equivalent identity/cancellation/lifetime proof. HTTP versus RPC is a later choice.
- APP-003 — preserve justified difference — RPC has separate safe client contract and request/procedure/response policy. Merging it directly into PublicCalculatorService would expose different failures or change SDK expectations. Keep transport projection and domain tax owner separate. A safe consumer-facing contract may be shared within existing calculator owner, but changing public error unions is a declared compatibility change, not a folder rename.
- APP-004 — preserve necessary difference — TaxKit needs compiled dist-only packages/SDK rather than Common Practice source-only manifests. `packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:14-38` and packed/downstream scripts are the owners. Common Practice Content/HTTP/RPC/MCP `package.json` directly resolve `src`; those are useful private-app patterns but do not prove TaxKit tarball compatibility. Removing source/types/default/publish maps, changing package names or moving exports is breaking unless old names continue to resolve. Keep source condition for local internal packages and dist-only actual publish staging; retain packed installed consumer, declaration and browser bundle proof.
- APP-005 — preserve necessary difference — tax request limits, anonymous rate identity, shared work pool and safe logging. `packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:9-56` gives each composed isolate eight places/five seconds. Timer cannot stop synchronous CPU; late result is rejected (`:25-33`). No global pool is claimed. Do not copy Common Practice wildcard browser CORS (`apps/api/src/http/handler.layer.ts:46-61`) to the tax API. TaxKit admits exact Website origin and disables native client tracing as containment (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:189-204`; RPC live `:68`, server `packages/api/rpc/src/server.ts:10-15`). Operational tracing requires reviewed safe fields, actual browser b3/traceparent preflight and errors, rather than changing CORS alone.
- APP-006 — optional — move app-owned MCP tool contracts into a package only if there is a real second consumer. Common Practice's shared ContentToolHandlers works for remote MCP and browser tools (`packages/mcp/src/handlers.layer.ts:6-16`). TaxKit browser tools deliberately operate the page's existing form/answer state; a plain remote calculate handler is not the same interaction. Preserve UI command coordination. Legacy Durable Object session/expiry stays API-host owned regardless of contract location.
- APP-007 — optional / retain until Q2 — two API execution hosts. Native API Worker has HTTP/RPC/MCP with rate policy; Bun host serves retained HTTP composition only (`apps/api/src/server.ts:1-28`, `src/index.ts:1-20`, `package.json` dev/start). Do not present Bun `dev` as native-pair proof. If Bun is no longer required, retire its launcher/config/smoke-only duplication after caller inventory and agreement. If it remains supported, document/prove its intentional behaviour separately; no need to copy native Cloudflare-only rate binding into an unrelated host.

1	---
     2	name: effect-client-wrapper
     3	description: Design, implement, or review a typed Effect service around a third-party SDK, API client, callback library, or Promise-based provider. Use for provider adapters, service Layers, external-client configuration, request and response Schemas, typed provider errors, retries, and test Layers. Enforce named operations, branded identifiers, Schema-backed Config, immediate output decoding, flat Effects, and the explicit rejection of generic use callbacks, raw clients, primitive config, instanceof, and unchecked SDK outputs.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Effect Client Wrapper
     7	
     8	Create a semantic adapter owned by the application, not a generic Effect-shaped escape hatch around an SDK.
     9	
    10	## Establish the boundary
    11	
    12	1. Read applicable repository instructions, architecture docs, lint rules, installed Effect and SDK versions, and representative services and Layers.
    13	2. Identify the owner of every request, response, identifier, configuration value, error, retry policy, and runtime boundary.
    14	3. Research the cloned Effect v4 source, record its revision/version, then reconcile the chosen APIs with installed source/types. Use matching primary SDK source for its contract; DeepWiki through Executor MCP is secondary explanation for the upstream Effect/SDK repository.
    15	4. Prefer extending an existing semantic adapter over creating a parallel client abstraction.
    16	
    17	## Define the public service
    18	
    19	- Expose named domain/provider operations such as `getCustomer`, `sendMessage`, or `renderImage`.
    20	- Accept owning Schema-derived inputs and branded identifiers. Never substitute raw `id: string`.
    21	- Return only decoded application-owned or explicitly provider-owned Schema types.
    22	- Keep the raw SDK instance private to the live Layer or adapter module.
    23	- Provide a live Layer and a mock/test Layer at the same service contract.
    24	
    25	Do not expose a generic `use`, `run`, `withClient`, callback, unconstrained generic result, or raw-client accessor. Those APIs erase operation ownership, output provenance, retry policy, and testability.
    26	
    27	## Implement each operation linearly
    28	
    29	Use the locally installed Effect APIs. A named operation should read as one flat program:
    30	
    31	1. encode the checked request at its actual outbound contract, without re-decoding internal typed data;
    32	2. call exactly one SDK operation through `Effect.tryPromise`, callback adaptation, or the repository's boundary primitive;
    33	3. map rejection immediately into an owner-named typed Schema error with safe diagnostics;
    34	4. decode the unknown SDK result immediately with the owning output Schema;
    35	5. apply operation-specific retry, a complete-operation deadline, tracing, metrics, and redaction policy;
    36	6. return the decoded value without another wrapper layer.
    37	
    38	Use `Effect.gen`, meaningful `Effect.fn`, or local equivalents for readable sequential work. Keep one-use request mapping, rejection mapping, and decoding beside the operation. Extract only demonstrated reuse, stable domain policy, or a real I/O boundary.
    39	
    40	For native Effect HTTP/RPC clients, reuse the domain service contract instead
    41	of exposing the generated client or inventing a second public service. Keep
    42	Schema-selected response checks and named transport/decode failures with their
    43	semantic owner. Promise adaptation is unnecessary when the client already
    44	returns Effect. Check the provider's public adapters as well as its high-level
    45	services: Alchemy's `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient`, for example,
    46	already adapt a Cloudflare service binding through the published
    47	`alchemy/Cloudflare/Bridge` runtime entry. Check runtime entries before adding
    48	package-export patches or importing a broad provider entry. Qualify their error, retry and
    49	cancellation behaviour before writing a replacement.
    50	
    51	A deadline includes headers and decoded body. Test both stalled phases, one
    52	total budget after late headers, underlying cleanup and earlier interruption.
    53	Do not reset the clock at each phase or add an automatic retry by default.
    54	
    55	## Configure safely
    56	
    57	- Model semantic configuration with Schema and `Config`/`ConfigProvider`, using the repository's supported API.
    58	- Give configuration an owner-named structure rather than passing independent primitive strings and numbers through the codebase.
    59	- Keep secrets redacted and unwrap them only for immediate SDK construction.
    60	- Construct the SDK once in the live Layer unless its documented lifecycle requires scoped acquisition and release.
    61	- Override configuration in tests through a test `ConfigProvider` or the repository's established Layer mechanism.
    62	
    63	Yield checked Config while constructing the live adapter Layer, then keep SDK
    64	operations using those checked settings. Related settings can share an owning
    65	Schema. Follow the [configuration decision procedure](../strict-effect-ts/references/services/config-and-secrets.md)
    66	before adding a separate Context service for them; Config already works with
    67	`yield*`.
    68	
    69	## Model failures explicitly
    70	
    71	- Use owner-named Schema-tagged errors for expected configuration, transport, rate-limit, authentication, provider, and decode failures when those distinctions affect callers.
    72	- Preserve safe provider codes, operation names, retryability, and diagnostic context; do not place unchecked `unknown` payloads in public tagged errors.
    73	- Use tagged catches or pattern matching. Never use `instanceof` for provider-error policy.
    74	- Treat truly unexpected failures as defects only when callers cannot reasonably recover.
    75	
    76	## Adapt browser hosts and callbacks
    77	
    78	Keep the original host object when a method depends on `this`; do not detach
    79	the method or decode it into a copied data object. Validate the required
    80	capability with the owning Schema. Detect absence inside Effect and distinguish
    81	it from a supported host refusing an operation. Keep safe refusal details.
    82	
    83	Scope callback execution and registration together. Release unregisters or
    84	aborts registration and interrupts unfinished callbacks. Accommodate synchronous
    85	and Promise return forms only where a supported host requires them. Confine the
    86	bridge and justified lint exceptions to the named adapter. For a browser tool
    87	interface, follow the sibling
    88	[MCP/WebMCP pattern](../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/mcp-and-webmcp.md).
    89	
    90	For a PostHog browser SDK in a React-owned Effect Atom runtime, read the
    91	[PostHog browser adapter guide](references/posthog-browser.md). It covers scoped
    92	SDK ownership, explicit event operations, the synchronous capture callback,
    93	privacy controls and real-client delivery proof. Native Distilled management
    94	and backend Effect HTTP capture do not need Promise bridges.
    95	
    96	## Test and enforce
    97	
    98	Test service operations through mock/test Layers and test the live adapter boundary narrowly. Cover success, request encoding, provider rejection mapping, output decode failure, redaction, timeout/retry policy, and non-idempotent retry exclusion.
    99	
   100	Update affected architecture docs, READMEs, lint/custom rules and fixtures, CI commands, SPEC/tasks, and repository-owned skills. Add the narrowest reliable static or stale-pattern check the repository supports.
   101	
   102	Acceptance requires zero examples or public APIs containing:
   103	
   104	- a generic SDK `use` callback or raw-client accessor;
   105	- a raw `id: string` where an owning branded ID exists;
   106	- primitive/manual semantic configuration in place of Schema-backed `Config`;
   107	- `instanceof` provider-error branching;
   108	- an SDK result escaping without immediate Schema decoding;
   109	- a one-use wrapper/helper that merely forwards, maps, reads one property, or hides the SDK call.
   110	
   111	Run the repository's actual format, lint, typecheck, test, build, boundary, skill-validation, and stale-pattern checks appropriate to the change. Do not invent commands or claim the wrapper is safe when any prohibited pattern remains.
   112	
   113	## Keep checked values checked
   114	
   115	The live adapter owns actual untrusted replies. Decode there once and return the
   116	owning inferred type. A caller does not re-decode a typed service reply; a test
   117	Layer follows that same contract. Reuse the domain's branded fields and shared
   118	whole-record checks in a provider codec, including checks lost when fields are
   119	spread. Keep expected identity, completeness and range checks as domain policy.
   120	
   121	New branded values use the installed fallible constructor; map its issue to the
   122	operation's named error. Plain mappings from checked values stay immutable with
   123	Effect Array/Record functions. Optional provider/source fields decode to Option;
   124	historical missing/null distinctions belong in the source codec. Internal caches
   125	use checked readonly keys directly, with equality, full-address and cancellation
   126	tests. Neither SDK typings nor another internal decoder replaces boundary proof.

1	---
     2	name: effect-client-wrapper
     3	description: Design, implement, or review a typed Effect service around a third-party SDK, API client, callback library, or Promise-based provider. Use for provider adapters, service Layers, external-client configuration, request and response Schemas, typed provider errors, retries, and test Layers. Enforce named operations, branded identifiers, Schema-backed Config, immediate output decoding, flat Effects, and the explicit rejection of generic use callbacks, raw clients, primitive config, instanceof, and unchecked SDK outputs.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Effect Client Wrapper
     7	
     8	Create a semantic adapter owned by the application, not a generic Effect-shaped escape hatch around an SDK.
     9	
    10	## Establish the boundary
    11	
    12	1. Read applicable repository instructions, architecture docs, lint rules, installed Effect and SDK versions, and representative services and Layers.
    13	2. Identify the owner of every request, response, identifier, configuration value, error, retry policy, and runtime boundary.
    14	3. Research the cloned Effect v4 source, record its revision/version, then reconcile the chosen APIs with installed source/types. Use matching primary SDK source for its contract; DeepWiki through Executor MCP is secondary explanation for the upstream Effect/SDK repository.
    15	4. Prefer extending an existing semantic adapter over creating a parallel client abstraction.
    16	
    17	## Define the public service
    18	
    19	- Expose named domain/provider operations such as `getCustomer`, `sendMessage`, or `renderImage`.
    20	- Accept owning Schema-derived inputs and branded identifiers. Never substitute raw `id: string`.
    21	- Return only decoded application-owned or explicitly provider-owned Schema types.
    22	- Keep the raw SDK instance private to the live Layer or adapter module.
    23	- Provide a live Layer and a mock/test Layer at the same service contract.
    24	
    25	Do not expose a generic `use`, `run`, `withClient`, callback, unconstrained generic result, or raw-client accessor. Those APIs erase operation ownership, output provenance, retry policy, and testability.
    26	
    27	## Implement each operation linearly
    28	
    29	Use the locally installed Effect APIs. A named operation should read as one flat program:
    30	
    31	1. encode the checked request at its actual outbound contract, without re-decoding internal typed data;
    32	2. call exactly one SDK operation through `Effect.tryPromise`, callback adaptation, or the repository's boundary primitive;
    33	3. map rejection immediately into an owner-named typed Schema error with safe diagnostics;
    34	4. decode the unknown SDK result immediately with the owning output Schema;
    35	5. apply operation-specific retry, a complete-operation deadline, tracing, metrics, and redaction policy;
    36	6. return the decoded value without another wrapper layer.
    37	
    38	Use `Effect.gen`, meaningful `Effect.fn`, or local equivalents for readable sequential work. Keep one-use request mapping, rejection mapping, and decoding beside the operation. Extract only demonstrated reuse, stable domain policy, or a real I/O boundary.
    39	
    40	For native Effect HTTP/RPC clients, reuse the domain service contract instead
    41	of exposing the generated client or inventing a second public service. Keep
    42	Schema-selected response checks and named transport/decode failures with their
    43	semantic owner. Promise adaptation is unnecessary when the client already
    44	returns Effect. Check the provider's public adapters as well as its high-level
    45	services: Alchemy's `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient`, for example,
    46	already adapt a Cloudflare service binding through the published
    47	`alchemy/Cloudflare/Bridge` runtime entry. Check runtime entries before adding
    48	package-export patches or importing a broad provider entry. Qualify their error, retry and
    49	cancellation behaviour before writing a replacement.
    50	
    51	A deadline includes headers and decoded body. Test both stalled phases, one
    52	total budget after late headers, underlying cleanup and earlier interruption.
    53	Do not reset the clock at each phase or add an automatic retry by default.
    54	
    55	## Configure safely
    56	
    57	- Model semantic configuration with Schema and `Config`/`ConfigProvider`, using the repository's supported API.
    58	- Give configuration an owner-named structure rather than passing independent primitive strings and numbers through the codebase.
    59	- Keep secrets redacted and unwrap them only for immediate SDK construction.
    60	- Construct the SDK once in the live Layer unless its documented lifecycle requires scoped acquisition and release.
    61	- Override configuration in tests through a test `ConfigProvider` or the repository's established Layer mechanism.
    62	
    63	Yield checked Config while constructing the live adapter Layer, then keep SDK
    64	operations using those checked settings. Related settings can share an owning
    65	Schema. Follow the [configuration decision procedure](../strict-effect-ts/references/services/config-and-secrets.md)
    66	before adding a separate Context service for them; Config already works with
    67	`yield*`.
    68	
    69	## Model failures explicitly
    70	
    71	- Use owner-named Schema-tagged errors for expected configuration, transport, rate-limit, authentication, provider, and decode failures when those distinctions affect callers.
    72	- Preserve safe provider codes, operation names, retryability, and diagnostic context; do not place unchecked `unknown` payloads in public tagged errors.
    73	- Use tagged catches or pattern matching. Never use `instanceof` for provider-error policy.
    74	- Treat truly unexpected failures as defects only when callers cannot reasonably recover.
    75	
    76	## Adapt browser hosts and callbacks
    77	
    78	Keep the original host object when a method depends on `this`; do not detach
    79	the method or decode it into a copied data object. Validate the required
    80	capability with the owning Schema. Detect absence inside Effect and distinguish
    81	it from a supported host refusing an operation. Keep safe refusal details.
    82	
    83	Scope callback execution and registration together. Release unregisters or
    84	aborts registration and interrupts unfinished callbacks. Accommodate synchronous
    85	and Promise return forms only where a supported host requires them. Confine the
    86	bridge and justified lint exceptions to the named adapter. For a browser tool
    87	interface, follow the sibling
    88	[MCP/WebMCP pattern](../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/mcp-and-webmcp.md).
    89	
    90	For a PostHog browser SDK in a React-owned Effect Atom runtime, read the
    91	[PostHog browser adapter guide](references/posthog-browser.md). It covers scoped
    92	SDK ownership, explicit event operations, the synchronous capture callback,
    93	privacy controls and real-client delivery proof. Native Distilled management
    94	and backend Effect HTTP capture do not need Promise bridges.
    95	
    96	## Test and enforce
    97	
    98	Test service operations through mock/test Layers and test the live adapter boundary narrowly. Cover success, request encoding, provider rejection mapping, output decode failure, redaction, timeout/retry policy, and non-idempotent retry exclusion.
    99	
   100	Update affected architecture docs, READMEs, lint/custom rules and fixtures, CI commands, SPEC/tasks, and repository-owned skills. Add the narrowest reliable static or stale-pattern check the repository supports.
   101	
   102	Acceptance requires zero examples or public APIs containing:
   103	
   104	- a generic SDK `use` callback or raw-client accessor;
   105	- a raw `id: string` where an owning branded ID exists;
   106	- primitive/manual semantic configuration in place of Schema-backed `Config`;
   107	- `instanceof` provider-error branching;
   108	- an SDK result escaping without immediate Schema decoding;
   109	- a one-use wrapper/helper that merely forwards, maps, reads one property, or hides the SDK call.
   110	
   111	Run the repository's actual format, lint, typecheck, test, build, boundary, skill-validation, and stale-pattern checks appropriate to the change. Do not invent commands or claim the wrapper is safe when any prohibited pattern remains.
   112	
   113	## Keep checked values checked
   114	
   115	The live adapter owns actual untrusted replies. Decode there once and return the
   116	owning inferred type. A caller does not re-decode a typed service reply; a test
   117	Layer follows that same contract. Reuse the domain's branded fields and shared
   118	whole-record checks in a provider codec, including checks lost when fields are
   119	spread. Keep expected identity, completeness and range checks as domain policy.
   120	
   121	New branded values use the installed fallible constructor; map its issue to the
   122	operation's named error. Plain mappings from checked values stay immutable with
   123	Effect Array/Record functions. Optional provider/source fields decode to Option;
   124	historical missing/null distinctions belong in the source codec. Internal caches
   125	use checked readonly keys directly, with equality, full-address and cancellation
   126	tests. Neither SDK typings nor another internal decoder replaces boundary proof.
