    70	## Maintenance
    71	
    72	Every material slice decides `Change required`, `Preserve`, or `N/A` for docs,
    73	READMEs, architecture, standards, public/generated references, runbooks,
    74	proof/evidence, skills, lint/config/CI, and active SPEC/tasks. Update the
    75	earliest durable owner and necessary pointers in the same slice. Counts prove
    76	accounting only; semantic and consumer claims need owner review and
    77	boundary-matched proof.
    78	
    79	Use the plugin `development-workflows:docs-maintainer` skill for this impact decision on
    80	both PRD and ordinary changes. `$docs-writer` is limited to public-copy wording
    81	after the maintenance route has selected the owner; it cannot close lifecycle,
    82	generated-content, package, proof, or validation work. Background freshness
    83	scans produce report-only candidates and cannot publish policy or documentation
    84	without separately attached implementation authority, review and publication
    85	identity.
    86	
    87	`bun run check:docs` enforces the mechanical owner contract in
    88	[`../tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`](../tools/documentation/owner-policy.json).
    89	It checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
    90	coverage, public/maintainer separation, accepted public-status representation,
    91	and generated-source edges with bounded diagnostics and a JSON detail receipt.
    92	The command accepts `--json`; failed checks return a nonzero exit after the
    93	report is saved. Effect CLI owns option parsing.
    94	`draft` means authored, locally renderable, visibly labelled candidate content;
    95	`published` means explicitly accepted current public documentation. Neither
    96	status proves runtime or external availability.
    97	
    98	Acceptance-record Schemas live in `@taxkit/content`. The docs tool explicitly
    99	selects source exports so it can run in a fresh checkout before package builds.
   100	Version-two records include the reviewed source hash, which this check verifies;
   101	version-one records retain their historical contract. The local accepted
   102	catalogue builder, `bun run docs:catalogue`, requires version two, checks source
   103	bytes before and after compilation, and writes generated output only when
   104	accepted pages and matching navigation exist. It does not accept pages or
   105	establish publication by running. See
   106	[`../packages/docs-content/README.md`](../packages/docs-content/README.md).
   107	
   108	`bun run check:runbooks` Schema-decodes the canonical runbook contract, the
   109	current journey inventory and the exact historical HGI-203 journey snapshot,
   110	then reconciles the immutable packet digest, four Markdown owners, commands,
   111	evidence paths, stop operations, index rows and authority rows. It writes only
   112	the ignored bounded receipt `tmp/runbook-validation-report.json`, executes none
   113	of the documented procedures and establishes no consequential state.
   114	
   115	Shared development workflows: [latest plugin and repository profiles](skills.md).
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	This doc owns cross-package Effect service conventions. Rule-specific service
    18	contracts live with their owning rule packages and should link back here.
    19	
    20	The private [analytics package](../../packages/analytics/README.md) owns the
    21	two accepted event contracts. Its native backend Layer encodes a fixed provider
    22	request and maps transport failures to safe errors. The exact encoder admission
    23	in `oxlint.config.ts` covers that provider egress and its safe error-byte test;
    24	it does not admit runtime execution, raw JSON or decoding in neighbouring code.
    25	The package’s collection-header boundary is reused by the API and Website.
    26	The private `WebsiteAnalyticsRelay` exposes one native request handler with
    27	checked failures and no service requirements escaping its caller. Its named
    28	adapter captures native HttpClient once, decodes metadata at that explicit
    29	boundary, forwards bounded complete bytes, and owns each request scope and
    30	whole-operation deadline. It uses the existing server runner. Exact decoder
    31	permissions admit neither neighbouring decoders, raw fetch nor another runner;
    32	actual lint fixtures enforce those limits.
    33	The browser calculator transport reads its native preference at dispatch, and
    34	the server transport reads the current original request; neither freezes policy
    35	when its Layer is built. Missing server/browser hosts refuse collection.
    36	The application owns when to capture and which checked collection policy applies.
    37	The API application captures its delivery service during initialisation, then
    38	supplies it to each returned request operation. Worker and older MCP session
    39	delivery use their own native `waitUntil`; request collection remains fresh.
    40	T008 Website/browser composition and provider readback remain pending.
    41	
    42	## Service shape
    43	
    44	Prefer package-owned `Context.Service` services with explicit dependencies through
    45	the Effect `R` channel. Do not hide rule, parameter or runtime dependencies in
    46	module globals.
    47	
    48	Core service categories:
    49	
    50	- fact providers for accepted input facts
    51	- parameter services for tax-year tables and constants
    52	- rule layers that derive facts from facts and parameters
    53	- calculator programs that require facts and return schema-backed reports
    54	- calculator, API and SDK services that adapt transport, CLI or plain-client
    55	  inputs to engine inputs
    56	
    57	Public calculator services should live in `packages/calculators`, not HTTP
    58	handler modules. A calculator service method should own calculator lookup,
    59	context validation, metadata projection, graph diagnostics, scenario layer
    60	composition, `CalculationEngine` execution and expected error shaping. HTTP
    61	handlers should only pass route input to the service and return the resulting
    62	schema-backed value or tagged error envelope.
    63	
    64	## Effect-native primitives
    65	
    66	TaxKit code MUST use Effect-native primitives and platform APIs when they fit
    67	the problem. This is a consistency and reliability rule, not a style
    68	preference.
    69	
    70	Use:
    71	
    72	- `Data`, `Schema`, `Schema.TaggedClass`, `Schema.TaggedStruct`,
    73	  `Data.TaggedClass` and `Data.TaggedError` for domain values and expected
    74	  errors.
    75	- `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `Record`, `Option`, `Result`,
    76	  `Exit` and `Match` for collection processing, lookup results, closed-domain
    77	  dispatch and program results.
    78	- `Context`, `Context.Service`, `Layer`, `Config`, `ConfigProvider`,
    79	  `ManagedRuntime`, Bun runtime/platform APIs and `Command` for dependency
    80	  injection, configuration, app runtime lifecycle and process/platform work.
    81	
    82	Do not fall back to ad hoc classes, manual `_tag` object literals, mutable
    83	JavaScript `Map`/`Set` indexes, nullable lookups, `switch`, `Object.values`,
    84	`Object.entries`, custom env parsing, manual process signal orchestration,
    85	request-local runtime creation or hand-rolled runtime wrappers when Effect
    86	owns the pattern.
    87	
    88	Calculator-owned context, help and filter fields use `Option<Option<A>>` in
    89	checked TypeScript values: `None` means a missing key, `Some(None)` means a
    90	present undefined key, and `Some(Some(value))` means a present value. Owning
    91	constructors default omitted keys to `None`. JSON and HTTP query fields retain
    92	their ordinary optional representation. Flatten the two absent forms only where
    93	they mean the same thing; do not invent a jurisdiction or tax year. Code MUST NOT use undefined checks and defaulting such
    94	as `payload.jurisdiction ?? "AU"` to invent missing calculator context.
    95	Missing context MUST either remain absent, be decoded by a schema that
    96	explicitly owns the default, or fail with a tagged expected error.
    97	
    98	Code MUST use pipe-first composition for readable Effect and data pipelines
    99	when it keeps the source value visible and data flow clearer, for example
   100	`query.pipe(filterCalculatorEntries, toFactsResponse)`. Do not nest

1	# Services and Layers
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [Contract first](#contract-first)
     6	- [Named operations](#named-operations)
     7	- [Public methods and private helpers](#public-methods-and-private-helpers)
     8	- [Close public requirements](#close-public-requirements)
     9	- [Layer construction](#layer-construction)
    10	- [Layer dependency direction](#layer-dependency-direction)
    11	- [Layer names](#layer-names)
    12	- [Memory test Layers](#memorytest-layers)
    13	- [Layer construction failures](#layer-construction-failures)
    14	- [Avoid over-layering](#avoid-over-layering)
    15	- [Tests](#tests)
    16	
    17	## Contract first
    18	
    19	A service exposes domain capabilities, not an implementation technology.
    20	
    21	```ts
    22	interface AccountsContract {
    23	  readonly load: (id: AccountId) => Effect.Effect<Account, AccountNotFound | AccountsUnavailable>;
    24	
    25	  readonly create: (
    26	    input: CreateAccount,
    27	  ) => Effect.Effect<Account, InvalidAccount | AccountsUnavailable>;
    28	}
    29	```
    30	
    31	Use the installed Effect version's Context service/tag API. Give tags globally unique stable identifiers according to repository policy.
    32	
    33	## Named operations
    34	
    35	Prefer:
    36	
    37	- `loadAccount`;
    38	- `createRedirectUri`;
    39	- `queryDataset`;
    40	- `readDeployment`.
    41	
    42	Reject:
    43	
    44	- `request<T>(options)`;
    45	- `execute<T>(callback)`;
    46	- `withClient(fn)`;
    47	- `raw`;
    48	- `sdk`.
    49	
    50	A caller should express domain intent without knowing URL paths, SDK methods, or credentials.
    51	
    52	## Public methods and private helpers
    53	
    54	Public service methods use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`. This names
    55	the operation's span and preserves useful call-site information. Use the same
    56	name in live and test implementations. Pass a generator directly to `Effect.fn`
    57	when the method needs several steps; do not add an arrow returning `Effect.gen`.
    58	
    59	Private Effect helpers use `Effect.fnUntraced` when their work belongs to the
    60	calling operation's span. It adds no automatic function tracing or span; the
    61	caller owns that context. A private helper that owns a
    62	meaningful external call or separately measured operation can use named
    63	`Effect.fn`; privacy alone does not forbid a span. Pure, total helpers remain
    64	plain functions. Do not replace public methods with `fnUntraced` to reduce
    65	telemetry noise; choose the public operations and sampling policy deliberately.
    66	
    67	```ts
    68	const lookupAccount = Effect.fnUntraced(function* (id: AccountId) {
    69	  return yield* store.load(id);
    70	});
    71	
    72	return Accounts.of({
    73	  load: Effect.fn("Accounts.load")(function* (id: AccountId) {
    74	    return yield* lookupAccount(id);
    75	  }),
    76	});
    77	```
    78	
    79	Here `store` was acquired inside the Layer. A one-use helper should normally
    80	stay inline; this example describes instrumentation, not a reason to extract it.
    81	
    82	Use `.pipe` for a short sequence of transformations. A private function can
    83	return that Effect directly; a generator that only yields and returns one
    84	pipeline adds no useful step. The qualified 4.0.2 `fnUntraced` builder accepts
    85	generators, so do not wrap a direct Effect-returning function in it. Use a
    86	generator with `fnUntraced` when later work needs earlier
    87	results. For a single property selection in a pipeline, prefer the installed
    88	`Struct.get("field")` over a callback that only extracts that field. Destructuring
    89	checked records remains appropriate when several fields are used together.
    90	Do not create a one-use name for `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect`: keep the decode
    91	at the host boundary, and share the owning Schema rather than a decoder alias.
    92	
    93	## Close public requirements
    94	
    95	Public service operations should normally return:
    96	
    97	```text
    98	Effect<Success, DomainError, never>
    99	```
   100	
   101	The service Layer acquires transport, persistence, Config, Clock, or provider SDK requirements while constructing the implementation. This prevents dependency details leaking to every caller.
   102	
   103	Keep a requirement public only when it is intentionally part of composition, such as a generic policy module designed to work over a caller-supplied service.
   104	
   105	## Layer construction
   106	
   107	Owned Layers are static values, including test Layers. Put dependencies in the
   108	Layer's Requirements type channel rather than function arguments. Supply them
   109	with `Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(Dependency, checkedValue))`; tests can replace
   110	an implementation with native `Layer.mock` or another static Layer. Declaring a
   111	Layer does not acquire resources; building it in a Scope does.
   112	
   113	Native inline callbacks in `Layer.unwrap`, `Layer.suspend`, Effect operations
   114	and Atom runtime composition remain valid. Functions returning Effects or
   115	scoped fixture bundles remain valid too. The portable `strict-effect/static-layers`
   116	rule rejects recognised constructors, aliases, pipes, native router builders
   117	and Layer return types. It checks syntax, so opaque imported helper results
   118	still need clear owning types and review. There are no factory exceptions.
   119	
   120	Construct implementations in `live.layer.ts`:
   121	
   122	1. acquire dependencies;
   123	2. derive private helpers;
   124	3. define named operations with exact contract types;
   125	4. add spans/log annotations at semantic operations;
   126	5. return the service implementation;
   127	6. expose a Layer.
   128	
   129	Avoid side effects during module import.
   130	
   131	Choose the smallest construction that matches the work:
   132	
   133	| Construction                                            | Use it when                                                                                                          |
   134	| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   135	| `Layer.succeed(Service, Service.of(implementation))`    | The implementation is already available and construction performs no effects.                                        |
   136	| `Layer.effect(Service, effect)`                         | Construction acquires other services, reads Config, or creates Effect-managed state, a cache or a concurrency limit. |
   137	| `Layer.effect(Service, effect)` with scoped acquisition | A resource needs release when the Layer's scope closes.                                                              |
   138	
   139	For the qualified Effect v4 RC API, use the two-argument `Layer.effect`. Check
   140	installed types before copying this into a different version. `Service.of`
   141	checks the implementation against the service contract; it does not run it.
   142	
   143	```ts
   144	export const AccountsLive = Layer.effect(
   145	  Accounts,
   146	  Effect.gen(function* () {
   147	    const store = yield* AccountsStore;
   148	    return Accounts.of({
   149	      load: Effect.fn("Accounts.load")((id: AccountId) => store.load(id)),
   150	      create: Effect.fn("Accounts.create")((input: CreateAccount) => store.create(input)),
   151	    });
   152	  }),
   153	);
   154	```
   155	
   156	Create caches, `Ref`s and semaphores during acquisition, once per intended
   157	Layer lifetime. A shared application Layer means shared state; a request Layer
   158	means request state. Cache failure retention, size, timeout and concurrency
   159	are deliberate policies, not universal defaults. Acquire external handles with
   160	`Effect.acquireRelease` or the installed scoped constructor and keep release
   161	inside that scope. Avoid closing a resource before a returned stream finishes.
   162	
   163	## Layer dependency direction
   164	
   165	If `AccountsLive` needs `AccountsStore` and `IdentityProvider`, its Layer input contains those services. Compose them at the application root.
   166	
   167	Do not:
   168	
   169	- provide dependencies inside every operation;
   170	- import `AccountsStoreLive` from `service.ts`;
   171	- make `AccountsLive` read process environment itself if Config can be layered;
   172	- rebuild expensive clients per call.
   173	
   174	`Layer.provide` supplies a Layer's dependencies while exposing the target's
   175	outputs. `Layer.provideMerge` also retains the supplied outputs for other
   176	consumers. `Layer.mergeAll` combines independent Layers; it does not wire one
   177	Layer's output into another's input. Share the same Layer value at the root so
   178	normal build memoisation shares acquisition. Recreating a Layer factory or
   179	building separate runtimes can create extra clients and separate state.
   180	
   181	Acquire individual dependency services, not the whole request Context. The
   182	native host supplies request services in the incoming fibre; keep their lifetime
   183	with that host. The separate TanStack frontend supplies client Layers without
   184	borrowing the API request Context. Consumers import service contracts and
   185	provide live Layers at the root, rather than importing raw SDK constructors.
   186	
   187	## Layer names
   188	
   189	Use:
   190	
   191	- `AccountsLive`;
   192	- `AccountsMemory`;
   193	- `AccountsTest` when it is test-specific;
   194	- `AccountsHttpLive` only if multiple live transports coexist.
   195	
   196	`live.layer.ts` may export multiple closely related Layers, but avoid a global mega-Layer with unrelated domains.
   197	
   198	## Memory/test Layers
   199	
   200	Implement the identical service contract. A memory Layer may expose a separate control service for:
   201	
   202	- seeding state;
   203	- observing calls;
   204	- injecting failure;
   205	- advancing a simulated provider state.
   206	
   207	Do not add testing-only methods to the Production service contract.
   208	
   209	Make state immutable/Effect-managed and tests scoped so suites cannot leak state.
   210	
   211	## Layer construction failures
   212	
   213	If configuration or SDK construction can fail, express it in the Layer error channel and prove application startup handles it. Do not throw during import or constructor evaluation.
   214	
   215	Once a runtime is successfully built, public service operations may be closed over those dependencies.
   216	
   217	## Avoid over-layering
   218	
   219	Do not create:
   220	
   221	- a service for a pure stateless function;
   222	- a Layer that only wraps a static constant with no composition value;
   223	- one service per SDK method;
   224	- a separate Layer for every helper.
   225	
   226	Use services for substitutable capabilities, dependency boundaries, state/lifetime, provider isolation, or observability policy.
   227	
   228	For fixed host settings, yield checked Config in the Layer that uses them.
   229	`Layer.unwrap` can read settings and return existing Layers without inventing a
   230	new service. Follow the [configuration decision procedure](config-and-secrets.md#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
   231	to choose Config, a real Context service, request data or an already checked
   232	argument.
   233	
   234	## Tests
   235	
   236	Test:
   237	
   238	- contract through memory and controlled live adapter;
   239	- Layer builds with valid Config;
   240	- Layer fails with typed error for invalid Config/client construction;
   241	- public operation requirements are intentional;
   242	- provider client is not publicly exported;
   243	- dependencies are constructed once per intended scope.
     1	# Config and Secrets
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [Acquire configuration through Effect](#acquire-configuration-through-effect)
     6	- [Read settings in the owning Layer](#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
     7	- [Choose Config, Context or request data](#choose-config-context-or-request-data)
     8	- [Root host adapter](#root-host-adapter)
     9	- [Refine primitive values](#refine-primitive-values)
    10	- [Secrets](#secrets)
    11	- [Secret JSON bindings](#secret-json-bindings)
    12	- [Configuration ownership](#configuration-ownership)
    13	- [Reloading](#reloading)
    14	- [Tests](#tests)
    15	
    16	## Acquire configuration through Effect
    17	
    18	Use Config for values supplied by the host:
    19	
    20	- environment variables;
    21	- platform bindings;
    22	- file/config providers;
    23	- test configuration;
    24	- provider endpoints and safe IDs;
    25	- timeouts, retry counts, and feature policy.
    26	
    27	Do not read `process.env`, `Bun.env`, `import.meta.env`, or Cloudflare bindings throughout domain code.
    28	
    29	## Read settings in the owning Layer
    30	
    31	`Config` is already yieldable. A native Effect host can supply its
    32	`ConfigProvider`, and an owning Layer can read a checked value with
    33	`yield* Config.schema(OwnedSchema, "KEY")`. No separate Context service is
    34	needed just to make a setting available through `yield*`.
    35	
    36	For settings that stay fixed during the application's lifetime:
    37	
    38	1. Inspect the installed host's configuration support. Reuse its native
    39	   `ConfigProvider`; replacing it with `fromEnv` can lose platform bindings or
    40	   test values. If the host has none, use the root adapter described below.
    41	2. Reuse the Schema owned by that setting's domain. Check its format, allowed
    42	   values and bounds, and keep meaningful strings branded.
    43	3. Read the Config while building the Layer that uses it. Use
    44	   `Layer.effect(Service, effect)` to construct an existing service, or
    45	   `Layer.unwrap(effect)` when the result is a composition of existing Layers.
    46	   Reusable static Layers receive already checked caller inputs through named
    47	   Context requirements. Keep the configuration reader at the host edge.
    48	4. Close the service operations or route registrations over that checked value.
    49	   Build the application Layer once at startup, so each request uses the same
    50	   settings and does not rebuild clients or registrations.
    51	5. Let missing required values and invalid input fail Layer construction with
    52	   the native typed `ConfigError`, or map it to the owner's named startup error.
    53	   Report the key and a safe constraint; do not expose the value in diagnostics.
    54	
    55	For the qualified Effect `4.0.2` API, a route Layer can use this shape:
    56	
    57	```ts
    58	import * as Config from "effect/Config";
    59	import * as Effect from "effect/Effect";
    60	import * as Layer from "effect/Layer";
    61	import { ApiOrigin } from "./schemas";
    62	import { ApiIdentity, routes } from "./routes";
    63	
    64	export const ApiRoutes = Layer.unwrap(
    65	  Effect.gen(function* () {
    66	    const origin = yield* Config.schema(ApiOrigin, "API_ORIGIN");
    67	    return routes.pipe(Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(ApiIdentity, { origin })));
    68	  }),
    69	);
    70	```
    71	
    72	Here `ApiOrigin` is the existing branded address Schema. The static `routes`
    73	Layer requires `ApiIdentity`, whose value contains that checked origin. These
    74	imports stand for the receiving project's owners; reuse an existing requirement
    75	and Schema where available. Recheck APIs against installed types before
    76	using this example in another version.
    77	
    78	Apply the same steps to other settings:
    79	
    80	| Setting                                      | Check and ownership                                                                                                  |
    81	| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    82	| Public address or provider endpoint          | Check the allowed URL shape in the owning Layer before registering links or constructing the client.                 |
    83	| Stage or feature switch                      | Check the declared values before selecting the implementation; avoid silently treating an invalid value as disabled. |
    84	| Batch size, retry count or concurrency limit | Check integer bounds before building the queue, retry policy or semaphore.                                           |
    85	| Timeout                                      | Check supported units and positive bounds before closing operations over the timeout policy.                         |
    86	| Credential                                   | Acquire a redacted value in the private provider Layer and keep it out of public results and diagnostics.            |
    87	
    88	Provide test settings through the same route Layer:
    89	
    90	```ts
    91	import * as ConfigProvider from "effect/ConfigProvider";
    92	
    93	const TestRoutes = ApiRoutes.pipe(
    94	  Layer.provide(
    95	    ConfigProvider.layer(ConfigProvider.fromUnknown({ API_ORIGIN: "https://api.example.com" })),
    96	  ),
    97	);
    98	```
    99	
   100	This replaces the provider for that test without changing the process
   101	environment. Building the same Layer in a separate runtime gives that runtime
   102	its own settings; it is not a module-global snapshot.
   103	
   104	## Choose Config, Context or request data
   105	
   106	Choose by what the value does and how long it must live:
   107	
   108	| Need                                                                                                          | Use                                                                                               |
   109	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   110	| Host setting fixed for a Layer's lifetime                                                                     | Yield checked Config while constructing that Layer.                                               |
   111	| Named operations, managed state/resources, substitutable implementation or deliberately shared checked policy | A Context service built by its owning Layer.                                                      |
   112	| Settings that change while the application runs                                                               | A service or subscription with checked updates and an explicit consistency policy; see Reloading. |
   113	| Data belonging to the current HTTP request                                                                    | Yield the native request service inside the request handler and check the needed fields.          |
   114	| Already checked input supplied by a caller or helper                                                          | Use a named requirement for a static Layer; ordinary helpers keep typed arguments.                |
   115	
   116	Read fixed host settings through Config. Supply already checked caller values
   117	to static Layers through named Context requirements; this allows native Layer
   118	replacement in tests. Do not add another reader, forwarding factory or runtime.
   119	Ordinary helper arguments still express a deliberate caller choice. Browser code receives only checked public settings through the
   120	application's existing loader/runtime boundary; server secrets stay private.
   121	
   122	## Root host adapter
   123	
   124	If a platform cannot provide an Effect ConfigProvider directly:
   125	
   126	1. read the host environment at the application boundary;
   127	2. select only owned keys;
   128	3. construct a ConfigProvider or typed adapter;
   129	4. decode/refine values;
   130	5. provide it to the runtime;
   131	6. keep the raw environment object private.
   132	
   133	Check whether the installed host exposes a native adapter for its encoded
   134	bindings before writing a decoder for those bindings. For qualified Alchemy
   135	`2.0.0-beta.81`, `reifyBoundConfigProvider` from `alchemy/Runtime` unwraps its
   136	protected markers around a `ConfigProvider.fromUnknown` source. Native Effect
   137	Workers already supply it; a non-Effect host can reuse it in its private root
   138	adapter. Pass only the selected app keys to both the provider and the helper.
   139	Keep this translation out of domain Config declarations.
   140	
   141	Tests supply a deterministic provider rather than mutating ambient environment.
   142	
   143	## Refine primitive values
   144	
   145	Inspect the installed Schema and Config exports before choosing a codec. Start
   146	with the native data type and add the owner's checks and brand; do not write
   147	another URL, number, JSON, duration, UUID or secret parser.
   148	
   149	For qualified Effect `4.0.2`:
   150	
   151	| Input and needed value            | Native choice and required owner checks                                                                                                                                                                           |
   152	| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   153	| URL string to a URL value         | `Schema.URLFromString`, or `Schema.URL` through Config's native string codec. Check protocols, credentials and the allowed URL components, then brand the owned address.                                          |
   154	| String identifier or closed stage | The existing owning Schema, using native literals or a business format check and `Schema.brand`. Use `Schema.isUUID` for a UUID contract. A brand alone does not check the format.                                |
   155	| Port, count or finite measurement | `Schema.Int` or `Schema.Finite` with native range checks and the owning brand. Config converts its string source through the native codec; `Schema.NumberFromString` is also available for a string-only ingress. |
   156	| Boolean switch                    | `Config.Boolean`, which uses `Schema.BooleanLiterals`. Check its accepted spellings; use an explicit literal Schema if the host contract requires stricter input.                                                 |
   157	| Timeout or interval               | `Schema.DurationFromString`, or `Config.Duration`. Check positive, finite bounds appropriate to the operation before using the duration.                                                                          |
   158	| JSON settings                     | `Schema.fromJsonString(OwnedSchema)` inside `Config.schema`. Preserve the complete owning record and its checks.                                                                                                  |
   159	| Structured settings               | `Config.schema(OwnedSchema)` for a provider record; `Config.all` composes existing declarations without redefining their keys.                                                                                    |
   160	| Separated list or dictionary      | `Config.Array` or `Config.Record` with owning element/key/value Schemas and explicit separators when the source contract needs them.                                                                              |
   161	| Optional host input               | `Config.option` for missing settings. At other boundaries, select the matching native Schema Option codec for omitted, undefined or null input. Invalid input remains an error.                                   |
   162	| Private credential                | `Schema.RedactedFromValue(OwnedCredentialSchema)` through Config for a checked branded secret, or `Config.Redacted` when no stronger owner exists. Unwrap only at the private provider boundary.                  |
   163	
   164	Native URL decoding can normalise its source. Keep original-source checks when
   165	the contract requires an exact serialised browser origin. When a checked URL
   166	must become a distinct branded string such as its origin, construct that new
   167	value with the owning Schema's `makeEffect`. Map its `SchemaIssue.Issue` to the
   168	native `ConfigError` through `Config.mapEffect`; do not cast the string or
   169	replace the native URL parser.
   170	
   171	Use `Config.withDefault` or `Config.option` for missing input. They do not
   172	recover from invalid input or a partly supplied group. An optional feature can
   173	have a valid checked disabled setting; invalid configuration is still an error.
   174	Never wrap required stage, address or combined application settings in
   175	`Config.orElse(() => Config.succeed(disabledValue))`: this discards every
   176	`ConfigError`, including provider read failures, and can hide a broken deployment.
   177	Let the typed failure reach startup or the application's checked error result.
   178	If an explicitly accepted policy requires recovery for a particular optional
   179	setting, contain it in that declaration, document the exact recovered failures
   180	and retain a safe diagnostic. Keep checks relating two settings, such as
   181	matching a project's stage to its Worker, when composing declarations. Copying
   182	a record's fields does not copy its record checks.
   183	
   184	Map invalid configuration to a typed startup/config error with key name and
   185	safe constraint, never its value.
   186	
   187	Recheck these choices against the receiving installation. The qualified source
   188	is Effect's [Config](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691/packages/effect/src/Config.ts)
   189	and [Schema](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts),
   190	plus Alchemy's [runtime binding adapter](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy-async/blob/e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e/packages/alchemy/src/Runtime.ts).
   191	
   192	## Secrets
   193	
   194	Acquire secrets as Redacted values or the installed equivalent. Unwrap only inside the smallest provider request boundary.
   195	
   196	Rules:
   197	
   198	- never convert a secret to a normal string for convenience;
   199	- never include secret values in error fields;
   200	- never interpolate secrets into logs, spans, metrics, or receipts;
   201	- never place a secret in a service's public success type;
   202	- never persist it in test snapshots;
   203	- choose the narrowest supported native authentication method; do not require
   204	  OIDC when a config-scoped read-only service token meets the approved boundary.
   205	
   206	For Alchemy deployments backed by Doppler, follow the canonical
   207	[native sources and sign-in procedure](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/services-config-and-errors.md#native-doppler-and-dotenv-sources).
   208	Local and hosted runs both load Doppler, then optional ignored `.env`, with shell
   209	stack settings explicitly disabled. Keep native provider sign-in separate from
   210	the settings it unlocks. Read settings through checked Config in their owning
   211	Layer; do not add another secret reader or mutate the process environment.
   212	
   213	## Secret JSON bindings
   214	
   215	When a platform binding contains JSON:
   216	
   217	1. obtain it as redacted;
   218	2. expose/unredact only inside a boundary Effect;
   219	3. decode JSON using an owned Schema;
   220	4. construct a private credentials value;
   221	5. discard the plaintext as soon as possible;
   222	6. log only credential class and safe scope.
   223	
   224	Do not use unchecked `JSON.parse`.
   225	
   226	## Configuration ownership
   227	
   228	Keep domain Config near the live Layer that owns it. A shared application config module may compose domain Config values but should not become an untyped registry of every environment key.
   229	
   230	Export reusable declarations from the owner's `config.ts` beside its Schemas.
   231	The declaration combines the Schema and key, stays lazy until yielded, and can
   232	be reused by multiple Layers. Keep cross-domain composition with an owner that
   233	can depend on all participating domains without creating a package cycle.
   234	
   235	Related settings can share an owning record Schema and Config recipe. Group
   236	them because they belong to the same client or policy; reading several settings
   237	does not by itself require a new Context service.
   238	
   239	Expose an environment key when the host needs to choose a different value for
   240	a deployment. Keep supported protocol implementations and fixed input validity
   241	rules in code. An access policy can become checked Config when deployments need
   242	different access; that does not make malformed inputs valid.
   243	
   244	Name keys consistently and document:
   245	
   246	- owner;
   247	- environment/stage scope;
   248	- secret status;
   249	- default;
   250	- validation;
   251	- rotation/reload behaviour.
   252	
   253	Avoid defaults for Production-critical identity and credentials. Missing should fail at startup.
   254	
   255	## Reloading
   256	
   257	Most application identity/config should be immutable for a runtime. If dynamic reload is required:
   258	
   259	- model it as a service or subscription;
   260	- decode every new value;
   261	- define consistency and failure behaviour;
   262	- avoid partially updated configuration;
   263	- instrument safe version/change identity.
   264	
   265	Do not poll raw environment variables on each operation.
   266	
   267	## Tests
   268	
   269	Test:
   270	
   271	- valid Config construction;
   272	- missing required keys;
   273	- refinement failure;
   274	- default policy;
   275	- redaction in logs/errors/inspection;
   276	- test provider isolation;
   277	- stage-specific key separation;
   278	- no ambient environment dependence.
     1	# Runtimes and Host Boundaries
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [One owner per host lifecycle](#one-owner-per-host-lifecycle)
     6	- [Adapter shape](#adapter-shape)
     7	- [Runtime composition](#runtime-composition)
     8	- [Shutdown](#shutdown)
     9	- [Cloudflare Workers](#cloudflare-workers)
    10	- [Framework loaders actions](#framework-loadersactions)
    11	- [Browser](#browser)
    12	- [Tests](#tests)
    13	- [Runtime anti-patterns](#runtime-anti-patterns)
    14	
    15	## One owner per host lifecycle
    16	
    17	An application owns runtime construction and disposal. A package exposes Effect programs and Layers.
    18	
    19	Typical owners:
    20	
    21	- Bun/Node CLI main;
    22	- HTTP server bootstrap;
    23	- Cloudflare Worker module/handler adapter;
    24	- browser application root;
    25	- test runner;
    26	- Alchemy entrypoint.
    27	
    28	Construct at most one long-lived runtime per independent host lifecycle. A browser and server may need separate runtimes because their environments differ.
    29	
    30	## Adapter shape
    31	
    32	Keep adapters small:
    33	
    34	```text
    35	host input
    36	  -> Schema decode
    37	  -> named Effect operation
    38	  -> provide application runtime
    39	  -> execute
    40	  -> Schema encode / host response
    41	```
    42	
    43	Do not perform domain branching, retry loops, provider calls, or manual logging in the adapter.
    44	
    45	## Runtime composition
    46	
    47	Compose Layers by dependency:
    48	
    49	1. platform services;
    50	2. Config provider;
    51	3. transport/storage/provider Layers;
    52	4. domain live Layers;
    53	5. observability Layers;
    54	6. application services;
    55	7. runtime.
    56	
    57	Memoise shared Layers according to the installed Effect API. Avoid constructing a new SDK/exporter/client for each request unless per-request lifetime is required.
    58	
    59	## Shutdown
    60	
    61	Tie runtime disposal to:
    62	
    63	- process signals for CLI/server;
    64	- framework shutdown/hot-reload lifecycle;
    65	- Worker request completion for scoped work;
    66	- test scope/finaliser;
    67	- explicit Alchemy callback lifecycle.
    68	
    69	Do not leave timers, sockets, spans, or fibres detached after shutdown.
    70	
    71	## Cloudflare Workers
    72	
    73	Treat the exported `fetch` handler as a host adapter.
    74	
    75	- Decode bindings once into a typed service/Config Layer.
    76	- Keep secrets redacted.
    77	- Use the host's incoming Effect request fibre when it supplies one; otherwise
    78	  run through the application's sole host runner.
    79	- Connect background completion to `ExecutionContext.waitUntil` or the installed platform integration.
    80	- Preserve interruption/resource finalisers within the platform constraints.
    81	- Avoid global mutable request state.
    82	
    83	Separate platform telemetry from application Effect telemetry.
    84	
    85	For the native Alchemy API, build shared Layers in the Worker-instance Scope.
    86	Each incoming request keeps its own Scope, interruption and response cleanup.
    87	The separate TanStack Website owns typed clients and one `runtime.server.ts`
    88	runner; its private binding adapter forwards requests to the same-stage API.
    89	Do not lend Effect Context or request services through TanStack, merge them
    90	into its runtime, or borrow native tracer hooks. The native API owns its request
    91	telemetry. Any frontend host-span adapter needs its own qualified owner and
    92	tests. Follow
    93	[hosted web telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md)
    94	for those separate lifetimes and proof limits.
    95	
    96	## Framework loaders/actions
    97	
    98	When a framework requires a Promise:
    99	
   100	- use one runtime bridge;
   101	- call one named operation;
   102	- encode only serialisable success/error data;
   103	- preserve redirects/responses as explicit protocol values;
   104	- do not return Effect services or Causes to the client.
   105	
   106	Hydration boundaries require encoded values. Never assume class instances, provider errors, or arbitrary tagged objects survive serialisation.
   107	
   108	## Browser
   109	
   110	Use a client runtime only for client-owned effects. Do not ship server secrets, provider Layers, filesystem services, or server Config.
   111	
   112	Web owners use `runtime.server.ts` and `runtime.client.ts`, with imports inside
   113	TanStack's matching environment functions. Runtime permission comes from the
   114	repository's exact allowed paths, not a filename suffix. React owns the browser
   115	Atom runtime and registry lifetime.
   116	
   117	Model browser lifecycle:
   118	
   119	- abort/interruption on navigation or unmount;
   120	- subscriptions scoped to components/routes;
   121	- transport through a typed client service;
   122	- cached state through a declared cache/store service;
   123	- telemetry with browser-safe fields.
   124	
   125	## Tests
   126	
   127	Tests may execute Effect directly through the test integration or a scoped test runtime. Do not make each test recreate unrelated live dependencies. Compose a deterministic test Layer and release it after the suite/test scope.
   128	
   129	## Runtime anti-patterns
   130	
   131	Reject:
   132	
   133	- `Effect.runPromise` inside `service.ts`;
   134	- one runtime per function call;
   135	- global runtime in a shared package;
   136	- environment reads during module import;
   137	- live Layer construction in React render;
   138	- swallowed shutdown/finaliser errors;
   139	- detached Promise background work.
     1	# Policy and Exceptions
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [The default](#the-default)
     6	- [Boundary test](#boundary-test)
     7	- [Host exceptions](#host-exceptions)
     8	- [Explicit exception record](#explicit-exception-record)
     9	- [Defects versus expected failures](#defects-versus-expected-failures)
    10	- [Strict review searches](#strict-review-searches)
    11	- [Do not fetishise syntax](#do-not-fetishise-syntax)
    12	
    13	## The default
    14	
    15	Use Effect whenever owned TypeScript performs or coordinates:
    16	
    17	- failure;
    18	- asynchronous work;
    19	- external input/output;
    20	- configuration;
    21	- resource acquisition/release;
    22	- time, retry, or randomness;
    23	- mutable or concurrent state;
    24	- queues, streams, or background work;
    25	- logging, tracing, or metrics.
    26	
    27	Keep plain TypeScript for total, deterministic leaf computation over decoded values.
    28	
    29	## Boundary test
    30	
    31	Ask four questions:
    32	
    33	1. Can this operation fail for an expected reason?
    34	2. Does it depend on the world outside its arguments?
    35	3. Does it have lifetime, cancellation, concurrency, or state semantics?
    36	4. Does it cross a trust or serialisation boundary?
    37	
    38	If any answer is yes, model it as Effect.
    39	
    40	## Host exceptions
    41	
    42	Frameworks may require:
    43	
    44	- a synchronous render function;
    45	- a Promise-returning loader/action;
    46	- a Worker `fetch` handler;
    47	- a Bun/Node CLI main;
    48	- a callback registration;
    49	- an Alchemy provider callback.
    50	
    51	Keep the exception at the outermost adapter:
    52	
    53	1. decode host input;
    54	2. construct a named Effect program;
    55	3. provide the application runtime/Layer;
    56	4. execute once;
    57	5. translate typed failure to the host protocol;
    58	6. tie shutdown to host lifecycle.
    59	
    60	Do not call `Effect.runPromise` in domain or package code.
    61	
    62	## Explicit exception record
    63	
    64	If owned code must use a normally forbidden construct, place a bounded comment or architecture rule that states:
    65	
    66	- host or measured constraint;
    67	- exact file/function;
    68	- why an Effect API cannot satisfy it;
    69	- how the exception is encapsulated;
    70	- test that prevents semantic leakage;
    71	- removal/review condition.
    72	
    73	Examples:
    74	
    75	- host callback must return Promise;
    76	- generated SDK type contains `any`;
    77	- native Map is measurably required inside one service;
    78	- a host requires one exact writable property during a controlled lifetime.
    79	
    80	React rendering can use Effect Array functions synchronously; it does not need a native collection exception.
    81	
    82	“Simpler” and “the SDK uses it” are not sufficient.
    83	
    84	## Defects versus expected failures
    85	
    86	Use the typed error channel for:
    87	
    88	- validation;
    89	- missing records;
    90	- provider rejection;
    91	- permissions;
    92	- timeout;
    93	- unavailable dependency;
    94	- conflict;
    95	- protocol/codec mismatch;
    96	- user cancellation when domain-relevant.
    97	
    98	Use defects only for impossible invariants, programmer bugs, or corrupted assumptions that cannot be handled meaningfully. Do not convert expected failure to `die` to make a signature look clean.
    99	
   100	## Strict review searches
   101	
   102	Search changed owned code for:
   103	
   104	```text
   105	async
   106	new Promise
   107	Promise.
   108	throw
   109	catch (
   110	fetch(
   111	process.env
   112	Bun.env
   113	import.meta.env
   114	JSON.parse
   115	JSON.stringify
   116	Date.now
   117	new Date(
   118	Math.random
   119	setTimeout
   120	setInterval
   121	console.
   122	new Map
   123	new Set
   124	 as
   125	: any
   126	Effect.run
   127	```
   128	
   129	Classify every match. Generated, vendor, fixtures, and host adapters may be excluded only through explicit path policy.
   130	
   131	## Do not fetishise syntax
   132	
   133	Strict Effect is about semantics, not maximizing `Effect.gen`.
   134	
   135	- Keep pure Effect `Array.map`/`reduce`/`unfold` transformations synchronous; they do not need Effect.gen. Use immutable values even inside a leaf.
   136	- Do not wrap a constant in `Effect.succeed` unless it participates in an Effect interface.
   137	- Do not create a Layer for a static value with no dependency/lifecycle role.
   138	- Do not split a linear program into tiny helpers just to look functional.
   139	
   140	The goal is explicit failure, dependency, lifetime, concurrency, and observability—not ceremony.
   141	
   142	An exception must name its exact repository-relative file and operation/property.
   143	Do not allow an entire file, glob, filename suffix, tests folder or package to
   144	use mutation or execute Effect. The native API already owns its request fibre
   145	and Scope; return the native Effect handler instead of adding a runner. A
   146	framework that truly requires a Promise gets one checked application runner,
   147	whose lint allowance is a complete path. A similarly named package file remains
   148	forbidden. Test both the allowed operation and a nearby forbidden operation.

    17	## Contract first
    18	
    19	A service exposes domain capabilities, not an implementation technology.
    20	
    21	```ts
    22	interface AccountsContract {
    23	  readonly load: (id: AccountId) => Effect.Effect<Account, AccountNotFound | AccountsUnavailable>;
    24	
    25	  readonly create: (
    26	    input: CreateAccount,
    27	  ) => Effect.Effect<Account, InvalidAccount | AccountsUnavailable>;
    28	}
    29	```
    30	
    31	Use the installed Effect version's Context service/tag API. Give tags globally unique stable identifiers according to repository policy.
    32	
    33	## Named operations
    34	
    35	Prefer:
    36	
    37	- `loadAccount`;
    38	- `createRedirectUri`;
    39	- `queryDataset`;
    40	- `readDeployment`.
    41	
    42	Reject:
    43	
    44	- `request<T>(options)`;
    45	- `execute<T>(callback)`;
    46	- `withClient(fn)`;
    47	- `raw`;
    48	- `sdk`.
    49	
    50	A caller should express domain intent without knowing URL paths, SDK methods, or credentials.
    51	
    52	## Public methods and private helpers
    53	
    54	Public service methods use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`. This names
    55	the operation's span and preserves useful call-site information. Use the same
    56	name in live and test implementations. Pass a generator directly to `Effect.fn`
    57	when the method needs several steps; do not add an arrow returning `Effect.gen`.
    58	
    59	Private Effect helpers use `Effect.fnUntraced` when their work belongs to the
    60	calling operation's span. It adds no automatic function tracing or span; the
    61	caller owns that context. A private helper that owns a
    62	meaningful external call or separately measured operation can use named
    63	`Effect.fn`; privacy alone does not forbid a span. Pure, total helpers remain
    64	plain functions. Do not replace public methods with `fnUntraced` to reduce
    65	telemetry noise; choose the public operations and sampling policy deliberately.
    66	
    67	```ts
    68	const lookupAccount = Effect.fnUntraced(function* (id: AccountId) {
    69	  return yield* store.load(id);
    70	});
    71	
    72	return Accounts.of({
    73	  load: Effect.fn("Accounts.load")(function* (id: AccountId) {
    74	    return yield* lookupAccount(id);
    75	  }),
    76	});
    77	```
    78	
    79	Here `store` was acquired inside the Layer. A one-use helper should normally
    80	stay inline; this example describes instrumentation, not a reason to extract it.
    81	
    82	Use `.pipe` for a short sequence of transformations. A private function can
    83	return that Effect directly; a generator that only yields and returns one
    84	pipeline adds no useful step. The qualified 4.0.2 `fnUntraced` builder accepts
    85	generators, so do not wrap a direct Effect-returning function in it. Use a
    86	generator with `fnUntraced` when later work needs earlier
    87	results. For a single property selection in a pipeline, prefer the installed
    88	`Struct.get("field")` over a callback that only extracts that field. Destructuring
    89	checked records remains appropriate when several fields are used together.
    90	Do not create a one-use name for `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect`: keep the decode
    91	at the host boundary, and share the owning Schema rather than a decoder alias.
    92	
    93	## Close public requirements
    94	
    95	Public service operations should normally return:
    96	
    97	```text
    98	Effect<Success, DomainError, never>
    99	```
   100	
   101	The service Layer acquires transport, persistence, Config, Clock, or provider SDK requirements while constructing the implementation. This prevents dependency details leaking to every caller.
   102	
   103	Keep a requirement public only when it is intentionally part of composition, such as a generic policy module designed to work over a caller-supplied service.
   104	
   105	## Layer construction
   106	
   107	Owned Layers are static values, including test Layers. Put dependencies in the
   108	Layer's Requirements type channel rather than function arguments. Supply them
   109	with `Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(Dependency, checkedValue))`; tests can replace
   110	an implementation with native `Layer.mock` or another static Layer. Declaring a
   111	Layer does not acquire resources; building it in a Scope does.
   112	
   113	Native inline callbacks in `Layer.unwrap`, `Layer.suspend`, Effect operations
   114	and Atom runtime composition remain valid. Functions returning Effects or
   115	scoped fixture bundles remain valid too. The portable `strict-effect/static-layers`
   116	rule rejects recognised constructors, aliases, pipes, native router builders
   117	and Layer return types. It checks syntax, so opaque imported helper results
   118	still need clear owning types and review. There are no factory exceptions.
   119	
   120	Construct implementations in `live.layer.ts`:
   121	
   122	1. acquire dependencies;
   123	2. derive private helpers;
   124	3. define named operations with exact contract types;
   125	4. add spans/log annotations at semantic operations;
   126	5. return the service implementation;
   127	6. expose a Layer.
   128	
   129	Avoid side effects during module import.
   130	
   131	Choose the smallest construction that matches the work:
   132	
   133	| Construction                                            | Use it when                                                                                                          |
   134	| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   135	| `Layer.succeed(Service, Service.of(implementation))`    | The implementation is already available and construction performs no effects.                                        |
   136	| `Layer.effect(Service, effect)`                         | Construction acquires other services, reads Config, or creates Effect-managed state, a cache or a concurrency limit. |
   137	| `Layer.effect(Service, effect)` with scoped acquisition | A resource needs release when the Layer's scope closes.                                                              |
   138	
   139	For the qualified Effect v4 RC API, use the two-argument `Layer.effect`. Check
   140	installed types before copying this into a different version. `Service.of`
   141	checks the implementation against the service contract; it does not run it.
   142	
   143	```ts
   144	export const AccountsLive = Layer.effect(
   145	  Accounts,
   146	  Effect.gen(function* () {
   147	    const store = yield* AccountsStore;
   148	    return Accounts.of({
   149	      load: Effect.fn("Accounts.load")((id: AccountId) => store.load(id)),
   150	      create: Effect.fn("Accounts.create")((input: CreateAccount) => store.create(input)),
   151	    });
   152	  }),
   153	);
   154	```
   155	
   156	Create caches, `Ref`s and semaphores during acquisition, once per intended
   157	Layer lifetime. A shared application Layer means shared state; a request Layer
   158	means request state. Cache failure retention, size, timeout and concurrency
   159	are deliberate policies, not universal defaults. Acquire external handles with
   160	`Effect.acquireRelease` or the installed scoped constructor and keep release
   161	inside that scope. Avoid closing a resource before a returned stream finishes.
   162	
   163	## Layer dependency direction
   164	
   165	If `AccountsLive` needs `AccountsStore` and `IdentityProvider`, its Layer input contains those services. Compose them at the application root.
   166	
   167	Do not:
   168	
   169	- provide dependencies inside every operation;
   170	- import `AccountsStoreLive` from `service.ts`;
   171	- make `AccountsLive` read process environment itself if Config can be layered;
   172	- rebuild expensive clients per call.
   173	
   174	`Layer.provide` supplies a Layer's dependencies while exposing the target's
   175	outputs. `Layer.provideMerge` also retains the supplied outputs for other
   176	consumers. `Layer.mergeAll` combines independent Layers; it does not wire one
   177	Layer's output into another's input. Share the same Layer value at the root so
   178	normal build memoisation shares acquisition. Recreating a Layer factory or
   179	building separate runtimes can create extra clients and separate state.
   180	
   181	Acquire individual dependency services, not the whole request Context. The
   182	native host supplies request services in the incoming fibre; keep their lifetime
   183	with that host. The separate TanStack frontend supplies client Layers without
   184	borrowing the API request Context. Consumers import service contracts and
   185	provide live Layers at the root, rather than importing raw SDK constructors.
   186	
   187	## Layer names
   188	
   189	Use:
   190	
   191	- `AccountsLive`;
   192	- `AccountsMemory`;
   193	- `AccountsTest` when it is test-specific;
   194	- `AccountsHttpLive` only if multiple live transports coexist.
   195	
   196	`live.layer.ts` may export multiple closely related Layers, but avoid a global mega-Layer with unrelated domains.
   197	
   198	## Memory/test Layers
   199	
   200	Implement the identical service contract. A memory Layer may expose a separate control service for:
   201	
   202	- seeding state;
   203	- observing calls;
   204	- injecting failure;
   205	- advancing a simulated provider state.
   206	
   207	Do not add testing-only methods to the Production service contract.
   208	
   209	Make state immutable/Effect-managed and tests scoped so suites cannot leak state.
   210	
   211	## Layer construction failures
   212	
   213	If configuration or SDK construction can fail, express it in the Layer error channel and prove application startup handles it. Do not throw during import or constructor evaluation.
   214	
   215	Once a runtime is successfully built, public service operations may be closed over those dependencies.
   216	
   217	## Avoid over-layering
   218	
   219	Do not create:
   220	
   221	- a service for a pure stateless function;
   222	- a Layer that only wraps a static constant with no composition value;
   223	- one service per SDK method;
   224	- a separate Layer for every helper.
   225	
   226	Use services for substitutable capabilities, dependency boundaries, state/lifetime, provider isolation, or observability policy.
   227	
   228	For fixed host settings, yield checked Config in the Layer that uses them.
   229	`Layer.unwrap` can read settings and return existing Layers without inventing a
   230	new service. Follow the [configuration decision procedure](config-and-secrets.md#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
   231	to choose Config, a real Context service, request data or an already checked
   232	argument.
   233	
   234	## Tests
   235	
   236	Test:
   237	
   238	- contract through memory and controlled live adapter;
   239	- Layer builds with valid Config;
   240	- Layer fails with typed error for invalid Config/client construction;
   241	- public operation requirements are intentional;
   242	- provider client is not publicly exported;
   243	- dependencies are constructed once per intended scope.

    16	## Acquire configuration through Effect
    17	
    18	Use Config for values supplied by the host:
    19	
    20	- environment variables;
    21	- platform bindings;
    22	- file/config providers;
    23	- test configuration;
    24	- provider endpoints and safe IDs;
    25	- timeouts, retry counts, and feature policy.
    26	
    27	Do not read `process.env`, `Bun.env`, `import.meta.env`, or Cloudflare bindings throughout domain code.
    28	
    29	## Read settings in the owning Layer
    30	
    31	`Config` is already yieldable. A native Effect host can supply its
    32	`ConfigProvider`, and an owning Layer can read a checked value with
    33	`yield* Config.schema(OwnedSchema, "KEY")`. No separate Context service is
    34	needed just to make a setting available through `yield*`.
    35	
    36	For settings that stay fixed during the application's lifetime:
    37	
    38	1. Inspect the installed host's configuration support. Reuse its native
    39	   `ConfigProvider`; replacing it with `fromEnv` can lose platform bindings or
    40	   test values. If the host has none, use the root adapter described below.
    41	2. Reuse the Schema owned by that setting's domain. Check its format, allowed
    42	   values and bounds, and keep meaningful strings branded.
    43	3. Read the Config while building the Layer that uses it. Use
    44	   `Layer.effect(Service, effect)` to construct an existing service, or
    45	   `Layer.unwrap(effect)` when the result is a composition of existing Layers.
    46	   Reusable static Layers receive already checked caller inputs through named
    47	   Context requirements. Keep the configuration reader at the host edge.
    48	4. Close the service operations or route registrations over that checked value.
    49	   Build the application Layer once at startup, so each request uses the same
    50	   settings and does not rebuild clients or registrations.
    51	5. Let missing required values and invalid input fail Layer construction with
    52	   the native typed `ConfigError`, or map it to the owner's named startup error.
    53	   Report the key and a safe constraint; do not expose the value in diagnostics.
    54	
    55	For the qualified Effect `4.0.2` API, a route Layer can use this shape:
    56	
    57	```ts
    58	import * as Config from "effect/Config";
    59	import * as Effect from "effect/Effect";
    60	import * as Layer from "effect/Layer";
    61	import { ApiOrigin } from "./schemas";
    62	import { ApiIdentity, routes } from "./routes";
    63	
    64	export const ApiRoutes = Layer.unwrap(
    65	  Effect.gen(function* () {
    66	    const origin = yield* Config.schema(ApiOrigin, "API_ORIGIN");
    67	    return routes.pipe(Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(ApiIdentity, { origin })));
    68	  }),
    69	);
    70	```
    71	
    72	Here `ApiOrigin` is the existing branded address Schema. The static `routes`
    73	Layer requires `ApiIdentity`, whose value contains that checked origin. These
    74	imports stand for the receiving project's owners; reuse an existing requirement
    75	and Schema where available. Recheck APIs against installed types before
    76	using this example in another version.
    77	
    78	Apply the same steps to other settings:
    79	
    80	| Setting                                      | Check and ownership                                                                                                  |
    81	| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    82	| Public address or provider endpoint          | Check the allowed URL shape in the owning Layer before registering links or constructing the client.                 |
    83	| Stage or feature switch                      | Check the declared values before selecting the implementation; avoid silently treating an invalid value as disabled. |
    84	| Batch size, retry count or concurrency limit | Check integer bounds before building the queue, retry policy or semaphore.                                           |
    85	| Timeout                                      | Check supported units and positive bounds before closing operations over the timeout policy.                         |
    86	| Credential                                   | Acquire a redacted value in the private provider Layer and keep it out of public results and diagnostics.            |
    87	
    88	Provide test settings through the same route Layer:
    89	
    90	```ts
    91	import * as ConfigProvider from "effect/ConfigProvider";
    92	
    93	const TestRoutes = ApiRoutes.pipe(
    94	  Layer.provide(
    95	    ConfigProvider.layer(ConfigProvider.fromUnknown({ API_ORIGIN: "https://api.example.com" })),
    96	  ),
    97	);
    98	```
    99	
   100	This replaces the provider for that test without changing the process
   101	environment. Building the same Layer in a separate runtime gives that runtime
   102	its own settings; it is not a module-global snapshot.
   103	
   104	## Choose Config, Context or request data
   105	
   106	Choose by what the value does and how long it must live:
   107	
   108	| Need                                                                                                          | Use                                                                                               |
   109	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   110	| Host setting fixed for a Layer's lifetime                                                                     | Yield checked Config while constructing that Layer.                                               |
   111	| Named operations, managed state/resources, substitutable implementation or deliberately shared checked policy | A Context service built by its owning Layer.                                                      |
   112	| Settings that change while the application runs                                                               | A service or subscription with checked updates and an explicit consistency policy; see Reloading. |
   113	| Data belonging to the current HTTP request                                                                    | Yield the native request service inside the request handler and check the needed fields.          |
   114	| Already checked input supplied by a caller or helper                                                          | Use a named requirement for a static Layer; ordinary helpers keep typed arguments.                |
   115	
   116	Read fixed host settings through Config. Supply already checked caller values
   117	to static Layers through named Context requirements; this allows native Layer
   118	replacement in tests. Do not add another reader, forwarding factory or runtime.
   119	Ordinary helper arguments still express a deliberate caller choice. Browser code receives only checked public settings through the
   120	application's existing loader/runtime boundary; server secrets stay private.
   121	
   122	## Root host adapter
   123	
   124	If a platform cannot provide an Effect ConfigProvider directly:
   125	
   126	1. read the host environment at the application boundary;
   127	2. select only owned keys;
   128	3. construct a ConfigProvider or typed adapter;
   129	4. decode/refine values;
   130	5. provide it to the runtime;
   131	6. keep the raw environment object private.
   132	
   133	Check whether the installed host exposes a native adapter for its encoded
   134	bindings before writing a decoder for those bindings. For qualified Alchemy
   135	`2.0.0-beta.81`, `reifyBoundConfigProvider` from `alchemy/Runtime` unwraps its
   136	protected markers around a `ConfigProvider.fromUnknown` source. Native Effect
   137	Workers already supply it; a non-Effect host can reuse it in its private root
   138	adapter. Pass only the selected app keys to both the provider and the helper.
   139	Keep this translation out of domain Config declarations.
   140	
   141	Tests supply a deterministic provider rather than mutating ambient environment.
   142	
   143	## Refine primitive values
   144	
   145	Inspect the installed Schema and Config exports before choosing a codec. Start
   146	with the native data type and add the owner's checks and brand; do not write
   147	another URL, number, JSON, duration, UUID or secret parser.
   148	
   149	For qualified Effect `4.0.2`:
   150	
   151	| Input and needed value            | Native choice and required owner checks                                                                                                                                                                           |
   152	| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   153	| URL string to a URL value         | `Schema.URLFromString`, or `Schema.URL` through Config's native string codec. Check protocols, credentials and the allowed URL components, then brand the owned address.                                          |
   154	| String identifier or closed stage | The existing owning Schema, using native literals or a business format check and `Schema.brand`. Use `Schema.isUUID` for a UUID contract. A brand alone does not check the format.                                |
   155	| Port, count or finite measurement | `Schema.Int` or `Schema.Finite` with native range checks and the owning brand. Config converts its string source through the native codec; `Schema.NumberFromString` is also available for a string-only ingress. |
   156	| Boolean switch                    | `Config.Boolean`, which uses `Schema.BooleanLiterals`. Check its accepted spellings; use an explicit literal Schema if the host contract requires stricter input.                                                 |
   157	| Timeout or interval               | `Schema.DurationFromString`, or `Config.Duration`. Check positive, finite bounds appropriate to the operation before using the duration.                                                                          |
   158	| JSON settings                     | `Schema.fromJsonString(OwnedSchema)` inside `Config.schema`. Preserve the complete owning record and its checks.                                                                                                  |
   159	| Structured settings               | `Config.schema(OwnedSchema)` for a provider record; `Config.all` composes existing declarations without redefining their keys.                                                                                    |
   160	| Separated list or dictionary      | `Config.Array` or `Config.Record` with owning element/key/value Schemas and explicit separators when the source contract needs them.                                                                              |
   161	| Optional host input               | `Config.option` for missing settings. At other boundaries, select the matching native Schema Option codec for omitted, undefined or null input. Invalid input remains an error.                                   |
   162	| Private credential                | `Schema.RedactedFromValue(OwnedCredentialSchema)` through Config for a checked branded secret, or `Config.Redacted` when no stronger owner exists. Unwrap only at the private provider boundary.                  |
   163	
   164	Native URL decoding can normalise its source. Keep original-source checks when
   165	the contract requires an exact serialised browser origin. When a checked URL
   166	must become a distinct branded string such as its origin, construct that new
   167	value with the owning Schema's `makeEffect`. Map its `SchemaIssue.Issue` to the
   168	native `ConfigError` through `Config.mapEffect`; do not cast the string or
   169	replace the native URL parser.
   170	
   171	Use `Config.withDefault` or `Config.option` for missing input. They do not
   172	recover from invalid input or a partly supplied group. An optional feature can
   173	have a valid checked disabled setting; invalid configuration is still an error.
   174	Never wrap required stage, address or combined application settings in
   175	`Config.orElse(() => Config.succeed(disabledValue))`: this discards every
   176	`ConfigError`, including provider read failures, and can hide a broken deployment.
   177	Let the typed failure reach startup or the application's checked error result.
   178	If an explicitly accepted policy requires recovery for a particular optional
   179	setting, contain it in that declaration, document the exact recovered failures
   180	and retain a safe diagnostic. Keep checks relating two settings, such as
   181	matching a project's stage to its Worker, when composing declarations. Copying
   182	a record's fields does not copy its record checks.
   183	
   184	Map invalid configuration to a typed startup/config error with key name and
   185	safe constraint, never its value.
   186	
   187	Recheck these choices against the receiving installation. The qualified source
   188	is Effect's [Config](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691/packages/effect/src/Config.ts)
   189	and [Schema](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts),
   190	plus Alchemy's [runtime binding adapter](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy-async/blob/e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e/packages/alchemy/src/Runtime.ts).
   191	
   192	## Secrets
   193	
   194	Acquire secrets as Redacted values or the installed equivalent. Unwrap only inside the smallest provider request boundary.
   195	
   196	Rules:
   197	
   198	- never convert a secret to a normal string for convenience;
   199	- never include secret values in error fields;
   200	- never interpolate secrets into logs, spans, metrics, or receipts;
   201	- never place a secret in a service's public success type;
   202	- never persist it in test snapshots;
   203	- choose the narrowest supported native authentication method; do not require
   204	  OIDC when a config-scoped read-only service token meets the approved boundary.
   205	
   206	For Alchemy deployments backed by Doppler, follow the canonical
   207	[native sources and sign-in procedure](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/services-config-and-errors.md#native-doppler-and-dotenv-sources).
   208	Local and hosted runs both load Doppler, then optional ignored `.env`, with shell
   209	stack settings explicitly disabled. Keep native provider sign-in separate from
   210	the settings it unlocks. Read settings through checked Config in their owning
   211	Layer; do not add another secret reader or mutate the process environment.
   212	
   213	## Secret JSON bindings
   214	
   215	When a platform binding contains JSON:
   216	
   217	1. obtain it as redacted;
   218	2. expose/unredact only inside a boundary Effect;
   219	3. decode JSON using an owned Schema;
   220	4. construct a private credentials value;
   221	5. discard the plaintext as soon as possible;
   222	6. log only credential class and safe scope.
   223	
   224	Do not use unchecked `JSON.parse`.
   225	
   226	## Configuration ownership
   227	
   228	Keep domain Config near the live Layer that owns it. A shared application config module may compose domain Config values but should not become an untyped registry of every environment key.
   229	
   230	Export reusable declarations from the owner's `config.ts` beside its Schemas.
   231	The declaration combines the Schema and key, stays lazy until yielded, and can
   232	be reused by multiple Layers. Keep cross-domain composition with an owner that
   233	can depend on all participating domains without creating a package cycle.
   234	
   235	Related settings can share an owning record Schema and Config recipe. Group
   236	them because they belong to the same client or policy; reading several settings
   237	does not by itself require a new Context service.
   238	
   239	Expose an environment key when the host needs to choose a different value for
   240	a deployment. Keep supported protocol implementations and fixed input validity
   241	rules in code. An access policy can become checked Config when deployments need
   242	different access; that does not make malformed inputs valid.
   243	
   244	Name keys consistently and document:
   245	
   246	- owner;
   247	- environment/stage scope;
   248	- secret status;
   249	- default;
   250	- validation;
   251	- rotation/reload behaviour.
   252	
   253	Avoid defaults for Production-critical identity and credentials. Missing should fail at startup.
   254	
   255	## Reloading
   256	
   257	Most application identity/config should be immutable for a runtime. If dynamic reload is required:
   258	
   259	- model it as a service or subscription;
   260	- decode every new value;
   261	- define consistency and failure behaviour;
   262	- avoid partially updated configuration;
   263	- instrument safe version/change identity.
   264	
   265	Do not poll raw environment variables on each operation.
   266	
   267	## Tests
   268	
   269	Test:
   270	
   271	- valid Config construction;
   272	- missing required keys;
   273	- refinement failure;
   274	- default policy;
   275	- redaction in logs/errors/inspection;
   276	- test provider isolation;
   277	- stage-specific key separation;
   278	- no ambient environment dependence.
