    21	- fork/join when the parent needs the result;
    22	- scoped fork when the child must end with a Scope;
    23	- supervision for application-owned background work;
    24	- race/parallel combinators for bounded competing operations;
    25	- explicit daemon/background semantics only at an application boundary.
    26	
    27	Reject detached Promises and unowned fibres.
    28	
    29	## Concurrency limits
    30	
    31	Set concurrency deliberately:
    32	
    33	- serial for provider reconciliation where ordering/readback matters;
    34	- small fixed bound for rate-limited APIs;
    35	- inherited/default only when the application policy is known;
    36	- unbounded only with proof that input is bounded and work is safe.
    37	
    38	Do not translate `Promise.all` into unbounded Effect traversal.
    39	
    40	Define failure policy:
    41	
    42	- fail fast and interrupt siblings;
    43	- collect typed results;
    44	- retry individual elements;
    45	- continue with bounded error receipt.
    46	
    47	## Deferred
    48	
    49	Use Deferred for one-shot coordination:
    50	
    51	- wait for server readiness;
    52	- complete a shared initialisation result;
    53	- communicate first terminal outcome;
    54	- test a concurrent ordering point.
    55	
    56	Do not use polling plus sleep when an event can complete a Deferred.
    57	
    58	## Queue
    59	
    60	Use Queue for point-to-point work with backpressure. Define:
    61	
    62	- capacity;
    63	- bounded/sliding/dropping strategy;
    64	- offer/take interruption;
    65	- shutdown;
    66	- work acknowledgement/retry;
    67	- metrics.
    68	
    69	Do not use an array plus timer as a queue.
    70	
    71	## PubSub
    72	
    73	Use PubSub when multiple subscribers need the same events. Define replay expectations, subscriber lifetime, buffer policy, and slow-subscriber behaviour.
    74	
    75	Do not use PubSub for durable delivery unless backed by a durable transport with an explicit adapter.
    76	
    77	## Stream
    78	
    79	Use Stream for incremental, pull/push, or potentially unbounded values:
    80	
    81	- paginated APIs;
    82	- file/network body;
    83	- event source;
    84	- batched processing;
    85	- telemetry pipeline.
    86	
    87	Preserve:
    88	
    89	- chunking;
    90	- backpressure;
    91	- typed failure;
    92	- resource Scope;
    93	- interruption;
    94	- finalisation.
    95	
    96	Avoid collecting to an array unless the contract is bounded and the limit is enforced.
    97	
    98	## Streaming truth
    99	
   100	Prove streaming end to end:
   101	
   102	1. source emits before completion;
   103	2. adapter does not buffer the full source;
   104	3. transformations preserve incremental delivery;
   105	4. sink observes early chunks;
   106	5. interruption closes the source;
   107	6. memory remains bounded.
   108	
   109	A Stream return type alone is not proof.
   110	
   111	## Workers and request completion
   112	
   113	Background work in a Worker/server request must connect to host lifecycle. Use the platform adapter to attach completion and keep domain work as Effect. Do not fire-and-forget a Promise after returning the response.
   114	
   115	## Tests
   116	
   117	Use Deferred/TestClock/controlled Queues to prove:
   118	
   119	- ordering;
   120	- concurrency bound;
   121	- cancellation;
   122	- shutdown;
   123	- backpressure;
   124	- failure propagation;
   125	- no orphan fibres;
   126	- early stream delivery.
   127	
   128	Avoid wall-clock sleeps.

1	# React and TanStack
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [Keep render pure](#keep-render-pure)
     6	- [Server and client runtimes](#server-and-client-runtimes)
     7	- [Loaders and actions](#loaders-and-actions)
     8	- [TanStack Query](#tanstack-query)
     9	- [TanStack Router Start](#tanstack-routerstart)
    10	- [Initial JavaScript and fonts](#initial-javascript-and-fonts)
    11	- [React lifecycle](#react-lifecycle)
    12	- [State](#state)
    13	- [Errors](#errors)
    14	- [Tests](#tests)
    15	
    16	## Keep render pure
    17	
    18	React components should be total render functions over props, decoded loader/query state, and declared hooks. Do not:
    19	
    20	- run Effect during render;
    21	- construct live Layers during render;
    22	- access server Config/secrets;
    23	- call raw provider clients;
    24	- mutate global state;
    25	- create unmanaged Promise side effects.
    26	
    27	JSX and pure view transformations may remain plain TypeScript.
    28	
    29	## Server and client runtimes
    30	
    31	Keep separate composition:
    32	
    33	- server runtime: filesystem/database/provider/secrets;
    34	- client runtime: browser transport, client cache, browser-safe telemetry.
    35	
    36	Never serialise a service, Layer, Cause, Redacted value, or SDK object into hydration data.
    37	
    38	Use TanStack's matching server/client environment functions for runtime imports
    39	as well as the `*.server.ts` and `*.client.ts` filenames. Keep browser globals
    40	out of module initialisation and inspect the built browser dependency graph.
    41	
    42	For an Alchemy-hosted Website/API pair, keep TanStack as the frontend. All
    43	Website server entry points use one runner whose Layers contain typed API
    44	clients, not live backend implementations. A private Cloudflare service-binding
    45	adapter supplies its same-stage API; browser clients use a checked public URL.
    46	The native API owns HTTP/RPC/MCP handlers and executes them in its incoming
    47	Effect fibre without another runtime.
    48	
    49	Do not carry Effect Context through TanStack, merge event services into its
    50	runtime, borrow tracer hooks or add a custom backend Worker around Start.
    51	Preserve cancellation and body streams at the narrow host adapter. Native API
    52	telemetry and any qualified frontend host-span adapter have separate owners;
    53	see [hosted telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).
    54	
    55	## Loaders and actions
    56	
    57	Framework loaders/actions are host adapters:
    58	
    59	1. decode params/search/body/session;
    60	2. call a named Effect service operation;
    61	3. map tagged errors to redirect/not-found/protocol result;
    62	4. encode hydration-safe data;
    63	5. bridge to Promise only at the required callback.
    64	
    65	Keep retries, provider calls, and business policy inside Effect services.
    66	
    67	## TanStack Query
    68	
    69	Wrap query/mutation functions through one runtime bridge. The query key must use stable encoded domain identity.
    70	
    71	Define intentionally:
    72	
    73	- which layer owns retry: Query or Effect Schedule, not both accidentally;
    74	- cancellation: Query AbortSignal interrupts the Effect;
    75	- error shape: encoded domain/protocol error, not Cause;
    76	- cache staleness versus Effect Cache;
    77	- invalidation after mutation;
    78	- server prefetch/hydration encoding.
    79	
    80	Avoid returning `Effect.runPromise(program)` ad hoc from every component.
    81	
    82	## TanStack Router/Start
    83	
    84	Keep route definitions declarative. Route loaders decode and bridge to the server/client runtime appropriate to the execution environment.
    85	
    86	For serialisable loader data:
    87	
    88	- Schema encode before crossing server/client;
    89	- Schema decode on the receiving side if trust boundary requires;
    90	- represent expected recoverable states explicitly;
    91	- prove all error variants are handled.
    92	
    93	Do not depend on class prototype identity after hydration. Return a
    94	Schema-encoded success/error result for expected backend failures and decode it
    95	on the receiving side. Prove tags and useful fields survive the actual TanStack
    96	transport, including an error response status.
    97	
    98	### Router preloading and freshness
    99	
   100	Set link preloading and loader freshness in `createRouter`, not the Vite plugin.
   101	Check the receiving installation's defaults: TanStack retains unused loader
   102	data for five minutes by default, but ordinary `staleTime` is zero. A cached
   103	page can render immediately while a return starts another server-function
   104	request. Retention does not promise a period without requests.
   105	
   106	For public page data that can be reused briefly, the repository starter uses
   107	`defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
   108	`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000`. Intent preloads on link hover, focus or touch;
   109	the one-minute freshness window applies to both loaded and preloaded data.
   110	Choose route-specific freshness and invalidation for changing or personal data.
   111	Encoded error envelopes are also loader data; account for their retry and
   112	recovery behaviour rather than treating them as successful content.
   113	
   114	Router memory, browser HTTP caching, Cloudflare caching and Effect Cache are
   115	separate owners. A server-function reply marked `no-store` can still be held by
   116	the router. A full reload starts a new router cache. Prefetching moves the first
   117	request before the click; freshness controls repeat reads. Analytics requests
   118	and a route's first JavaScript download are separate from page-data refreshes.
   119	
   120	Prove the behaviour in a real browser: hover before opening a page, return to a
   121	visited page within its freshness window, then return after expiry. Inspect the
   122	page-data requests separately from assets and analytics. A build does not prove
   123	these interactions. See TanStack's official [data loading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/data-loading)
   124	and [preloading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/preloading) guides;
   125	reconcile their current descriptions with installed source and types.
   126	
   127	## Initial JavaScript and fonts
   128	
   129	Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
   130	plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
   131	installation. Router-only applications need their matching bundler's automatic
   132	splitting setting. Keep optional implementations out of the root route and
   133	other modules imported by every page. A separate file or lazy service acquisition
   134	does not remove a static import from the initial download. Use the framework's
   135	normal splitting and keep necessary matching and loader code readily available.
   136	
   137	Import important font assets through Vite's `?url` handling and declare ordinary
   138	font preload links in the owning route's `head` result. Render `HeadContent` so
   139	the browser sees those links in the initial HTML. For WOFF2 use `rel: "preload"`,
   140	`as: "font"`, `type: "font/woff2"` and `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`. The preload and
   141	stylesheet must resolve to the same asset. Preload only the styles and character
   142	sets used by visible opening content; every extra preload competes with it.
   143	Keep the chosen `font-display` policy explicit.
   144	
   145	For owned conditional head data, prefer a checked Schema constructor with fixed
   146	tags, `Option` and `Array.fromOption`, and immutable `Array` or `Struct` operations.
   147	Do not spread a ternary array of repeated font objects into every route.
   148	Trusted Vite asset URLs need no runtime environment reader or browser global.
   149	
   150	Measure compressed transfer bytes separately from expanded JavaScript size,
   151	fonts and styles. Record Lighthouse's network, CPU and cache settings, and retain
   152	repeated results when scores vary. A smaller download alone does not prove that
   153	visible content appears sooner. Prove the emitted HTML, browser font requests
   154	and route navigation separately from local checks. See the official
   155	[code splitting](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/code-splitting),
   156	[head management](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/document-head-management)
   157	and [Vite asset](https://vite.dev/guide/assets) guides, then check installed behaviour.
   158	
   159	## React lifecycle
   160	
   161	For subscriptions/streams:
   162	
   163	- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
   164	- scope to mount/route lifetime;
   165	- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
   166	- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
   167	- encode backpressure/sampling;
   168	- update view state through a controlled adapter.
   169	
   170	Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.
   171	
   172	When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
   173	An optional registration/subscription pattern is
   174	`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
   175	under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
   176	interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
   177	counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
   178	extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
   179	not required for purely synchronous local UI state.
   180	
   181	Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
   182	local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
   183	and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
   184	tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
   185	register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
   186	than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
   187	not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
   188	state or cleanup has a real owner.
   189	
   190	Declare service Layers as static values and supply their checked requirements
   191	at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
   192	Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
   193	operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
   194	registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
   195	operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
   196	mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
   197	one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
   198	its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
   199	Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.
   200	
   201	Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
   202	action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
   203	name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
   204	cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.
   205	
   206	## State
   207	
   208	Keep domain state in Effect services when it is shared, concurrent, or effectful. Keep local ephemeral UI state in React when it is truly view-local and synchronous.
   209	
   210	Do not move every `useState` into Effect. Do move provider/cache/concurrent workflows out of component-local mutable logic.
   211	
   212	## Errors
   213	
   214	Translate domain errors to a closed UI state:
   215	
   216	- not found;
   217	- unauthorised;
   218	- validation fields;
   219	- unavailable/retry;
   220	- conflict;
   221	- unexpected defect boundary.
   222	
   223	Never render raw provider messages, stack traces, or Causes.
   224	
   225	## Tests
   226	
   227	Test:
   228	
   229	- domain service independently;
   230	- loader/action decoding and encoding;
   231	- runtime bridge and cancellation;
   232	- hydration round-trip;
   233	- retry ownership;
   234	- subscription cleanup;
   235	- no server dependency in client bundle;
   236	- independent optional service acquisition and root/mount cleanup, including
   237	  a stalled unrelated service;
   238	- exhaustive UI error states.
     1	# HTTP, RPC, and Serialisation
     2	
     3	## Outbound HTTP
     4	
     5	Use Effect Platform HttpClient or a private provider adapter.
     6	
     7	For each operation:
     8	
     9	1. construct path/query/header/body from branded domain input;
    10	2. encode body with Schema;
    11	3. keep credentials redacted until the request boundary;
    12	4. set one timeout for headers and complete body decoding, plus redirect policy;
    13	5. classify transport/status failures;
    14	6. decode response body with Schema;
    15	7. scope streaming bodies;
    16	8. add span and safe attributes.
    17	
    18	Do not use global `fetch` in domain code. If a host supplies fetch, provide it as the platform HttpClient Layer.
    19	
    20	## Status handling
    21	
    22	Map status/code to a closed domain vocabulary. Do not accept every 2xx response without decoding. Do not turn every non-2xx into one string error.
    23	
    24	Handle redirects intentionally:
    25	
    26	- follow when the operation contract permits;
    27	- inspect manually for redirect proof/auth flows;
    28	- reject unexpected cross-origin redirects;
    29	- never log sensitive Location query values.
    30	
    31	## Inbound HTTP
    32	
    33	At the route boundary:
    34	
    35	- decode path, query, headers, cookies, and body;
    36	- enforce size limits;
    37	- construct a named domain operation;
    38	- map tagged errors exhaustively to protocol errors;
    39	- encode response through Schema;
    40	- set headers/cookies through typed protocol facilities;
    41	- execute in the incoming native Effect request fibre when the host supplies one;
    42	- otherwise bridge only at the application-owned host runner.
    43	
    44	Do not pass a raw Request into the domain service.
    45	
    46	For a native Alchemy HTTP host, keep its HttpEffect contract and let the host
    47	adapt routing failures, defects and cancellation. Do not replace all failures
    48	with 500: a missing route must still return 404. Test the native host adaptation
    49	and select safe ErrorReporter fields separately from the response mapping.
    50	
    51	## RPC
    52	
    53	Define RPC procedures from shared Schemas and tagged serialisable errors. Keep transport details out of the domain service.
    54	
    55	Require:
    56	
    57	- request/response Schema;
    58	- error Schema;
    59	- authentication/authorisation boundary;
    60	- deadline/cancellation propagation;
    61	- versioning;
    62	- payload limits;
    63	- observability safe fields.
    64	
    65	Do not expose arbitrary Effect Causes or unencoded class instances over RPC.
    66	Declared Schema-tagged errors are encoded on the wire and decoded by clients.
    67	
    68	## Shared client contract
    69	
    70	Keep native generated clients private to semantic client Layers. HTTP and RPC
    71	clients implement the same domain service contract as the backend. Decode
    72	expected backend failures with the shared Schema and map connection or invalid
    73	reply failures to distinct named domain-access errors. No protocol error or
    74	unchecked provider payload leaks into UI policy.
    75	
    76	Test syntactically valid replies with the wrong payload Schema, as well as
    77	broken JSON. In the qualified 4.0.2, native RPC reply decoding can produce a
    78	SchemaError defect. The private client marks failure inside only the native
    79	exit reply codec's decoder, before native RPC converts that failure to a
    80	defect. Its semantic operation translates only that private marker to the named
    81	invalid-response error. Keep the native Schemas, Ndjson parser, Protocol and
    82	client; do not replace them with a handwritten protocol.
    83	
    84	Never infer reply failure from the SchemaError class alone. An unrelated
    85	transport or request encoder can fail with that same class and must keep its
    86	original defect identity. Test both reads with bad native replies and an
    87	unrelated adapter SchemaError. Preserve caller interruption and other defects;
    88	do not turn every Cause into an expected failure. Requalify the cached native
    89	exit Schema identity and reply decoder behaviour on Effect upgrades before
    90	retaining or removing this compatibility handling.
    91	
    92	For public, unauthenticated browser reads, omit credentials and reject redirects
    93	so a checked API address cannot silently send the browser somewhere else.
    94	Supply native Fetch RequestInit policy when the operation executes, not only
    95	while constructing its Layer. Protected clients need their own explicit policy.
    96	
    97	A selecting field can identify a response union. Native generation alone does
    98	not give a dependent return type: check the selected response Schema before
    99	narrowing literal/default inputs. See the [format-selected example](../examples/format-selected-client.md).
   100	
   101	For browser clients, test CORS preflight with the actual native request headers.
   102	In the qualified Effect version this includes b3 and traceparent. A successful
   103	server request is not browser-access proof. Remote MCP and Website WebMCP have
   104	separate Origin policies; do not inherit one policy from the other.
   105	
   106	## Serialisation
   107	
   108	Values crossing a process/runtime/hydration boundary must be encoded.
   109	
   110	Watch:
   111	
   112	- Dates/instants;
   113	- Option/Result;
   114	- branded values;
   115	- big integers;
   116	- Maps/Sets/Chunks;
   117	- tagged errors;
   118	- URLs;
   119	- Redacted;
   120	- binary data;
   121	- cyclic values.
   122	
   123	Never assume JSON.stringify preserves domain semantics. Use Schema transformations and a versioned envelope.
   124	
   125	## Streaming HTTP/RPC
   126	
   127	Use Stream for actual incremental bodies/messages. Scope the response body and propagate cancellation. Define framing, maximum frame size, decode failure, heartbeat, and reconnection.
   128	
   129	Do not buffer a full stream into text/JSON and still claim streaming.
   130	
   131	## Testing
   132	
   133	Provide controlled HttpClient/fetch Layers. Assert:
   134	
   135	- encoded request;
   136	- secret header redaction;
   137	- redirect policy;
   138	- status/error mapping;
   139	- invalid JSON/body;
   140	- whole-read deadline before headers and while decoding a stalled body;
   141	- earlier caller interruption and request/body finalisation;
   142	- retry policy;
   143	- serialisation round-trip;
   144	- no live network in unit tests.
     1	# State, Collections, and Caches
     2	
     3	## State selection
     4	
     5	Choose the narrowest primitive:
     6	
     7	- immutable local value for pure transformation;
     8	- `Ref` for atomic synchronous Effect-managed state;
     9	- synchronised/ref variant when updates require effects;
    10	- subscription ref for observable current state;
    11	- `TxRef` inside `Effect.tx` for coordinated changes to several values;
    12	- Queue/PubSub for communication rather than shared mutable state;
    13	- Cache for keyed effectful memoisation with policy;
    14	- scoped resource for state tied to a lifetime.
    15	
    16	Inspect installed Effect exports; names and modules can change across versions.
    17	
    18	## No mutable globals
    19	
    20	Reject module-level mutable objects, arrays, Maps, Sets, clients, counters, or caches in shared packages.
    21	
    22	Application-level state belongs in a Layer so:
    23	
    24	- construction is explicit;
    25	- lifetime is scoped;
    26	- tests can substitute it;
    27	- concurrent access policy is visible;
    28	- shutdown can clear resources.
    29	
    30	## Ref
    31	
    32	Use Ref for small atomic state such as:
    33	
    34	- last safe provider cursor;
    35	- in-memory test inventory;
    36	- bounded operation observations;
    37	- feature state;
    38	- counters where Metric is not the right semantic store.
    39	
    40	Keep updates pure and atomic. Return a new readonly value using immutable collection functions; do not mutate the old value or use transient collection modes. Do not read-modify-write using separate operations when lost updates matter. Pure folds need no Ref. Effects inside an update need the installed synchronised or transactional primitive and its tested interruption policy.
    41	
    42	## Transactions
    43	
    44	The qualified Effect 4.0.2 uses `Effect.tx` with `TxRef` and the other
    45	transactional collections, such as `TxQueue`. Use them when several values must
    46	change together, or an operation must wait until transactional state changes.
    47	The outermost `Effect.tx` commits all changes together on success and discards
    48	them on failure. Nested transactions share that boundary. `Effect.txRetry`
    49	waits for a value read by the transaction to change, then retries the transaction.
    50	
    51	```ts
    52	import { Effect, TxRef } from "effect";
    53	
    54	const incrementTogether = Effect.gen(function* () {
    55	  const left = yield* TxRef.make(0);
    56	  const right = yield* TxRef.make(0);
    57	  yield* Effect.tx(
    58	    Effect.gen(function* () {
    59	      yield* TxRef.update(left, (value) => value + 1);
    60	      yield* TxRef.update(right, (value) => value + 1);
    61	    }),
    62	  );
    63	  return { left: yield* TxRef.get(left), right: yield* TxRef.get(right) };
    64	});
    65	```
    66	
    67	Keep external writes outside the transaction. Retrying a transaction can repeat
    68	its program; network calls and file writes are not rolled back with `TxRef`
    69	changes. Test both successful coordinated changes and failure rollback.
    70	
    71	Examples:
    72	
    73	- reserve capacity and enqueue work together;
    74	- move an item between two collections;
    75	- update resource inventory plus index;
    76	- coordinate a bounded pool.
    77	
    78	Do not introduce a transaction for a single simple value.
    79	
    80	## Domain collections
    81	
    82	Use immutable Effect collections for domain state where they express equality, hashing, ordering, and persistent updates. Use ReadonlyArray for bounded ordered serialisable values.
    83	
    84	Native Map/Set may remain:
    85	
    86	- within a private performance-critical implementation;
    87	- when a host API requires them;
    88	- never solely because the code is a total leaf or the mutation is local.
    89	
    90	Document and test the containment. Never expose a mutable reference.
    91	
    92	## Cache
    93	
    94	Define:
    95	
    96	- key Schema/brand;
    97	- lookup Effect and error;
    98	- capacity;
    99	- expiry using Effect time;
   100	- invalidation;
   101	- concurrent miss behaviour;
   102	- negative-cache policy;
   103	- observability;
   104	- scope/shutdown.
   105	
   106	Do not use a plain global Map as a cache. Do not cache secrets, provider errors, or unbounded payloads without explicit policy.
   107	
   108	## Context-local state
   109	
   110	Use Effect context/fibre-local facilities for request correlation or scoped annotations when supported by the installed version. Do not use ambient global variables for request identity.
   111	
   112	## Tests
   113	
   114	Test:
   115	
   116	- atomic concurrent updates;
   117	- scoped isolation;
   118	- cache hit/miss/expiry with TestClock;
   119	- invalidation;
   120	- bounded capacity;
   121	- failure caching policy;
   122	- no state leakage between test Layers;
   123	- immutable collection behaviour.
   124	
   125	## Structured keys and shared cancellation
   126	
   127	A key includes every part of the saved address: for example record ID, version,
   128	revision and preparation hash. Infer it from one owning Struct using existing
   129	branded fields. Pass that readonly record directly to the cache. Internal cache
   130	keys and values need no JSON encode/decode. Serialisation belongs only to a real
   131	persistence or message boundary.
   132	
   133	Research installed Equal, Hash, Cache and ScopedCache source before changing
   134	keys or resource ownership. Qualified v4 plain records use structural equality
   135	and hashing; prove separately reconstructed equivalent keys share one lookup
   136	and changing each address field creates a distinct lookup. Do not mutate a key
   137	after insertion or use Effect Hash as a cryptographic source hash.
   138	
   139	For a scoped shared lookup, keep the existing capacity, success/failure expiry,
   140	deadline and acquisition/finaliser contract. Test that cancelling one of two
   141	readers keeps the lookup alive, the last reader cancels it, and cancellation
   142	waits for underlying cleanup. Requalify these behaviours on a version change;
   143	matching names in an older clone do not prove the installed cancellation rules.
     1	# Logging, Tracing, and Metrics
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [One observability design](#one-observability-design)
     6	- [Structured logging](#structured-logging)
     7	- [Log levels](#log-levels)
     8	- [Tracing](#tracing)
     9	- [Metrics](#metrics)
    10	- [Resource identity](#resource-identity)
    11	- [Exporter Layers](#exporter-layers)
    12	- [Failure policy](#failure-policy)
    13	- [Proof](#proof)
    14	- [Alchemy](#alchemy)
    15	
    16	## One observability design
    17	
    18	Treat logs, traces, and metrics as part of the service contract:
    19	
    20	- what semantic operation is visible;
    21	- what identity connects signals;
    22	- which fields are safe;
    23	- what cardinality is bounded;
    24	- how exporters attach to the runtime;
    25	- how ingestion is proved.
    26	
    27	Do not scatter `console.log` and later wrap it with a logger.
    28	
    29	## Structured logging
    30	
    31	Use Effect logging and annotations. Prefer an event name plus typed safe fields:
    32	
    33	- service/operation;
    34	- environment/stage;
    35	- resource/domain safe ID;
    36	- outcome/error tag;
    37	- attempt;
    38	- duration;
    39	- bounded count;
    40	- source revision where useful.
    41	
    42	Avoid:
    43	
    44	- string-concatenated blobs;
    45	- full objects;
    46	- raw Errors/Causes;
    47	- headers/cookies;
    48	- provider responses;
    49	- credentials;
    50	- user content unless explicitly governed;
    51	- high-volume per-item logging.
    52	
    53	Define a safe error-to-fields function for each error union.
    54	
    55	Native Alchemy beta.81 HTTP handling logs the raw Cause when no ErrorReporter
    56	is visible to its failure mapper. A reporter provided only inside the route
    57	does not reach that outer catch. At the API host boundary, qualify native
    58	`Http.safeHttpEffect` around the handler and provide its checked reporter set
    59	to that mapper with `Effect.provideService`. Build the reporter Layer once;
    60	capture only `ErrorReporter.CurrentErrorReporters`, never the initialisation
    61	Scope, logger or tracer. Avoid a new scoped Layer around each returned response.
    62	
    63	Effect 4.0.2 requires a synchronous ErrorReporter callback. Keep this narrow
    64	host exception explicit beside the callback. It may call the current native
    65	loggers with fixed bounded fields, an empty Cause and the host-supplied fibre
    66	and timestamp; it must ignore original error text, Causes, attributes and
    67	provider payloads. Add no console call, ambient clock or extra runner. Test the
    68	real handler with secret-like sentinels and original metadata, preserve native
    69	404/499/503/500 handling, and prove the incoming request Scope is retained and
    70	released. Requalify the native mapper and callback on Effect/Alchemy upgrades.
    71	
    72	## Log levels
    73	
    74	Use consistent semantics:
    75	
    76	- debug/trace: bounded development diagnostics;
    77	- info: lifecycle or meaningful state transition;
    78	- warning: recovered degradation or operator attention;
    79	- error: terminal operation failure;
    80	- fatal: application/runtime cannot continue.
    81	
    82	Do not log expected not-found/validation at error by default.
    83	
    84	## Tracing
    85	
    86	Create spans around:
    87	
    88	- domain service operation;
    89	- external provider/HTTP/database call;
    90	- queue/message handling;
    91	- infrastructure plan/apply/readback;
    92	- meaningful stream stage.
    93	
    94	Do not instrument every pure helper or Layer constructor.
    95	
    96	Use stable span names. Attach safe low-cardinality operation attributes and high-cardinality identifiers only when trace backends and privacy policy permit them.
    97	
    98	Public service methods use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`; private
    99	Effect helpers normally use `Effect.fnUntraced` and stay within the caller's
   100	span. A private external operation can own a separate named span. Keep pure
   101	helpers plain and avoid extracting one-use helpers just to decorate them.
   102	For contracts exposing an Effect value rather than a method, use the operation's
   103	named `Effect.withSpan` without changing the public API into a fake method.
   104	
   105	Propagate context across supported HTTP/RPC/queue boundaries. Do not leak it into untrusted channels without validation.
   106	
   107	## Metrics
   108	
   109	Use:
   110	
   111	- counters for occurrences;
   112	- histograms/timers for distributions;
   113	- gauges for current bounded state;
   114	- frequency/category metrics only with closed values.
   115	
   116	Good labels:
   117	
   118	- operation from a closed set;
   119	- result tag;
   120	- provider kind;
   121	- environment;
   122	- service.
   123	
   124	Bad labels:
   125	
   126	- user/resource/request ID;
   127	- full URL;
   128	- error message;
   129	- revision on every metric;
   130	- arbitrary stage/branch without a bounded policy.
   131	
   132	## Resource identity
   133	
   134	Attach runtime resource attributes such as:
   135	
   136	- service name;
   137	- service version/source revision;
   138	- deployment environment;
   139	- deployment stage;
   140	- repository/application identity.
   141	
   142	Keep request-level identity out of resource attributes.
   143	
   144	If shared Axiom datasets are used, ensure logs/spans carry enough identity for stage/service/revision proof. Keep metric labels low-cardinality and use logs/traces for revision-level proof.
   145	
   146	## Exporter Layers
   147	
   148	Register logger/tracer/meter/exporter configuration at its owning application
   149	boundary. Build resources for the lifetime their host actually supports:
   150	
   151	- acquire endpoint/token through Config/Redacted;
   152	- select transport and batching;
   153	- scope exporter lifetime;
   154	- flush on shutdown/host completion;
   155	- avoid multiple duplicate exporters;
   156	- separate server and browser policy;
   157	- separate application and platform telemetry.
   158	
   159	Long-lived servers can build exporters once and flush at graceful shutdown.
   160	Cloudflare's per-event exporters and metric registries belong to each event,
   161	not a process-global batch created by an earlier request. Native Alchemy registers
   162	the configuration once, then builds exporters into each event's Scope.
   163	
   164	First consider platform-managed delivery. On Cloudflare, Effect's structured
   165	console logger can feed Workers logs, with Alchemy-owned ObservabilityDestination
   166	resources delivering logs and native traces to Axiom. This removes the application
   167	exporter and its flush Scope/`waitUntil` adapter. Use native `Cloudflare.Telemetry()`
   168	for Effect Worker traces; do not pretend framework Websites receive its services.
   169	Use automatic platform tracing for a standard framework Website rather than
   170	recreating Alchemy's tracer or adding manual span lifecycle wrappers. Keep normal
   171	host imports and request-time binding reads inside the private live adapter,
   172	separate from host-independent operations tested with Effect Layers. Custom spans need a specific unmet diagnostic requirement.
   173	Cloudflare currently exports logs and traces, not custom metrics. Request-log
   174	counts can replace custom counters when the product accepts their coverage and
   175	best-effort limits. Remove direct OTLP bindings at cutover, explicitly configure
   176	both hosts, and qualify the actual stored log shape and dashboard queries.
   177	
   178	Only when application-managed export is required: an ordinary Effect Scope waits
   179	for finalisers, so keep its cleanup outside response delivery. Native Alchemy owns
   180	this lifecycle. A framework may hand a separate monitoring Scope's bounded closure
   181	to host completion through its existing runtime and private Promise adapter.
   182	Avoid coordination handshakes, borrowed contexts, detached fibres and extra
   183	runtimes. Preserve response streams and never fall back to blocking on upload.
   184	
   185	Required business work and durable audit records have a separate delivery
   186	contract. This policy does not let a command abandon its final flush or a
   187	long-lived server skip graceful shutdown. Follow the Alchemy
   188	[hosted web telemetry owner](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md)
   189	for the native Worker and framework Website adaptations.
   190	
   191	## Failure policy
   192	
   193	Decide whether telemetry failure:
   194	
   195	- is best-effort and annotated;
   196	- degrades a feature;
   197	- blocks startup because auditability is required.
   198	
   199	Avoid recursive logging loops when the exporter fails. Never expose secrets in exporter errors.
   200	
   201	## Proof
   202	
   203	Test locally:
   204	
   205	- Layer composition;
   206	- log field safety;
   207	- span structure;
   208	- metric label bounds;
   209	- exporter request formation.
   210	- response release while uploads remain pending;
   211	- bounded cleanup, failure and cancellation independently of response streaming.
   212	
   213	For a live ingestion claim:
   214	
   215	1. emit a unique bounded proof signal;
   216	2. allow the documented ingestion delay;
   217	3. query the backend by service/environment/stage and proof identity;
   218	4. verify signal fields;
   219	5. record only safe counts/IDs/time window.
   220	
   221	An exporter HTTP success is not query proof.
   222	
   223	## Alchemy
   224	
   225	Infrastructure Effects use the same policy:
   226	
   227	- span plan/apply/readback, not pure declarations;
   228	- annotate stack/stage/resource/change class;
   229	- never log state or credentials;
   230	- use metrics for bounded operation outcomes;
   231	- keep durable receipts separate from telemetry;
   232	- query configured Axiom datasets independently after deployment.

    15	
    16	## Keep render pure
    17	
    18	React components should be total render functions over props, decoded loader/query state, and declared hooks. Do not:
    19	
    20	- run Effect during render;
    21	- construct live Layers during render;
    22	- access server Config/secrets;
    23	- call raw provider clients;
    24	- mutate global state;
    25	- create unmanaged Promise side effects.
    26	
    27	JSX and pure view transformations may remain plain TypeScript.
    28	
    29	## Server and client runtimes
    30	
    31	Keep separate composition:
    32	
    33	- server runtime: filesystem/database/provider/secrets;
    34	- client runtime: browser transport, client cache, browser-safe telemetry.
    35	
    36	Never serialise a service, Layer, Cause, Redacted value, or SDK object into hydration data.
    37	
    38	Use TanStack's matching server/client environment functions for runtime imports
    39	as well as the `*.server.ts` and `*.client.ts` filenames. Keep browser globals
    40	out of module initialisation and inspect the built browser dependency graph.
    41	
    42	For an Alchemy-hosted Website/API pair, keep TanStack as the frontend. All
    43	Website server entry points use one runner whose Layers contain typed API
    44	clients, not live backend implementations. A private Cloudflare service-binding
    45	adapter supplies its same-stage API; browser clients use a checked public URL.
    46	The native API owns HTTP/RPC/MCP handlers and executes them in its incoming
    47	Effect fibre without another runtime.
    48	
    49	Do not carry Effect Context through TanStack, merge event services into its
    50	runtime, borrow tracer hooks or add a custom backend Worker around Start.
    51	Preserve cancellation and body streams at the narrow host adapter. Native API
    52	telemetry and any qualified frontend host-span adapter have separate owners;
    53	see [hosted telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).
    54	
    55	## Loaders and actions
    56	
    57	Framework loaders/actions are host adapters:
    58	
    59	1. decode params/search/body/session;
    60	2. call a named Effect service operation;
    61	3. map tagged errors to redirect/not-found/protocol result;
    62	4. encode hydration-safe data;
    63	5. bridge to Promise only at the required callback.
    64	
    65	Keep retries, provider calls, and business policy inside Effect services.
    66	
    67	## TanStack Query
    68	
    69	Wrap query/mutation functions through one runtime bridge. The query key must use stable encoded domain identity.
    70	
    71	Define intentionally:
    72	
    73	- which layer owns retry: Query or Effect Schedule, not both accidentally;
    74	- cancellation: Query AbortSignal interrupts the Effect;
    75	- error shape: encoded domain/protocol error, not Cause;
    76	- cache staleness versus Effect Cache;
    77	- invalidation after mutation;
    78	- server prefetch/hydration encoding.
    79	
    80	Avoid returning `Effect.runPromise(program)` ad hoc from every component.
    81	
    82	## TanStack Router/Start
    83	
    84	Keep route definitions declarative. Route loaders decode and bridge to the server/client runtime appropriate to the execution environment.
    85	
    86	For serialisable loader data:
    87	
    88	- Schema encode before crossing server/client;
    89	- Schema decode on the receiving side if trust boundary requires;
    90	- represent expected recoverable states explicitly;
    91	- prove all error variants are handled.
    92	
    93	Do not depend on class prototype identity after hydration. Return a
    94	Schema-encoded success/error result for expected backend failures and decode it
    95	on the receiving side. Prove tags and useful fields survive the actual TanStack
    96	transport, including an error response status.
    97	
    98	### Router preloading and freshness
    99	
   100	Set link preloading and loader freshness in `createRouter`, not the Vite plugin.
   101	Check the receiving installation's defaults: TanStack retains unused loader
   102	data for five minutes by default, but ordinary `staleTime` is zero. A cached
   103	page can render immediately while a return starts another server-function
   104	request. Retention does not promise a period without requests.
   105	
   106	For public page data that can be reused briefly, the repository starter uses
   107	`defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
   108	`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000`. Intent preloads on link hover, focus or touch;
   109	the one-minute freshness window applies to both loaded and preloaded data.
   110	Choose route-specific freshness and invalidation for changing or personal data.
   111	Encoded error envelopes are also loader data; account for their retry and
   112	recovery behaviour rather than treating them as successful content.
   113	
   114	Router memory, browser HTTP caching, Cloudflare caching and Effect Cache are
   115	separate owners. A server-function reply marked `no-store` can still be held by
   116	the router. A full reload starts a new router cache. Prefetching moves the first
   117	request before the click; freshness controls repeat reads. Analytics requests
   118	and a route's first JavaScript download are separate from page-data refreshes.
   119	
   120	Prove the behaviour in a real browser: hover before opening a page, return to a
   121	visited page within its freshness window, then return after expiry. Inspect the
   122	page-data requests separately from assets and analytics. A build does not prove
   123	these interactions. See TanStack's official [data loading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/data-loading)
   124	and [preloading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/preloading) guides;
   125	reconcile their current descriptions with installed source and types.
   126	
   127	## Initial JavaScript and fonts
   128	
   129	Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
   130	plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
   131	installation. Router-only applications need their matching bundler's automatic
   132	splitting setting. Keep optional implementations out of the root route and
   133	other modules imported by every page. A separate file or lazy service acquisition
   134	does not remove a static import from the initial download. Use the framework's
   135	normal splitting and keep necessary matching and loader code readily available.
   136	
   137	Import important font assets through Vite's `?url` handling and declare ordinary
   138	font preload links in the owning route's `head` result. Render `HeadContent` so
   139	the browser sees those links in the initial HTML. For WOFF2 use `rel: "preload"`,
   140	`as: "font"`, `type: "font/woff2"` and `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`. The preload and
   141	stylesheet must resolve to the same asset. Preload only the styles and character
   142	sets used by visible opening content; every extra preload competes with it.
   143	Keep the chosen `font-display` policy explicit.
   144	
   145	For owned conditional head data, prefer a checked Schema constructor with fixed
   146	tags, `Option` and `Array.fromOption`, and immutable `Array` or `Struct` operations.
   147	Do not spread a ternary array of repeated font objects into every route.
   148	Trusted Vite asset URLs need no runtime environment reader or browser global.
   149	
   150	Measure compressed transfer bytes separately from expanded JavaScript size,
   151	fonts and styles. Record Lighthouse's network, CPU and cache settings, and retain
   152	repeated results when scores vary. A smaller download alone does not prove that
   153	visible content appears sooner. Prove the emitted HTML, browser font requests
   154	and route navigation separately from local checks. See the official
   155	[code splitting](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/code-splitting),
   156	[head management](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/document-head-management)
   157	and [Vite asset](https://vite.dev/guide/assets) guides, then check installed behaviour.
   158	
   159	## React lifecycle
   160	
   161	For subscriptions/streams:
   162	
   163	- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
   164	- scope to mount/route lifetime;
   165	- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
   166	- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
   167	- encode backpressure/sampling;
   168	- update view state through a controlled adapter.
   169	
   170	Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.
   171	
   172	When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
   173	An optional registration/subscription pattern is
   174	`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
   175	under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
   176	interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
   177	counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
   178	extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
   179	not required for purely synchronous local UI state.
   180	
   181	Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
   182	local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
   183	and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
   184	tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
   185	register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
   186	than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
   187	not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
   188	state or cleanup has a real owner.
   189	
   190	Declare service Layers as static values and supply their checked requirements
   191	at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
   192	Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
   193	operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
   194	registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
   195	operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
   196	mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
   197	one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
   198	its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
   199	Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.
   200	
   201	Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
   202	action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
   203	name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
   204	cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.
   205	
   206	## State
   207	
   208	Keep domain state in Effect services when it is shared, concurrent, or effectful. Keep local ephemeral UI state in React when it is truly view-local and synchronous.
   209	
   210	Do not move every `useState` into Effect. Do move provider/cache/concurrent workflows out of component-local mutable logic.
   211	
   212	## Errors
   213	
   214	Translate domain errors to a closed UI state:
   215	
   216	- not found;
   217	- unauthorised;
   218	- validation fields;
   219	- unavailable/retry;
   220	- conflict;
   221	- unexpected defect boundary.
   222	
   223	Never render raw provider messages, stack traces, or Causes.
   224	
   225	## Tests
   226	
   227	Test:
   228	
   229	- domain service independently;
   230	- loader/action decoding and encoding;
   231	- runtime bridge and cancellation;
   232	- hydration round-trip;
   233	- retry ownership;
   234	- subscription cleanup;
   235	- no server dependency in client bundle;
   236	- independent optional service acquisition and root/mount cleanup, including
   237	  a stalled unrelated service;
   238	- exhaustive UI error states.
     1	# HTTP, RPC, and Serialisation
     2	
     3	## Outbound HTTP
     4	
     5	Use Effect Platform HttpClient or a private provider adapter.
     6	
     7	For each operation:
     8	
     9	1. construct path/query/header/body from branded domain input;
    10	2. encode body with Schema;
    11	3. keep credentials redacted until the request boundary;
    12	4. set one timeout for headers and complete body decoding, plus redirect policy;
    13	5. classify transport/status failures;
    14	6. decode response body with Schema;
    15	7. scope streaming bodies;
    16	8. add span and safe attributes.
    17	
    18	Do not use global `fetch` in domain code. If a host supplies fetch, provide it as the platform HttpClient Layer.
    19	
    20	## Status handling
    21	
    22	Map status/code to a closed domain vocabulary. Do not accept every 2xx response without decoding. Do not turn every non-2xx into one string error.
    23	
    24	Handle redirects intentionally:
    25	
    26	- follow when the operation contract permits;
    27	- inspect manually for redirect proof/auth flows;
    28	- reject unexpected cross-origin redirects;
    29	- never log sensitive Location query values.
    30	
    31	## Inbound HTTP
    32	
    33	At the route boundary:
    34	
    35	- decode path, query, headers, cookies, and body;
    36	- enforce size limits;
    37	- construct a named domain operation;
    38	- map tagged errors exhaustively to protocol errors;
    39	- encode response through Schema;
    40	- set headers/cookies through typed protocol facilities;
    41	- execute in the incoming native Effect request fibre when the host supplies one;
    42	- otherwise bridge only at the application-owned host runner.
    43	
    44	Do not pass a raw Request into the domain service.
    45	
    46	For a native Alchemy HTTP host, keep its HttpEffect contract and let the host
    47	adapt routing failures, defects and cancellation. Do not replace all failures
    48	with 500: a missing route must still return 404. Test the native host adaptation
    49	and select safe ErrorReporter fields separately from the response mapping.
    50	
    51	## RPC
    52	
    53	Define RPC procedures from shared Schemas and tagged serialisable errors. Keep transport details out of the domain service.
    54	
    55	Require:
    56	
    57	- request/response Schema;
    58	- error Schema;
    59	- authentication/authorisation boundary;
    60	- deadline/cancellation propagation;
    61	- versioning;
    62	- payload limits;
    63	- observability safe fields.
    64	
    65	Do not expose arbitrary Effect Causes or unencoded class instances over RPC.
    66	Declared Schema-tagged errors are encoded on the wire and decoded by clients.
    67	
    68	## Shared client contract
    69	
    70	Keep native generated clients private to semantic client Layers. HTTP and RPC
    71	clients implement the same domain service contract as the backend. Decode
    72	expected backend failures with the shared Schema and map connection or invalid
    73	reply failures to distinct named domain-access errors. No protocol error or
    74	unchecked provider payload leaks into UI policy.
    75	
    76	Test syntactically valid replies with the wrong payload Schema, as well as
    77	broken JSON. In the qualified 4.0.2, native RPC reply decoding can produce a
    78	SchemaError defect. The private client marks failure inside only the native
    79	exit reply codec's decoder, before native RPC converts that failure to a
    80	defect. Its semantic operation translates only that private marker to the named
    81	invalid-response error. Keep the native Schemas, Ndjson parser, Protocol and
    82	client; do not replace them with a handwritten protocol.
    83	
    84	Never infer reply failure from the SchemaError class alone. An unrelated
    85	transport or request encoder can fail with that same class and must keep its
    86	original defect identity. Test both reads with bad native replies and an
    87	unrelated adapter SchemaError. Preserve caller interruption and other defects;
    88	do not turn every Cause into an expected failure. Requalify the cached native
    89	exit Schema identity and reply decoder behaviour on Effect upgrades before
    90	retaining or removing this compatibility handling.
    91	
    92	For public, unauthenticated browser reads, omit credentials and reject redirects
    93	so a checked API address cannot silently send the browser somewhere else.
    94	Supply native Fetch RequestInit policy when the operation executes, not only
    95	while constructing its Layer. Protected clients need their own explicit policy.
    96	
    97	A selecting field can identify a response union. Native generation alone does
    98	not give a dependent return type: check the selected response Schema before
    99	narrowing literal/default inputs. See the [format-selected example](../examples/format-selected-client.md).
   100	
   101	For browser clients, test CORS preflight with the actual native request headers.
   102	In the qualified Effect version this includes b3 and traceparent. A successful
   103	server request is not browser-access proof. Remote MCP and Website WebMCP have
   104	separate Origin policies; do not inherit one policy from the other.
   105	
   106	## Serialisation
   107	
   108	Values crossing a process/runtime/hydration boundary must be encoded.
   109	
   110	Watch:
   111	
   112	- Dates/instants;
   113	- Option/Result;
   114	- branded values;
   115	- big integers;
   116	- Maps/Sets/Chunks;
   117	- tagged errors;
   118	- URLs;
   119	- Redacted;
   120	- binary data;
   121	- cyclic values.
   122	
   123	Never assume JSON.stringify preserves domain semantics. Use Schema transformations and a versioned envelope.
   124	
   125	## Streaming HTTP/RPC
   126	
   127	Use Stream for actual incremental bodies/messages. Scope the response body and propagate cancellation. Define framing, maximum frame size, decode failure, heartbeat, and reconnection.
   128	
   129	Do not buffer a full stream into text/JSON and still claim streaming.
   130	
   131	## Testing
   132	
   133	Provide controlled HttpClient/fetch Layers. Assert:
   134	
   135	- encoded request;
   136	- secret header redaction;
   137	- redirect policy;
   138	- status/error mapping;
   139	- invalid JSON/body;
   140	- whole-read deadline before headers and while decoding a stalled body;
   141	- earlier caller interruption and request/body finalisation;
   142	- retry policy;
   143	- serialisation round-trip;
   144	- no live network in unit tests.
     1	# State, Collections, and Caches
     2	
     3	## State selection
     4	
     5	Choose the narrowest primitive:
     6	
     7	- immutable local value for pure transformation;
     8	- `Ref` for atomic synchronous Effect-managed state;
     9	- synchronised/ref variant when updates require effects;
    10	- subscription ref for observable current state;
    11	- `TxRef` inside `Effect.tx` for coordinated changes to several values;
    12	- Queue/PubSub for communication rather than shared mutable state;
    13	- Cache for keyed effectful memoisation with policy;
    14	- scoped resource for state tied to a lifetime.
    15	
    16	Inspect installed Effect exports; names and modules can change across versions.
    17	
    18	## No mutable globals
    19	
    20	Reject module-level mutable objects, arrays, Maps, Sets, clients, counters, or caches in shared packages.
    21	
    22	Application-level state belongs in a Layer so:
    23	
    24	- construction is explicit;
    25	- lifetime is scoped;
    26	- tests can substitute it;
    27	- concurrent access policy is visible;
    28	- shutdown can clear resources.
    29	
    30	## Ref
    31	
    32	Use Ref for small atomic state such as:
    33	
    34	- last safe provider cursor;
    35	- in-memory test inventory;
    36	- bounded operation observations;
    37	- feature state;
    38	- counters where Metric is not the right semantic store.
    39	
    40	Keep updates pure and atomic. Return a new readonly value using immutable collection functions; do not mutate the old value or use transient collection modes. Do not read-modify-write using separate operations when lost updates matter. Pure folds need no Ref. Effects inside an update need the installed synchronised or transactional primitive and its tested interruption policy.
    41	
    42	## Transactions
    43	
    44	The qualified Effect 4.0.2 uses `Effect.tx` with `TxRef` and the other
    45	transactional collections, such as `TxQueue`. Use them when several values must
    46	change together, or an operation must wait until transactional state changes.
    47	The outermost `Effect.tx` commits all changes together on success and discards
    48	them on failure. Nested transactions share that boundary. `Effect.txRetry`
    49	waits for a value read by the transaction to change, then retries the transaction.
    50	
    51	```ts
    52	import { Effect, TxRef } from "effect";
    53	
    54	const incrementTogether = Effect.gen(function* () {
    55	  const left = yield* TxRef.make(0);
    56	  const right = yield* TxRef.make(0);
    57	  yield* Effect.tx(
    58	    Effect.gen(function* () {
    59	      yield* TxRef.update(left, (value) => value + 1);
    60	      yield* TxRef.update(right, (value) => value + 1);
    61	    }),
    62	  );
    63	  return { left: yield* TxRef.get(left), right: yield* TxRef.get(right) };
    64	});
    65	```
    66	
    67	Keep external writes outside the transaction. Retrying a transaction can repeat
    68	its program; network calls and file writes are not rolled back with `TxRef`
    69	changes. Test both successful coordinated changes and failure rollback.
    70	
    71	Examples:
    72	
    73	- reserve capacity and enqueue work together;
    74	- move an item between two collections;
    75	- update resource inventory plus index;
    76	- coordinate a bounded pool.
    77	
    78	Do not introduce a transaction for a single simple value.
    79	
    80	## Domain collections
    81	
    82	Use immutable Effect collections for domain state where they express equality, hashing, ordering, and persistent updates. Use ReadonlyArray for bounded ordered serialisable values.
    83	
    84	Native Map/Set may remain:
    85	
    86	- within a private performance-critical implementation;
    87	- when a host API requires them;
    88	- never solely because the code is a total leaf or the mutation is local.
    89	
    90	Document and test the containment. Never expose a mutable reference.
    91	
    92	## Cache
    93	
    94	Define:
    95	
    96	- key Schema/brand;
    97	- lookup Effect and error;
    98	- capacity;
    99	- expiry using Effect time;
   100	- invalidation;
   101	- concurrent miss behaviour;
   102	- negative-cache policy;
   103	- observability;
   104	- scope/shutdown.
   105	
   106	Do not use a plain global Map as a cache. Do not cache secrets, provider errors, or unbounded payloads without explicit policy.
   107	
   108	## Context-local state
   109	
   110	Use Effect context/fibre-local facilities for request correlation or scoped annotations when supported by the installed version. Do not use ambient global variables for request identity.
   111	
   112	## Tests
   113	
   114	Test:
   115	
   116	- atomic concurrent updates;
   117	- scoped isolation;
   118	- cache hit/miss/expiry with TestClock;
   119	- invalidation;
   120	- bounded capacity;
   121	- failure caching policy;
   122	- no state leakage between test Layers;
   123	- immutable collection behaviour.
   124	
   125	## Structured keys and shared cancellation
   126	
   127	A key includes every part of the saved address: for example record ID, version,
   128	revision and preparation hash. Infer it from one owning Struct using existing
   129	branded fields. Pass that readonly record directly to the cache. Internal cache
   130	keys and values need no JSON encode/decode. Serialisation belongs only to a real
   131	persistence or message boundary.
   132	
   133	Research installed Equal, Hash, Cache and ScopedCache source before changing
   134	keys or resource ownership. Qualified v4 plain records use structural equality
   135	and hashing; prove separately reconstructed equivalent keys share one lookup
   136	and changing each address field creates a distinct lookup. Do not mutate a key
   137	after insertion or use Effect Hash as a cryptographic source hash.
   138	
   139	For a scoped shared lookup, keep the existing capacity, success/failure expiry,
   140	deadline and acquisition/finaliser contract. Test that cancelling one of two
   141	readers keeps the lookup alive, the last reader cancels it, and cancellation
   142	waits for underlying cleanup. Requalify these behaviours on a version change;
   143	matching names in an older clone do not prove the installed cancellation rules.
     1	# Logging, Tracing, and Metrics
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [One observability design](#one-observability-design)
     6	- [Structured logging](#structured-logging)
     7	- [Log levels](#log-levels)
     8	- [Tracing](#tracing)
     9	- [Metrics](#metrics)
    10	- [Resource identity](#resource-identity)
    11	- [Exporter Layers](#exporter-layers)
    12	- [Failure policy](#failure-policy)
    13	- [Proof](#proof)
    14	- [Alchemy](#alchemy)
    15	
    16	## One observability design
    17	
    18	Treat logs, traces, and metrics as part of the service contract:
    19	
    20	- what semantic operation is visible;
    21	- what identity connects signals;
    22	- which fields are safe;
    23	- what cardinality is bounded;
    24	- how exporters attach to the runtime;
    25	- how ingestion is proved.
    26	
    27	Do not scatter `console.log` and later wrap it with a logger.
    28	
    29	## Structured logging
    30	
    31	Use Effect logging and annotations. Prefer an event name plus typed safe fields:
    32	
    33	- service/operation;
    34	- environment/stage;
    35	- resource/domain safe ID;
    36	- outcome/error tag;
    37	- attempt;
    38	- duration;
    39	- bounded count;
    40	- source revision where useful.
    41	
    42	Avoid:
    43	
    44	- string-concatenated blobs;
    45	- full objects;
    46	- raw Errors/Causes;
    47	- headers/cookies;
    48	- provider responses;
    49	- credentials;
    50	- user content unless explicitly governed;
    51	- high-volume per-item logging.
    52	
    53	Define a safe error-to-fields function for each error union.
    54	
    55	Native Alchemy beta.81 HTTP handling logs the raw Cause when no ErrorReporter
    56	is visible to its failure mapper. A reporter provided only inside the route
    57	does not reach that outer catch. At the API host boundary, qualify native
    58	`Http.safeHttpEffect` around the handler and provide its checked reporter set
    59	to that mapper with `Effect.provideService`. Build the reporter Layer once;
    60	capture only `ErrorReporter.CurrentErrorReporters`, never the initialisation
    61	Scope, logger or tracer. Avoid a new scoped Layer around each returned response.
    62	
    63	Effect 4.0.2 requires a synchronous ErrorReporter callback. Keep this narrow
    64	host exception explicit beside the callback. It may call the current native
    65	loggers with fixed bounded fields, an empty Cause and the host-supplied fibre
    66	and timestamp; it must ignore original error text, Causes, attributes and
    67	provider payloads. Add no console call, ambient clock or extra runner. Test the
    68	real handler with secret-like sentinels and original metadata, preserve native
    69	404/499/503/500 handling, and prove the incoming request Scope is retained and
    70	released. Requalify the native mapper and callback on Effect/Alchemy upgrades.
    71	
    72	## Log levels
    73	
    74	Use consistent semantics:
    75	
    76	- debug/trace: bounded development diagnostics;
    77	- info: lifecycle or meaningful state transition;
    78	- warning: recovered degradation or operator attention;
    79	- error: terminal operation failure;
    80	- fatal: application/runtime cannot continue.
    81	
    82	Do not log expected not-found/validation at error by default.
    83	
    84	## Tracing
    85	
    86	Create spans around:
    87	
    88	- domain service operation;
    89	- external provider/HTTP/database call;
    90	- queue/message handling;
    91	- infrastructure plan/apply/readback;
    92	- meaningful stream stage.
    93	
    94	Do not instrument every pure helper or Layer constructor.
    95	
    96	Use stable span names. Attach safe low-cardinality operation attributes and high-cardinality identifiers only when trace backends and privacy policy permit them.
    97	
    98	Public service methods use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`; private
    99	Effect helpers normally use `Effect.fnUntraced` and stay within the caller's
   100	span. A private external operation can own a separate named span. Keep pure
   101	helpers plain and avoid extracting one-use helpers just to decorate them.
   102	For contracts exposing an Effect value rather than a method, use the operation's
   103	named `Effect.withSpan` without changing the public API into a fake method.
   104	
   105	Propagate context across supported HTTP/RPC/queue boundaries. Do not leak it into untrusted channels without validation.
   106	
   107	## Metrics
   108	
   109	Use:
   110	
   111	- counters for occurrences;
   112	- histograms/timers for distributions;
   113	- gauges for current bounded state;
   114	- frequency/category metrics only with closed values.
   115	
   116	Good labels:
   117	
   118	- operation from a closed set;
   119	- result tag;
   120	- provider kind;
   121	- environment;
   122	- service.
   123	
   124	Bad labels:
   125	
   126	- user/resource/request ID;
   127	- full URL;
   128	- error message;
   129	- revision on every metric;
   130	- arbitrary stage/branch without a bounded policy.
   131	
   132	## Resource identity
   133	
   134	Attach runtime resource attributes such as:
   135	
   136	- service name;
   137	- service version/source revision;
   138	- deployment environment;
   139	- deployment stage;
   140	- repository/application identity.
   141	
   142	Keep request-level identity out of resource attributes.
   143	
   144	If shared Axiom datasets are used, ensure logs/spans carry enough identity for stage/service/revision proof. Keep metric labels low-cardinality and use logs/traces for revision-level proof.
   145	
   146	## Exporter Layers
   147	
   148	Register logger/tracer/meter/exporter configuration at its owning application
   149	boundary. Build resources for the lifetime their host actually supports:
   150	
   151	- acquire endpoint/token through Config/Redacted;
   152	- select transport and batching;
   153	- scope exporter lifetime;
   154	- flush on shutdown/host completion;
   155	- avoid multiple duplicate exporters;
   156	- separate server and browser policy;
   157	- separate application and platform telemetry.
   158	
   159	Long-lived servers can build exporters once and flush at graceful shutdown.
   160	Cloudflare's per-event exporters and metric registries belong to each event,
   161	not a process-global batch created by an earlier request. Native Alchemy registers
   162	the configuration once, then builds exporters into each event's Scope.
   163	
   164	First consider platform-managed delivery. On Cloudflare, Effect's structured
   165	console logger can feed Workers logs, with Alchemy-owned ObservabilityDestination
   166	resources delivering logs and native traces to Axiom. This removes the application
   167	exporter and its flush Scope/`waitUntil` adapter. Use native `Cloudflare.Telemetry()`
   168	for Effect Worker traces; do not pretend framework Websites receive its services.
   169	Use automatic platform tracing for a standard framework Website rather than
   170	recreating Alchemy's tracer or adding manual span lifecycle wrappers. Keep normal
   171	host imports and request-time binding reads inside the private live adapter,
   172	separate from host-independent operations tested with Effect Layers. Custom spans need a specific unmet diagnostic requirement.
   173	Cloudflare currently exports logs and traces, not custom metrics. Request-log
   174	counts can replace custom counters when the product accepts their coverage and
   175	best-effort limits. Remove direct OTLP bindings at cutover, explicitly configure
   176	both hosts, and qualify the actual stored log shape and dashboard queries.
   177	
   178	Only when application-managed export is required: an ordinary Effect Scope waits
   179	for finalisers, so keep its cleanup outside response delivery. Native Alchemy owns
   180	this lifecycle. A framework may hand a separate monitoring Scope's bounded closure
   181	to host completion through its existing runtime and private Promise adapter.
   182	Avoid coordination handshakes, borrowed contexts, detached fibres and extra
   183	runtimes. Preserve response streams and never fall back to blocking on upload.
   184	
   185	Required business work and durable audit records have a separate delivery
   186	contract. This policy does not let a command abandon its final flush or a
   187	long-lived server skip graceful shutdown. Follow the Alchemy
   188	[hosted web telemetry owner](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md)
   189	for the native Worker and framework Website adaptations.
   190	
   191	## Failure policy
   192	
   193	Decide whether telemetry failure:
   194	
   195	- is best-effort and annotated;
   196	- degrades a feature;
   197	- blocks startup because auditability is required.
   198	
   199	Avoid recursive logging loops when the exporter fails. Never expose secrets in exporter errors.
   200	
   201	## Proof
   202	
   203	Test locally:
   204	
   205	- Layer composition;
   206	- log field safety;
   207	- span structure;
   208	- metric label bounds;
   209	- exporter request formation.
   210	- response release while uploads remain pending;
   211	- bounded cleanup, failure and cancellation independently of response streaming.
   212	
   213	For a live ingestion claim:
   214	
   215	1. emit a unique bounded proof signal;
   216	2. allow the documented ingestion delay;
   217	3. query the backend by service/environment/stage and proof identity;
   218	4. verify signal fields;
   219	5. record only safe counts/IDs/time window.
   220	
   221	An exporter HTTP success is not query proof.
   222	
   223	## Alchemy
   224	
   225	Infrastructure Effects use the same policy:
   226	
   227	- span plan/apply/readback, not pure declarations;
   228	- annotate stack/stage/resource/change class;
   229	- never log state or credentials;
   230	- use metrics for bounded operation outcomes;
   231	- keep durable receipts separate from telemetry;
   232	- query configured Axiom datasets independently after deployment.

1	# React and TanStack
     2	
     3	## Contents
     4	
     5	- [Keep render pure](#keep-render-pure)
