    42	## Service shape
    43	
    44	Prefer package-owned `Context.Service` services with explicit dependencies through
    45	the Effect `R` channel. Do not hide rule, parameter or runtime dependencies in
    46	module globals.
    47	
    48	Core service categories:
    49	
    50	- fact providers for accepted input facts
    51	- parameter services for tax-year tables and constants
    52	- rule layers that derive facts from facts and parameters
    53	- calculator programs that require facts and return schema-backed reports
    54	- calculator, API and SDK services that adapt transport, CLI or plain-client
    55	  inputs to engine inputs
    56	
    57	Public calculator services should live in `packages/calculators`, not HTTP
    58	handler modules. A calculator service method should own calculator lookup,
    59	context validation, metadata projection, graph diagnostics, scenario layer
    60	composition, `CalculationEngine` execution and expected error shaping. HTTP
    61	handlers should only pass route input to the service and return the resulting
    62	schema-backed value or tagged error envelope.

    64	## Effect-native primitives
    65	
    66	TaxKit code MUST use Effect-native primitives and platform APIs when they fit
    67	the problem. This is a consistency and reliability rule, not a style
    68	preference.
    69	
    70	Use:
    71	
    72	- `Data`, `Schema`, `Schema.TaggedClass`, `Schema.TaggedStruct`,
    73	  `Data.TaggedClass` and `Data.TaggedError` for domain values and expected
    74	  errors.
    75	- `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `Record`, `Option`, `Result`,
    76	  `Exit` and `Match` for collection processing, lookup results, closed-domain
    77	  dispatch and program results.
    78	- `Context`, `Context.Service`, `Layer`, `Config`, `ConfigProvider`,
    79	  `ManagedRuntime`, Bun runtime/platform APIs and `Command` for dependency
    80	  injection, configuration, app runtime lifecycle and process/platform work.
    81	
    82	Do not fall back to ad hoc classes, manual `_tag` object literals, mutable
    83	JavaScript `Map`/`Set` indexes, nullable lookups, `switch`, `Object.values`,
    84	`Object.entries`, custom env parsing, manual process signal orchestration,
    85	request-local runtime creation or hand-rolled runtime wrappers when Effect
    86	owns the pattern.
    87	
    88	Calculator-owned context, help and filter fields use `Option<Option<A>>` in
    89	checked TypeScript values: `None` means a missing key, `Some(None)` means a
    90	present undefined key, and `Some(Some(value))` means a present value. Owning
    91	constructors default omitted keys to `None`. JSON and HTTP query fields retain
    92	their ordinary optional representation. Flatten the two absent forms only where
    93	they mean the same thing; do not invent a jurisdiction or tax year. Code MUST NOT use undefined checks and defaulting such
    94	as `payload.jurisdiction ?? "AU"` to invent missing calculator context.
    95	Missing context MUST either remain absent, be decoded by a schema that
    96	explicitly owns the default, or fail with a tagged expected error.
    97	
    98	Code MUST use pipe-first composition for readable Effect and data pipelines
    99	when it keeps the source value visible and data flow clearer, for example
   100	`query.pipe(filterCalculatorEntries, toFactsResponse)`. Do not nest
   101	transformations in wrapper calls when a left-to-right pipeline makes ownership
   102	and flow clearer.
   103	
   104	Use the installed Effect v4 `Effect.fn` when a reusable operation benefits from
   105	a stable stack-frame boundary, readable tracing name or operation-level
   106	transforms. Keep it on meaningful service/provider operations; do not wrap a
   107	single expression merely to add another name. Primary operations remain one
   108	flat, sequential pipe or generator.

   110	## String-shaped contracts
   111	
   112	Classify a string-shaped value by the policy it carries, not by the fact that
   113	its JavaScript representation is a string. The owning package or app owns the
   114	Schema, schema-derived `Type`, encoded representation and constructor. Do not
   115	create a central strings package, generic brand factory or content wrapper.
   116	
   117	Use these six categories:
   118	
   119	- **Open semantic value.** Use an owner-named string Schema and
   120	  `Schema.brand` when mixing the value with another otherwise-valid string is
   121	  a real defect, for example a fact ID passed where a rule ID is required.
   122	  `Schema.brand` is nominal only in the installed Effect version; it does not
   123	  validate syntax. Add checks only for a stable documented invariant.
   124	- **Closed vocabulary.** Use an owner-named `Schema.Literal` or
   125	  `Schema.Literals` for a finite set of kinds, statuses, modes or operations.
   126	  Use `Match` for material branching over that vocabulary. A literal Schema
   127	  may also carry an existing owner brand when both the finite runtime contract
   128	  and nominal identity matter.
   129	- **Redacted secret.** For raw secret ingress, use an owner-named
   130	  `Schema.RedactedFromValue` and set `disallowEncode` unless an explicit secret
   131	  egress exists. `Schema.Redacted` expects an already-redacted value. Reveal a
   132	  secret only in the owning live adapter at final client construction; do not
   133	  reveal it merely to apply a brand.
   134	- **Checked content.** Ordinary titles, descriptions, messages and authored
   135	  text may remain `string`, `Schema.String` or `Schema.NonEmptyString`. Extract
   136	  an owner-named Schema only when content has independent validation, secrecy,
   137	  mixing or repeated boundary policy. Brand only when two valid content
   138	  domains must not be mixed.
   139	- **Transport primitive.** Serialized JSON, URLs, headers, file/process
   140	  representations and encoded keys use owner-named boundary Schemas when they
   141	  are exported. Parser-local fragments may stay local after the complete
   142	  representation has been decoded.
   143	- **Diagnostic text.** Safety is an egress data-flow property, not a nominal
   144	  string type. Persistent, provider-facing or user-facing diagnostics must not
   145	  contain secrets, private paths, raw private payloads or unchecked exception
   146	  bodies. Prove the egress with sentinel tests, or document the exact local,
   147	  non-persistent operator boundary that intentionally receives raw output.
   148	
   149	At every boundary, record the Schema's `Type` and `Encoded` forms separately.
   150	Decode an unknown or representation-level value once at ingress, pass the
   151	canonical `Type` inward, and encode only at an explicit HTTP, provider,
   152	persistence, route or command egress. The owning Schema’s `make` is valid construction for
   153	trusted literals; it is not evidence of runtime validation that the underlying
   154	Schema does not provide.
   155	
   156	Core's constrained money, date and decimal helpers return owned schema-tagged
   157	errors through Effects. `aud` remains pure for already checked cents; use
   158	`audFromCents` for a number that still needs checking. New arithmetic results
   159	must pass the owning fallible constructor. Rules translate those failures to
   160	safe calculation errors without copying the input amount or a raw Schema issue.
   161	The [core README](../../packages/core/README.md) owns the concrete helper and
   162	date Option contracts. A representation codec must retain its whole-record
   163	check on the encoded side when Type/Encoded transformations differ.
   164	
   165	Explicit recursive encoded contracts such as `TraceNodeEncoded`, and generic
   166	descriptor relations that preserve schema-to-service inference, are not
   167	DTO mirrors. Keep them when TypeScript cannot otherwise express the recursive
   168	or generic relation. Do not use that exception for ordinary duplicated object
   169	shapes. The trace domain/encoded aliases infer their non-recursive fields
   170	from one shared Schema and annotate only children. Ledger component aliases
   171	are inferred directly from their owning Schema. These exported aliases replace
   172	open interfaces, so declaration merging is no longer an extension point; their
   173	historical encoded values remain the same.
   174	
   175	The calculation engine separates its service contract from its live Layer.
   176	Its real Effect/Layer/result relation stays generic; optional validation input
   177	retains its empty-collection meaning. Fact/parameter/rule metadata derives from
   178	private owning Schemas, with Option for meaningful absence and a total rule
   179	parameter array. Tuple service types derive from the native key Identifier.
   180	The [Core owner](../../packages/core/README.md) explains missing versus explicit
   181	undefined trace/question representations.

   183	## Provider and SDK adapters
   184	
   185	Third-party SDKs remain private inside one exact live adapter. Public
   186	`Context.Service` contracts expose owner-named operations over canonical
   187	Schema-derived input/output and closed schema-tagged errors. They must not expose
   188	the raw client, accept a generic callback over the SDK, publish raw identifier
   189	fields or allow an SDK result to escape unchecked.
   190	
   191	Encode canonical input at provider egress and decode `unknown` provider output
   192	immediately at provider ingress. Map transport and malformed-response failures
   193	to safe `Schema.TaggedError` values at the operation boundary. Do not use
   194	`instanceof`, raw provider tags, exception objects, response bodies or secrets in
   195	public error contracts. Use decoded literals/tagged unions with `Match` or typed
   196	Effect handlers.
   197	
   198	Provider configuration follows `configuration.md`: owner-named Schema and
   199	`Config.schema` fragments, app-owned `ConfigProvider`, and secret unwrapping
   200	only at final SDK construction. A provider service must have an explicit live
   201	Layer and deterministic mock Layer with focused encoding, failure, malformed
   202	output and substitution tests.
   203	
   204	The Fumadocs generated-source boundary follows the same rule.
   205	`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs/service` exposes only named `getPage` and `listPages`
   206	Effects over schema-decoded generic page values. Its live Layer accepts one
   207	narrow generated-collection adapter at construction, contains unknown provider
   208	output plus promise and throw handling, and emits safe tagged errors.
   209	`@taxkit/docs-content` supplies the TaxKit collection adapter and decodes the
   210	generic value into its canonical content Schemas. Neither package executes a
   211	runtime. The accepted catalogue is built through the generated adapter;
   212	`apps/api` owns its checked content service and `apps/web` owns the reader
   213	runner and private API connection. The old app runtime is retained history.
   214	
   215	The infrastructure-owned `PostHogManagement` contract has only find, read,
   216	create and update operations over checked TaxKit identities. Its private
   217	Distilled adapter contains paging, credentials, supported privacy settings,
   218	bounded replies and safe failure mapping. The native resource provider and
   219	deterministic test Layer depend on that closed contract. Alchemy beta.80 requires
   220	provider registration without an error channel, so the composition Layer caches
   221	fallible live acquisition in the native stack scope and defers it to a lifecycle
   222	operation. Invalid settings remain typed failures before any request. The
   223	[infrastructure owner](../../packages/infrastructure/README.md) records the
   224	retention, limits and qualification boundaries; no app runtime receives this
   225	management service. Its native HTTP attempt owns deterministic abort within
   226	the operation's scope, including refusal before reading a redirect body. The
   227	SDK receives only a bounded, collected in-memory response; that response can
   228	outlive the completed native request without retaining its connection.

   230	Use [the repo-owned effect client wrapper skill](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/effect-client-wrapper/SKILL.md)
   231	when introducing or reviewing a provider adapter. Its canonical example and

   234	## Runtime composition
   235	
   236	Use `ManagedRuntime.make(...)` for module-scoped app runtimes that run many
   237	Effects against the same fully provided service graph. Do not create a
   238	`ManagedRuntime` inside route loaders, React components, request handlers or
   239	per-operation helpers. The docs app owns one server-only managed runtime and an
   240	explicit disposal operation for focused tests and host lifecycle integration;
   241	it has no browser Effect runtime. Browser routes restore the schema-encoded
   242	server-function transport and render canonical values.
   243	
   244	The Website candidate owns one server runner and a React Atom registry in the
   245	browser. Its typed route context contains named framework settings/catalogue and
   246	documentation page and search transports, never an Effect runtime or Context. The root restores encoded values and passes
   247	checked submission state through ordinary React context. The container owns
   248	commands; focused leaves render readonly values. Editing and form unmount
   249	interrupt active work. Private binding transport belongs to the server Layer;
   250	public browser transport belongs to the registry. The RPC protocol Layer keeps
   251	configuration, while each named native client receive loop has an operation scope.
   252	No calculation or catalogue read builds a Layer or runner. See the [Website owner](../../apps/web/README.md).
   253	The SDK owns one runtime per client, with caller disposal and bounded one-shot
   254	helpers; see the [SDK lifetime owner](api-and-sdk.md#typescript-sdk-facade).
   255	
   256	Use `@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain(...)` for Bun process entrypoints
   257	where the root Effect is the process lifecycle. Process entrypoints should
   258	compose config, platform layers and server layers, then let Effect
   259	interruption/scopes release resources.

   280	## Promise boundaries
   281	
   282	Fallible Promise and SDK calls enter Effect with an explicit inline rejection
   283	mapping:
   284	
   285	```ts
   286	Effect.tryPromise({
   287	  try: () => providerOperation(),
   288	  catch: () => new ProviderRequestError({ message: "Provider request failed" }),
   289	});
   290	```
   291	
   292	Do not use callback-form `Effect.tryPromise`, which exposes
   293	`Cause.UnknownError` instead of the owning boundary's closed tagged error. Keep
   294	the `try` and `catch` policy inline so the raw rejection cannot escape or be
   295	hidden in a generic options/helper value. Both properties must be direct inline
   296	arrow, function or object-method implementations; do not use shorthand,
   297	extracted callbacks, non-function values or spread policy. Use `Effect.promise`
   298	only when a Promise rejection is intentionally treated as a defect. The current
   299	portable lint scope enforces this contract in packages, the API app and
   300	repository tools and both website applications. The strict override covers all
   301	owned TypeScript and JavaScript extensions. Five unexecuted upstream lint-input
   302	fixtures have exact strict-only exclusions; their neighbouring files still
   303	receive the full policy. The [testing owner](testing-and-quality.md) records
   304	the coverage and actual-command rejection proof.
   305	
   306	## Callsite error handling
   307	
   308	One-off Effect error handling MUST stay at the callsite. Error transformations
   309	MUST live directly beside the operation whose failure is being transformed:
   310	
   311	```ts
   312	program.pipe(
   313	  Effect.mapError(
   314	    () => new BoundaryError({ message: "Boundary settings are invalid" })
   315	  )
   316	);
   317	```
   318	
   319	Do not extract one-off helpers such as `mapConfigError`, `toBoundaryError` or
   320	`createRuntimeLayer` only to wrap a single `Effect.mapError`, `Effect.catchTag`,
   321	`Effect.catchAll` or `Effect.catchAllDefect` call. Extraction is allowed only
   322	when the helper is reused across boundaries, owns a real policy, or materially
   323	reduces complex duplication.
   324	
   325	## Abstraction admission
   326	
   327	Effect abstractions follow the repository-wide
   328	[abstraction admission contract](../design-docs/abstraction-admission.md).
   329	Before adding a shared service, layer, runtime wrapper, codec helper or program
   330	fragment, record its owner, semantic policy, second consumer or real
   331	substitution point, simpler before/after call graph and focused tests.
   332	
   333	A live/test Layer pair is a real substitution point when both implement one
   334	host-neutral service contract and tests exercise the production policy through
   335	that contract. Splitting every operation into its own service, mapper or layer
   336	does not qualify. Keep one-use decoding, encoding, tagged-error mapping and
   337	runtime execution inline at their owning boundary, and keep a primary
   338	operation as one readable `pipe` or `Effect.gen` program.

   340	## Boundary-only decoding
   341	
   342	Decode a value only when it crosses an explicit trust or type-erasure boundary.
   343	After an owning `Schema` has produced its schema-derived type, internal code
   344	must pass that type inward without decoding it again. This is a contract rule;
   345	it is not permission to replace Schema with casts, manual guards or object
   346	readers.
   347	
   348	Executable decoding belongs at one of these boundaries:
   349	
   350	- external input from HTTP, configuration, environment, storage, files,
   351	  serialised server/client transport or another process
   352	- an exported API that intentionally accepts `unknown`
   353	- normalisation of representation-level data supplied by an external library
   354	- dynamic catalogue or descriptor selection, where heterogeneous storage has
   355	  erased the selected schema's concrete type
   356	- a focused boundary test that proves one of these behaviours
   357	
   358	Do not decode between internal services, as defensive validation of an already
   359	typed parameter, inside ordinary rule or calculator code, or merely to build a
   360	unit-test fixture. A repeated or internal decoder is implementation work, not a
   361	new boundary to allowlist.
   362	
   363	For dynamic catalogue and descriptor dispatch, a policy-owning generic
   364	constructor must close over both the selected schema and the continuation that
   365	accepts `InputSchema["Type"]` before heterogeneous storage erases that generic.
   366	Do not recover the concrete type with an unsafe cast or by passing the decoded
   367	value through an `unknown` callback. The selected calculator input decoder and
   368	SDK report decoder are examples of required type-erasure boundaries.
   369	
   370	Keep each boundary operation linear. Start with the canonical decoder, map its
   371	expected `Schema.SchemaError` inline where that boundary owns the public error
   372	context, then continue with the typed value in one readable `pipe` or
   373	`Effect.gen` program. Preserve unrelated typed errors; do not use broad
   374	`Effect.catchAll`, `Effect.orDie`, raw Promise control flow or nested runtime
   375	execution to bridge a decoder. An app entrypoint, route loader or plain SDK
   376	facade may execute a completed Effect only at its exact outer host. The plain
   377	SDK host has a caller-owned runtime for each client and a temporary scope for
   378	one-shot helpers; it has no package-global runtime. The
   379	[SDK lifetime owner](api-and-sdk.md#typescript-sdk-facade) explains closing,
   380	interruption, bounded outcomes and the separate Effect interface.
   381	
   382	Do not extract one-use fragments such as `decodePayload`, `mapDecodeError`,
   383	`runDecoder`, `withDecodedInput` or generic `decodeOrFail`. A shared helper is
   384	appropriate only when it owns real, repeated policy, such as the generic
   385	catalogue constructor that preserves schema-to-continuation coupling. Review
   386	helper reuse and ownership with the task's path-evidenced semantic audit rather
   387	than a brittle function-size rule or a fixed audit count.
   388	
   389	`taxkit/no-decoding-outside-boundaries` enforces decoder placement across the
   390	repository. Its exact file allowlist belongs only in `oxlint.config.ts`; this
   391	architecture page owns the categories and review contract, not a duplicate
   392	path list. Use the active decoder inventory and this contract during review.
   393	
   394	## Encoding and contract boundaries
   395	
   396	Encoding is the inverse trust operation. Execute an owning Schema encoder only
   397	where a canonical value leaves the system as HTTP or route transport, provider
   398	input, persisted representation or command output. Do not encode between
   399	services, as a defensive copy, or inside ordinary React composition.
   400	`effect/no-schema-encoder-outside-egress` is enabled repository-wide and exact
   401	egress files are disabled only in `oxlint.config.ts`.
   402	
   403	Production code must not use throwing `Schema.*Sync` codecs. Prefer
   404	`Schema.decodeUnknownEffect` or `Schema.encodeUnknownEffect` at an Effect
   405	boundary and keep `Schema.SchemaError` in the typed channel. A synchronous
   406	consumer may use `Result`, `Exit` or `Option` codecs and must handle failure
   407	explicitly. Exact legacy test fixtures that intentionally prove throwing
   408	behaviour are listed in `oxlint.config.ts`; runtime filenames are not an
   409	implicit exception.
   410	
   411	Service methods accept schema-derived inputs and expose closed tagged errors.
   412	Do not annotate service parameters or Effect error channels as `unknown`.
   413	Tagged errors must not expose `Schema.Unknown` or a TypeScript `unknown` cause;
   414	reuse the owning error, preserve a true adapter defect with `Schema.Defect()`,
   415	or retain schema-safe diagnostic fields. Static lint cannot decide whether a
   416	`Schema.Defect()` cause should instead be a known provider or domain error, so
   417	that distinction remains a three-pass review requirement.
   418	
   419	Runtime execution, `console`, `process`, Bun host APIs and host-specific imports
   420	belong to exact adapters configured in `oxlint.config.ts`. Service, schema,
   421	error and config contracts depend on Effect Platform services or a
   422	`Context.Service`; their live layers choose Bun or another host. Provider SDK
   423	imports also require review because package names alone cannot reliably
   424	distinguish a portable contract from a legitimate adapter. Lint follows
   425	scope-resolved canonical Effect and platform imports, global host references,
   426	renamed bindings, aliases and statically known destructuring. Local values that
   427	merely reuse names such as `Effect`, `Schema`, `console`, `process`, `Bun` or
   428	`BunRuntime` are not host/runtime references. Dynamic and interprocedural value
   429	flow remains a review concern rather than a reason for broad suppressions.
   430	
   431	### TanStack loader transport
   432	
   433	Treat a TanStack Start server-function call and TanStack Router loader-state
   434	transport as separate representation crossings. When a server function
   435	produces route data, keep the schema-encoded representation intact through the
   436	route loader. On initial SSR, Router dehydrates and hydrates that encoded
   437	loader state. On client navigation, the server-function RPC serialiser and the
   438	route loader carry the same encoded value.
   439	
   440	Use a browser-safe boundary adapter built around
   441	`Schema.Exit(success, expectedError, Schema.Never)` when a route needs to
   442	transport an Effect outcome. The producer must capture `Effect.exit` once,
   443	encode a success or exactly one typed expected failure, and preserve any Cause
   444	containing a defect or interruption with `Effect.failCause`. An empty or
   445	multi-failure producer Cause is an invariant defect. Use `Effect.orDie` only
   446	when canonical schema encoding fails after the program has already satisfied
   447	the declared success and error contracts.
   448	
   449	The direct route component or route-owned `head` consumer may restore the
   450	encoded loader value when it first reads `Route.useLoaderData` or callback
   451	loader data. Restore once per consumer invocation, map malformed or
   452	semantically invalid transport to a schema-owned tagged transport error, and
   453	match the resulting `Result` before passing canonical values into React
   454	composition. Ordinary hooks, containers and leaf components must not receive
   455	encoded loader data, call the restore operation or run Effect runtimes.

   457	## Guardrails
   458	
   459	- Use `Schema` from `effect` for boundary and persisted values.
   460	- Schemas and tagged value shapes MUST live in colocated `schemas.ts` files, or
   461	  in the owning package's public schema module. Exported types MUST be derived
   462	  from those schemas. Runtime and handler files should compose services and
   463	  layers, not define or duplicate reusable shapes inline.
   464	- Canonical ids, branded scalar fields, request/response shapes, facts,
   465	  descriptors and tagged values MUST be declared once by the owning package.
   466	  Consumers MUST import and reuse the owning schema, type, constructor, service
   467	  tag or branded id. Do not redeclare canonical fields as local primitives such
   468	  as `id: string`, `ruleId: string` or object mirrors outside the owning
   469	  schema/type source.
   470	- Use `Layer` composition for rule packs and scenario inputs.
   471	- Keep parameter data separate from algorithms.
   472	- Use tagged errors for expected domain failures.
   473	- Expected domain and API failures MUST remain in the typed Effect error
   474	  channel. Do not use `Effect.die` for schema decode failures,
   475	  `CalculationError`, unsupported calculator/context errors, config decode
   476	  failures or other recoverable service-contract errors. Reserve defects for
   477	  impossible states outside the declared contract.
   478	- Manual `_tag` object literals are not allowed. Tagged values MUST be
   479	  constructed with `Data.TaggedClass`, `Data.TaggedError`,
   480	  `Schema.TaggedClass`, or an owning package constructor built from those
   481	  primitives.
   482	- Keep one-off error mapping and transformation logic inline at the callsite;
   483	  tiny mapper or wrapper helpers are not allowed.
   484	- Avoid local DTO mirrors when an owning schema already exists.
   485	- MUST use schema-owned optional fields instead of conditional object-spread
   486	  transforms for response shaping. Complex response-shaping policy MUST live in
   487	  the owning service package, not an HTTP handler.
   488	- Keep schema issue formatting in owning schema/error modules or services. Do
   489	  not inline ad hoc `typeof`/`in` object probes in handlers.
   490	- Keep engine services independent of React, request handlers and app state.
   491	- Keep HTTP handlers thin. Do not put reusable calculator transformation,
   492	  graph assembly, calculation dispatch or expected error-shaping policy in
   493	  `HttpApiBuilder.group(...)` handlers.

   499	- [Calculators](./calculators.md)
   500	- [API and SDK](./api-and-sdk.md)
   501	
   502	## Shared calculation work limits
   503	
   504	The calculator-owned [bounded Layer](../../packages/calculators/README.md#shared-calculation-work-limits)
   505	is a real host substitution point over `PublicCalculatorService`: native API and
   506	standalone HTTP roots build it once over the live implementation, while focused
   507	tests supply controlled work at the same contract. One pool serves all native
   508	transports and counts individual batch calculations. Scope and semaphore release
   509	own cleanup on every exit. Metadata remains outside calculation capacity, while
   510	all nine calls share the five-second completion budget. Lazy invocation counts
   511	metadata construction within it. The HTTP-owned streamed body policy provides
   512	Schema-owned JSON errors or fixed HTML guidance at the host boundary. No
   513	runner or live Layer is built inside a calculation, and no transport gains a
   514	competing application contract. The owning package records timeout and CPU limits.
   515	
   516	
   517	The [RPC owner](../../packages/api/rpc/README.md#complete-named-operation-contract)
   518	exposes all nine existing calculator operations. Its private concrete native
   519	operation transformation shares scope/deadline/safe transport policy across
   520	those named methods; application work remains at the calculator service. No
   521	operation constructs a Layer or runner, and callers receive no raw client.
   522	
   523	
   524	## Native calculation rate admission
   525	
   526	`CalculatorAdmission` is a closed named service; its [owning contract](../../packages/calculators/README.md#native-calculation-rate-admission) and redacted key Schema live with calculators. The request Context reference carries checked identity separately from facts. `PublicCalculatorServiceRateLimited` provides calculation-only admission; the native API composes it once below bounded work. Its provider Layer, installed live Layer and mock test Layer remain separate. Native provider replies are decoded immediately and failures become fixed errors without provider causes or addresses.
   527	
   528	
   529	Native rate decoding is admitted at the exact original-address, private-call,
   530	provider-reply and host-root owners in `oxlint.config.ts`. Its exact wire and
   531	redacted-key fixtures have separate decoder/encoder admissions. Actual CLI
   532	fixtures accept those owned crossings, reject encoder execution at production
   533	ingress, reject runners at every admitted file and reject decoding in the
   534	nearby calculator admission Layer. No wildcard or new unknown-parameter
   535	exception is added. The Website Layer accepts the generated native Fetcher
   536	capability; its settings boundary checks the richer API binding once.
   537	
   538	The native documentation RPC handler Layer captures the same supplied
   539	`ContentService` as public HTTP. It owns no runtime or catalogue fallback. A
   540	separate `DocsRpcClient` provides five closed named operations over native RPC,
   541	with its own revision/error vocabulary and per-call resource scope. Only the
   542	concrete closed JSON byte reader is shared with the calculator client; no raw
   543	client callback or provider object enters either service contract.
   544	
   545	The native API composes `ContentDiscoveryLive` once from the checked catalogue
   546	and its existing cached settings Effect. Configuration remains application-owned;
   547	the content capability lazily reads checked addresses and returns one bounded
   548	document for a closed file identity. `ContentDiscovery` is contract-only;
   549	the live and observed test Layers remain separate. The Website reuses its
   550	existing runner/private client and projects the checked document to an HTTP
   551	body. No incoming request builds a Layer, compiler, content cache or runtime.
   552	
   553	
   554	Website Markdown composition uses a named HTTP policy over the existing native
   555	HTML Effect. Original URL and Accept ingress decode once at that exact boundary;
   556	checked body lookup uses the already captured app service. It owns the
   557	representation's response/error headers inside the host's existing runner and
   558	request scope. No request builds a Layer or executes another runtime. The
   559	policy preserves existing HTML Vary fields and expected/fatal error separation.
   560	Its exact decoder admission and adjacent rejected paths have actual CLI proof.
   561	
   562	### Website build-only share rendering
   563	
   564	`apps/web/scripts/docs-images.build.ts` is a lazy scoped build program, composed
   565	and executed by the existing Vite host with NodeServices. Filesystem catalogue
   566	input and private native renderer bytes are decoded at this exact ingress.
   567	`acquireRelease` owns the renderer's lifetime, sequential page Effects own fixed
   568	catalogue/render/image/write failures, and the scoped finaliser releases native
   569	memory. No client or runner escapes into content/page logic. The named metadata
   570	output module separately encodes the owning public TechArticle Schema. Exact
   571	lint selectors admit these crossings only; adjacent route/rendering modules
   572	retain their restrictions.
   573	
   574	
   575	Native MCP tools use `Toolkit.toLayer` and `McpServer.toolkit`; no replacement
   576	registry or package runner is introduced. Current HTTP cancellation enters via
   577	an app-private `Context.Reference<Option<AbortSignal>>`. The named lifetime
   578	operation races tool work against an Effect callback for the native stop event.
   579	Listener registration and a second aborted-state check close the early-abort
   580	race; losing work and its finalisers are awaited. This capability carries no
   581	figures or identity and never changes a calculator/content service contract.
   582	The [API owner](../../apps/api/README.md#native-remote-calculator-tools-candidate)
   583	records the actual-client and built-Worker proof limits.

     9	
    10	# Effect services
    11	
    12	TaxKit uses Effect services, layers, schemas and tagged errors as the default
    13	shape for deterministic tax calculation boundaries.
    14	
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	This doc owns cross-package Effect service conventions. Rule-specific service
    18	contracts live with their owning rule packages and should link back here.
    19	
    20	The private [analytics package](../../packages/analytics/README.md) owns the
    21	two accepted event contracts. Its native backend Layer encodes a fixed provider
    22	request and maps transport failures to safe errors. The exact encoder admission
    23	in `oxlint.config.ts` covers that provider egress and its safe error-byte test;
    24	it does not admit runtime execution, raw JSON or decoding in neighbouring code.
    25	The package’s collection-header boundary is reused by the API and Website.
    26	The private `WebsiteAnalyticsRelay` exposes one native request handler with
    27	checked failures and no service requirements escaping its caller. Its named
    28	adapter captures native HttpClient once, decodes metadata at that explicit
    29	boundary, forwards bounded complete bytes, and owns each request scope and
    30	whole-operation deadline. It uses the existing server runner. Exact decoder
    31	permissions admit neither neighbouring decoders, raw fetch nor another runner;
    32	actual lint fixtures enforce those limits.
    33	The browser calculator transport reads its native preference at dispatch, and
    34	the server transport reads the current original request; neither freezes policy
    35	when its Layer is built. Missing server/browser hosts refuse collection.
    36	The application owns when to capture and which checked collection policy applies.
    37	The API application captures its delivery service during initialisation, then
    38	supplies it to each returned request operation. Worker and older MCP session
    39	delivery use their own native `waitUntil`; request collection remains fresh.
    40	T008 Website/browser composition and provider readback remain pending.
    41	
    42	## Service shape
    43	
    44	Prefer package-owned `Context.Service` services with explicit dependencies through
    45	the Effect `R` channel. Do not hide rule, parameter or runtime dependencies in
    46	module globals.
    47	
    48	Core service categories:
    49	
    50	- fact providers for accepted input facts
    51	- parameter services for tax-year tables and constants
    52	- rule layers that derive facts from facts and parameters
    53	- calculator programs that require facts and return schema-backed reports
    54	- calculator, API and SDK services that adapt transport, CLI or plain-client
    55	  inputs to engine inputs
    56	
    57	Public calculator services should live in `packages/calculators`, not HTTP
    58	handler modules. A calculator service method should own calculator lookup,
    59	context validation, metadata projection, graph diagnostics, scenario layer
    60	composition, `CalculationEngine` execution and expected error shaping. HTTP
    61	handlers should only pass route input to the service and return the resulting
    62	schema-backed value or tagged error envelope.
    63	
    64	## Effect-native primitives
    65	
    66	TaxKit code MUST use Effect-native primitives and platform APIs when they fit
    67	the problem. This is a consistency and reliability rule, not a style
    68	preference.
    69	
    70	Use:
    71	
    72	- `Data`, `Schema`, `Schema.TaggedClass`, `Schema.TaggedStruct`,
    73	  `Data.TaggedClass` and `Data.TaggedError` for domain values and expected
    74	  errors.
    75	- `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `Record`, `Option`, `Result`,
    76	  `Exit` and `Match` for collection processing, lookup results, closed-domain
    77	  dispatch and program results.
    78	- `Context`, `Context.Service`, `Layer`, `Config`, `ConfigProvider`,
    79	  `ManagedRuntime`, Bun runtime/platform APIs and `Command` for dependency
    80	  injection, configuration, app runtime lifecycle and process/platform work.
    81	
    82	Do not fall back to ad hoc classes, manual `_tag` object literals, mutable
    83	JavaScript `Map`/`Set` indexes, nullable lookups, `switch`, `Object.values`,
    84	`Object.entries`, custom env parsing, manual process signal orchestration,
    85	request-local runtime creation or hand-rolled runtime wrappers when Effect
    86	owns the pattern.
    87	
    88	Calculator-owned context, help and filter fields use `Option<Option<A>>` in
    89	checked TypeScript values: `None` means a missing key, `Some(None)` means a
    90	present undefined key, and `Some(Some(value))` means a present value. Owning
    91	constructors default omitted keys to `None`. JSON and HTTP query fields retain
    92	their ordinary optional representation. Flatten the two absent forms only where
    93	they mean the same thing; do not invent a jurisdiction or tax year. Code MUST NOT use undefined checks and defaulting such
    94	as `payload.jurisdiction ?? "AU"` to invent missing calculator context.
    95	Missing context MUST either remain absent, be decoded by a schema that
    96	explicitly owns the default, or fail with a tagged expected error.
    97	
    98	Code MUST use pipe-first composition for readable Effect and data pipelines
    99	when it keeps the source value visible and data flow clearer, for example
   100	`query.pipe(filterCalculatorEntries, toFactsResponse)`. Do not nest
   101	transformations in wrapper calls when a left-to-right pipeline makes ownership
   102	and flow clearer.
   103	
   104	Use the installed Effect v4 `Effect.fn` when a reusable operation benefits from
   105	a stable stack-frame boundary, readable tracing name or operation-level
   106	transforms. Keep it on meaningful service/provider operations; do not wrap a
   107	single expression merely to add another name. Primary operations remain one
   108	flat, sequential pipe or generator.
   109	
   110	## String-shaped contracts
   111	
   112	Classify a string-shaped value by the policy it carries, not by the fact that
   113	its JavaScript representation is a string. The owning package or app owns the
   114	Schema, schema-derived `Type`, encoded representation and constructor. Do not
   115	create a central strings package, generic brand factory or content wrapper.
   116	
   117	Use these six categories:
   118	
   119	- **Open semantic value.** Use an owner-named string Schema and
   120	  `Schema.brand` when mixing the value with another otherwise-valid string is
   121	  a real defect, for example a fact ID passed where a rule ID is required.
   122	  `Schema.brand` is nominal only in the installed Effect version; it does not
   123	  validate syntax. Add checks only for a stable documented invariant.
   124	- **Closed vocabulary.** Use an owner-named `Schema.Literal` or
   125	  `Schema.Literals` for a finite set of kinds, statuses, modes or operations.
   126	  Use `Match` for material branching over that vocabulary. A literal Schema
   127	  may also carry an existing owner brand when both the finite runtime contract
   128	  and nominal identity matter.
   129	- **Redacted secret.** For raw secret ingress, use an owner-named
   130	  `Schema.RedactedFromValue` and set `disallowEncode` unless an explicit secret
   131	  egress exists. `Schema.Redacted` expects an already-redacted value. Reveal a
   132	  secret only in the owning live adapter at final client construction; do not
   133	  reveal it merely to apply a brand.
   134	- **Checked content.** Ordinary titles, descriptions, messages and authored
   135	  text may remain `string`, `Schema.String` or `Schema.NonEmptyString`. Extract
   136	  an owner-named Schema only when content has independent validation, secrecy,
   137	  mixing or repeated boundary policy. Brand only when two valid content
   138	  domains must not be mixed.
   139	- **Transport primitive.** Serialized JSON, URLs, headers, file/process
   140	  representations and encoded keys use owner-named boundary Schemas when they
   141	  are exported. Parser-local fragments may stay local after the complete
   142	  representation has been decoded.
   143	- **Diagnostic text.** Safety is an egress data-flow property, not a nominal
   144	  string type. Persistent, provider-facing or user-facing diagnostics must not
   145	  contain secrets, private paths, raw private payloads or unchecked exception
   146	  bodies. Prove the egress with sentinel tests, or document the exact local,
   147	  non-persistent operator boundary that intentionally receives raw output.
   148	
   149	At every boundary, record the Schema's `Type` and `Encoded` forms separately.
   150	Decode an unknown or representation-level value once at ingress, pass the
   151	canonical `Type` inward, and encode only at an explicit HTTP, provider,
   152	persistence, route or command egress. The owning Schema’s `make` is valid construction for
   153	trusted literals; it is not evidence of runtime validation that the underlying
   154	Schema does not provide.
   155	
   156	Core's constrained money, date and decimal helpers return owned schema-tagged
   157	errors through Effects. `aud` remains pure for already checked cents; use
   158	`audFromCents` for a number that still needs checking. New arithmetic results
   159	must pass the owning fallible constructor. Rules translate those failures to
   160	safe calculation errors without copying the input amount or a raw Schema issue.
   161	The [core README](../../packages/core/README.md) owns the concrete helper and
   162	date Option contracts. A representation codec must retain its whole-record
   163	check on the encoded side when Type/Encoded transformations differ.
   164	
   165	Explicit recursive encoded contracts such as `TraceNodeEncoded`, and generic
   166	descriptor relations that preserve schema-to-service inference, are not
   167	DTO mirrors. Keep them when TypeScript cannot otherwise express the recursive
   168	or generic relation. Do not use that exception for ordinary duplicated object
   169	shapes. The trace domain/encoded aliases infer their non-recursive fields
   170	from one shared Schema and annotate only children. Ledger component aliases
   171	are inferred directly from their owning Schema. These exported aliases replace
   172	open interfaces, so declaration merging is no longer an extension point; their
   173	historical encoded values remain the same.
   174	
   175	The calculation engine separates its service contract from its live Layer.
   176	Its real Effect/Layer/result relation stays generic; optional validation input
   177	retains its empty-collection meaning. Fact/parameter/rule metadata derives from
   178	private owning Schemas, with Option for meaningful absence and a total rule
   179	parameter array. Tuple service types derive from the native key Identifier.
   180	The [Core owner](../../packages/core/README.md) explains missing versus explicit
   181	undefined trace/question representations.
   182	
   183	## Provider and SDK adapters
   184	
   185	Third-party SDKs remain private inside one exact live adapter. Public
   186	`Context.Service` contracts expose owner-named operations over canonical
   187	Schema-derived input/output and closed schema-tagged errors. They must not expose
   188	the raw client, accept a generic callback over the SDK, publish raw identifier
   189	fields or allow an SDK result to escape unchecked.
   190	
   191	Encode canonical input at provider egress and decode `unknown` provider output
   192	immediately at provider ingress. Map transport and malformed-response failures
   193	to safe `Schema.TaggedError` values at the operation boundary. Do not use
   194	`instanceof`, raw provider tags, exception objects, response bodies or secrets in
   195	public error contracts. Use decoded literals/tagged unions with `Match` or typed
   196	Effect handlers.
   197	
   198	Provider configuration follows `configuration.md`: owner-named Schema and
   199	`Config.schema` fragments, app-owned `ConfigProvider`, and secret unwrapping
   200	only at final SDK construction. A provider service must have an explicit live
   201	Layer and deterministic mock Layer with focused encoding, failure, malformed
   202	output and substitution tests.
   203	
   204	The Fumadocs generated-source boundary follows the same rule.
   205	`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs/service` exposes only named `getPage` and `listPages`
   206	Effects over schema-decoded generic page values. Its live Layer accepts one
   207	narrow generated-collection adapter at construction, contains unknown provider
   208	output plus promise and throw handling, and emits safe tagged errors.
   209	`@taxkit/docs-content` supplies the TaxKit collection adapter and decodes the
   210	generic value into its canonical content Schemas. Neither package executes a
   211	runtime. The accepted catalogue is built through the generated adapter;
   212	`apps/api` owns its checked content service and `apps/web` owns the reader
   213	runner and private API connection. The old app runtime is retained history.
   214	
   215	The infrastructure-owned `PostHogManagement` contract has only find, read,
   216	create and update operations over checked TaxKit identities. Its private
   217	Distilled adapter contains paging, credentials, supported privacy settings,
   218	bounded replies and safe failure mapping. The native resource provider and
   219	deterministic test Layer depend on that closed contract. Alchemy beta.80 requires
   220	provider registration without an error channel, so the composition Layer caches
   221	fallible live acquisition in the native stack scope and defers it to a lifecycle
   222	operation. Invalid settings remain typed failures before any request. The
   223	[infrastructure owner](../../packages/infrastructure/README.md) records the
   224	retention, limits and qualification boundaries; no app runtime receives this
   225	management service. Its native HTTP attempt owns deterministic abort within
   226	the operation's scope, including refusal before reading a redirect body. The
   227	SDK receives only a bounded, collected in-memory response; that response can
   228	outlive the completed native request without retaining its connection.
   229	
   230	Use [the repo-owned effect client wrapper skill](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/effect-client-wrapper/SKILL.md)
   231	when introducing or reviewing a provider adapter. Its canonical example and
   232	stale-pattern audit are acceptance requirements, not an optional template.
   233	
   234	## Runtime composition
   235	
   236	Use `ManagedRuntime.make(...)` for module-scoped app runtimes that run many
   237	Effects against the same fully provided service graph. Do not create a
   238	`ManagedRuntime` inside route loaders, React components, request handlers or
   239	per-operation helpers. The docs app owns one server-only managed runtime and an
   240	explicit disposal operation for focused tests and host lifecycle integration;
   241	it has no browser Effect runtime. Browser routes restore the schema-encoded
   242	server-function transport and render canonical values.
   243	
   244	The Website candidate owns one server runner and a React Atom registry in the
   245	browser. Its typed route context contains named framework settings/catalogue and
   246	documentation page and search transports, never an Effect runtime or Context. The root restores encoded values and passes
   247	checked submission state through ordinary React context. The container owns
   248	commands; focused leaves render readonly values. Editing and form unmount
   249	interrupt active work. Private binding transport belongs to the server Layer;
   250	public browser transport belongs to the registry. The RPC protocol Layer keeps
   251	configuration, while each named native client receive loop has an operation scope.
   252	No calculation or catalogue read builds a Layer or runner. See the [Website owner](../../apps/web/README.md).
   253	The SDK owns one runtime per client, with caller disposal and bounded one-shot
   254	helpers; see the [SDK lifetime owner](api-and-sdk.md#typescript-sdk-facade).
   255	
   256	Use `@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain(...)` for Bun process entrypoints
   257	where the root Effect is the process lifecycle. Process entrypoints should
   258	compose config, platform layers and server layers, then let Effect
   259	interruption/scopes release resources.
   260	
   261	### Native API instance and request ownership
   262	
   263	The DEV-74 API candidate uses the native Alchemy Worker class and `.make`.
   264	`ApiWorkerApplication` constructs its router in the native instance scope and
   265	receives one calculator service for HTTP and RPC. It creates no ManagedRuntime.
   266	Each handler runs in the incoming native fibre and request scope; tests observe
   267	both request paths and the corresponding finalisers. The selected native
   268	workerd instance scope has no teardown hook, so no isolate-finaliser claim is
   269	made; request-coupled I/O belongs inside incoming dispatch.
   270	
   271	Origins stay deferred during native planning. A cached native Config effect
   272	decodes bound addresses on first incoming runtime use. HTTP/RPC handling builds no live Layer. The native MCP protocol host is
   273	built once on first runtime use in the existing instance scope, after addresses
   274	resolve; its registrations omit first-caller request capabilities. The native body stream has bounded accumulation, total read
   275	time and scoped cancellation. Safe logger/reporter context is built at instance
   276	initialisation and supplied to both native router construction and dispatch;
   277	T009 retains unqualified safe native trace exports. T003's local connection
   278	acceptance does not establish that later requirement.
   279	
   280	## Promise boundaries
   281	
   282	Fallible Promise and SDK calls enter Effect with an explicit inline rejection
   283	mapping:
   284	
   285	```ts
   286	Effect.tryPromise({
   287	  try: () => providerOperation(),
   288	  catch: () => new ProviderRequestError({ message: "Provider request failed" }),
   289	});
   290	```
   291	
   292	Do not use callback-form `Effect.tryPromise`, which exposes
   293	`Cause.UnknownError` instead of the owning boundary's closed tagged error. Keep
   294	the `try` and `catch` policy inline so the raw rejection cannot escape or be
   295	hidden in a generic options/helper value. Both properties must be direct inline
   296	arrow, function or object-method implementations; do not use shorthand,
   297	extracted callbacks, non-function values or spread policy. Use `Effect.promise`
   298	only when a Promise rejection is intentionally treated as a defect. The current
   299	portable lint scope enforces this contract in packages, the API app and
   300	repository tools and both website applications. The strict override covers all
   301	owned TypeScript and JavaScript extensions. Five unexecuted upstream lint-input
   302	fixtures have exact strict-only exclusions; their neighbouring files still
   303	receive the full policy. The [testing owner](testing-and-quality.md) records
   304	the coverage and actual-command rejection proof.
   305	
   306	## Callsite error handling
   307	
   308	One-off Effect error handling MUST stay at the callsite. Error transformations
   309	MUST live directly beside the operation whose failure is being transformed:
   310	
   311	```ts
   312	program.pipe(
   313	  Effect.mapError(
   314	    () => new BoundaryError({ message: "Boundary settings are invalid" })
   315	  )
   316	);
   317	```
   318	
   319	Do not extract one-off helpers such as `mapConfigError`, `toBoundaryError` or
   320	`createRuntimeLayer` only to wrap a single `Effect.mapError`, `Effect.catchTag`,
   321	`Effect.catchAll` or `Effect.catchAllDefect` call. Extraction is allowed only
   322	when the helper is reused across boundaries, owns a real policy, or materially
   323	reduces complex duplication.
   324	
   325	## Abstraction admission
   326	
   327	Effect abstractions follow the repository-wide
   328	[abstraction admission contract](../design-docs/abstraction-admission.md).
   329	Before adding a shared service, layer, runtime wrapper, codec helper or program
   330	fragment, record its owner, semantic policy, second consumer or real
   331	substitution point, simpler before/after call graph and focused tests.
   332	
   333	A live/test Layer pair is a real substitution point when both implement one
   334	host-neutral service contract and tests exercise the production policy through
   335	that contract. Splitting every operation into its own service, mapper or layer
   336	does not qualify. Keep one-use decoding, encoding, tagged-error mapping and
   337	runtime execution inline at their owning boundary, and keep a primary
   338	operation as one readable `pipe` or `Effect.gen` program.
   339	
   340	## Boundary-only decoding
   341	
   342	Decode a value only when it crosses an explicit trust or type-erasure boundary.
   343	After an owning `Schema` has produced its schema-derived type, internal code
   344	must pass that type inward without decoding it again. This is a contract rule;
   345	it is not permission to replace Schema with casts, manual guards or object
   346	readers.
   347	
   348	Executable decoding belongs at one of these boundaries:
   349	
   350	- external input from HTTP, configuration, environment, storage, files,
   351	  serialised server/client transport or another process
   352	- an exported API that intentionally accepts `unknown`
   353	- normalisation of representation-level data supplied by an external library
   354	- dynamic catalogue or descriptor selection, where heterogeneous storage has
   355	  erased the selected schema's concrete type
   356	- a focused boundary test that proves one of these behaviours
   357	
   358	Do not decode between internal services, as defensive validation of an already
   359	typed parameter, inside ordinary rule or calculator code, or merely to build a
   360	unit-test fixture. A repeated or internal decoder is implementation work, not a
   361	new boundary to allowlist.
   362	
   363	For dynamic catalogue and descriptor dispatch, a policy-owning generic
   364	constructor must close over both the selected schema and the continuation that
   365	accepts `InputSchema["Type"]` before heterogeneous storage erases that generic.
   366	Do not recover the concrete type with an unsafe cast or by passing the decoded
   367	value through an `unknown` callback. The selected calculator input decoder and
   368	SDK report decoder are examples of required type-erasure boundaries.
   369	
   370	Keep each boundary operation linear. Start with the canonical decoder, map its
   371	expected `Schema.SchemaError` inline where that boundary owns the public error
   372	context, then continue with the typed value in one readable `pipe` or
   373	`Effect.gen` program. Preserve unrelated typed errors; do not use broad
   374	`Effect.catchAll`, `Effect.orDie`, raw Promise control flow or nested runtime
   375	execution to bridge a decoder. An app entrypoint, route loader or plain SDK
   376	facade may execute a completed Effect only at its exact outer host. The plain
   377	SDK host has a caller-owned runtime for each client and a temporary scope for
   378	one-shot helpers; it has no package-global runtime. The
   379	[SDK lifetime owner](api-and-sdk.md#typescript-sdk-facade) explains closing,
   380	interruption, bounded outcomes and the separate Effect interface.
   381	
   382	Do not extract one-use fragments such as `decodePayload`, `mapDecodeError`,
   383	`runDecoder`, `withDecodedInput` or generic `decodeOrFail`. A shared helper is
   384	appropriate only when it owns real, repeated policy, such as the generic
   385	catalogue constructor that preserves schema-to-continuation coupling. Review
   386	helper reuse and ownership with the task's path-evidenced semantic audit rather
   387	than a brittle function-size rule or a fixed audit count.
   388	
   389	`taxkit/no-decoding-outside-boundaries` enforces decoder placement across the
   390	repository. Its exact file allowlist belongs only in `oxlint.config.ts`; this
   391	architecture page owns the categories and review contract, not a duplicate
   392	path list. Use the active decoder inventory and this contract during review.
   393	
   394	## Encoding and contract boundaries
   395	
   396	Encoding is the inverse trust operation. Execute an owning Schema encoder only
   397	where a canonical value leaves the system as HTTP or route transport, provider
   398	input, persisted representation or command output. Do not encode between
   399	services, as a defensive copy, or inside ordinary React composition.

    10	export const CalculatorOperationBudget = Duration.seconds(5);
    11	
    12	// The shared service budget covers completion and scoped cleanup. Every caller
    13	// suspends the service invocation so eager metadata construction is counted.
    14	const withinOperationBudget = Effect.fnUntraced(function* <A, E, R>(
    15	  operation: Effect.Effect<A, E, R>
    16	) {
    17	  const started = yield* Clock.monotonicTimeNanos;
    18	  const result = yield* operation.pipe(
    19	    Effect.scoped,
    20	    Effect.timeoutOrElse({
    21	      duration: CalculatorOperationBudget,
    22	      orElse: () => Effect.fail(new CalculatorOperationTimedOut()),
    23	    })
    24	  );
    25	  const finished = yield* Clock.monotonicTimeNanos;
    26	  // Timers cannot pre-empt synchronous JavaScript. Reject a late result
    27	  // once control returns, without claiming that CPU work was stopped.
    28	  return yield* Duration.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(
    29	    Duration.nanos(finished - started),
    30	    CalculatorOperationBudget
    31	  )
    32	    ? Effect.fail(new CalculatorOperationTimedOut())
    33	    : Effect.succeed(result);
    34	});

     9	export const CalculatorConcurrencyLimit = 8;
    10	export const CalculatorOperationBudget = Duration.seconds(5);
    11	
    12	// The shared service budget covers completion and scoped cleanup. Every caller
    13	// suspends the service invocation so eager metadata construction is counted.
    14	const withinOperationBudget = Effect.fnUntraced(function* <A, E, R>(
    15	  operation: Effect.Effect<A, E, R>
    16	) {
    17	  const started = yield* Clock.monotonicTimeNanos;
    18	  const result = yield* operation.pipe(
    19	    Effect.scoped,
    20	    Effect.timeoutOrElse({
    21	      duration: CalculatorOperationBudget,
    22	      orElse: () => Effect.fail(new CalculatorOperationTimedOut()),
    23	    })
    24	  );
    25	  const finished = yield* Clock.monotonicTimeNanos;
    26	  // Timers cannot pre-empt synchronous JavaScript. Reject a late result
    27	  // once control returns, without claiming that CPU work was stopped.
    28	  return yield* Duration.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(
    29	    Duration.nanos(finished - started),
    30	    CalculatorOperationBudget
    31	  )
    32	    ? Effect.fail(new CalculatorOperationTimedOut())
    33	    : Effect.succeed(result);
    34	});
    35	
    36	// The host builds this Layer once over its calculation implementation. Every
    37	// transport shares this pool; each calculation in a batch takes its own place.

    40	  Effect.gen(function* () {
    41	    const calculator = yield* PublicCalculatorService;
    42	    const places = yield* Semaphore.make(CalculatorConcurrencyLimit);

1	import "@tanstack/react-start/server-only";
     2	import { CalculatorHostMode } from "@taxkit/api-rpc/rate-identity";
     3	import type { TaxKitApiBinding } from "api/worker";
     4	import { Config, Effect, Predicate, Schema } from "effect";
     5	
     6	import { TaxKitWebConfigError } from "./config";
     7	import { WebsitePublicSettings } from "./schemas";
     8	
     9	// This is the native SDK capability boundary. Preserve the original Fetcher
    10	// object (and method receiver); a Struct would copy its methods off the binding.
    11	const PrivateApiBinding: Schema.Codec<TaxKitApiBinding> =
    12	  Schema.declare<TaxKitApiBinding>(
    13	    (value): value is TaxKitApiBinding =>
    14	      Predicate.isObject(value) &&
    15	      Predicate.hasProperty(value, "fetch") &&
    16	      Predicate.isFunction(value.fetch) &&
    17	      Predicate.hasProperty(value, "connect") &&
    18	      Predicate.isFunction(value.connect) &&
    19	      Predicate.hasProperty(value, "calculatorRequest") &&
    20	      Predicate.isFunction(value.calculatorRequest)
    21	  );
    22	export const TaxKitWebServerConfig = (
    23	  rawBinding: unknown
    24	): Effect.Effect<
    25	  typeof WebsitePublicSettings.Type & {
    26	    readonly binding: typeof PrivateApiBinding.Type;
    27	    readonly hostMode: CalculatorHostMode;
    28	  },
    29	  TaxKitWebConfigError
    30	> =>
    31	  Effect.all({
    32	    apiOrigin: Config.schema(
    33	      WebsitePublicSettings.fields.apiOrigin,
    34	      "API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN"
    35	    ),
    36	    binding: Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(PrivateApiBinding)(rawBinding),
    37	    hostMode: Config.schema(CalculatorHostMode, "CALCULATOR_HOST_MODE").pipe(
    38	      Config.withDefault("edge")
    39	    ),
    40	    websiteOrigin: Config.schema(
    41	      WebsitePublicSettings.fields.websiteOrigin,
    42	      "WEBSITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN"
    43	    ),
    44	  }).pipe(
    45	    Effect.mapError(
    46	      () =>
    47	        new TaxKitWebConfigError({
    48	          message: "TaxKit web settings are missing or invalid.",
    49	          operation: "settings",
    50	          runtime: "server",
    51	        })
    52	    )
    53	  );

107	Owned Layers are static values, including test Layers. Put dependencies in the
   108	Layer's Requirements type channel rather than function arguments. Supply them
   109	with `Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(Dependency, checkedValue))`; tests can replace
   110	an implementation with native `Layer.mock` or another static Layer. Declaring a
   111	Layer does not acquire resources; building it in a Scope does.
   112	
   113	Native inline callbacks in `Layer.unwrap`, `Layer.suspend`, Effect operations
   114	and Atom runtime composition remain valid. Functions returning Effects or
   115	scoped fixture bundles remain valid too. The portable `strict-effect/static-layers`
   116	rule rejects recognised constructors, aliases, pipes, native router builders
   117	and Layer return types. It checks syntax, so opaque imported helper results
   118	still need clear owning types and review. There are no factory exceptions.
   119	
   120	Construct implementations in `live.layer.ts`:
   121	
   122	1. acquire dependencies;
   123	2. derive private helpers;
   124	3. define named operations with exact contract types;
   125	4. add spans/log annotations at semantic operations;
   126	5. return the service implementation;
   127	6. expose a Layer.
   128	
   129	Avoid side effects during module import.
   130	
   131	Choose the smallest construction that matches the work:
   132	
   133	| Construction                                            | Use it when                                                                                                          |
   134	| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   135	| `Layer.succeed(Service, Service.of(implementation))`    | The implementation is already available and construction performs no effects.                                        |
   136	| `Layer.effect(Service, effect)`                         | Construction acquires other services, reads Config, or creates Effect-managed state, a cache or a concurrency limit. |
   137	| `Layer.effect(Service, effect)` with scoped acquisition | A resource needs release when the Layer's scope closes.                                                              |

   139	For the qualified Effect v4 RC API, use the two-argument `Layer.effect`. Check
   140	installed types before copying this into a different version. `Service.of`
   141	checks the implementation against the service contract; it does not run it.

68	## Shared client contract
    69	
    70	Keep native generated clients private to semantic client Layers. HTTP and RPC
    71	clients implement the same domain service contract as the backend. Decode
    72	expected backend failures with the shared Schema and map connection or invalid
    73	reply failures to distinct named domain-access errors. No protocol error or
    74	unchecked provider payload leaks into UI policy.
    75	
    76	Test syntactically valid replies with the wrong payload Schema, as well as
    77	broken JSON. In the qualified 4.0.2, native RPC reply decoding can produce a
    78	SchemaError defect. The private client marks failure inside only the native
    79	exit reply codec's decoder, before native RPC converts that failure to a
    80	defect. Its semantic operation translates only that private marker to the named
    81	invalid-response error. Keep the native Schemas, Ndjson parser, Protocol and
    82	client; do not replace them with a handwritten protocol.
    83	
    84	Never infer reply failure from the SchemaError class alone. An unrelated
    85	transport or request encoder can fail with that same class and must keep its
    86	original defect identity. Test both reads with bad native replies and an
    87	unrelated adapter SchemaError. Preserve caller interruption and other defects;
    88	do not turn every Cause into an expected failure. Requalify the cached native
    89	exit Schema identity and reply decoder behaviour on Effect upgrades before
    90	retaining or removing this compatibility handling.
    91	
    92	For public, unauthenticated browser reads, omit credentials and reject redirects
    93	so a checked API address cannot silently send the browser somewhere else.
    94	Supply native Fetch RequestInit policy when the operation executes, not only
    95	while constructing its Layer. Protected clients need their own explicit policy.
    96	
    97	A selecting field can identify a response union. Native generation alone does
    98	not give a dependent return type: check the selected response Schema before
    99	narrowing literal/default inputs. See the [format-selected example](../examples/format-selected-client.md).

   101	For browser clients, test CORS preflight with the actual native request headers.
   102	In the qualified Effect version this includes b3 and traceparent. A successful
   103	server request is not browser-access proof. Remote MCP and Website WebMCP have
   104	separate Origin policies; do not inherit one policy from the other.

    87	      Jurisdiction,
    88	      TaxYear,
    89	      InputSchema,
    90	      OutputSchema
    91	    >,
    92	    input: InputSchema["Type"]
    93	  ): Effect.Effect<TaxKitSafeResult<OutputSchema["Type"]>> =>
    94	    Effect.interruptible(
    95	      runtime.contextEffect.pipe(
    96	        Effect.flatMap((context) =>

   107	            Ref.getUnsafe(disposed)

   110	          onSuccess: (value) => new TaxKitSuccess({ value }),
   111	        })
   112	      )
   113	    );
